name: sa_0001
text:
The drawing shows N-fluorobenzenesulfonimide (NFSI). A central nitrogen carries one fluorine and is bonded to two sulfur atoms. Each sulfur has two double-bonded oxygens (a sulfonyl group) and one phenyl group, labelled "Ph" in the image, which I expanded to c1ccccc1.

SMILES: O=S(=O)(c1ccccc1)N(F)S(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0003
text:
The drawing shows MeO2C–C≡C–CO2Me, which is dimethyl acetylenedicarboxylate.

- Each end is a methyl ester, MeO2C, written as C(=O)OC.
- The center is a carbon–carbon triple bond joining the two ester carbons.

The SMILES is COC(=O)C#CC(=O)OC. It is valid and matches the drawing atom for atom, and no stereochemistry is shown.

SMILES: COC(=O)C#CC(=O)OC

name: sa_0002
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with four substituents:

- A dipropylamino group, N(nPr)2, on the ring carbon at the right.
- A nitro group on each of the two ring carbons next to it (top and bottom).
- A CF3 group on the ring carbon opposite the amine (left).

This is trifluralin, which is N,N-dipropyl-2,6-dinitro-4-(trifluoromethyl)aniline. Each nPr is written as CCC.

SMILES: CCCN(CCC)c1c([N+](=O)[O-])cc(C(F)(F)F)cc1[N+](=O)[O-]

name: sa_0005
text:
The drawing shows diethyl azodicarboxylate (DEAD): an N=N double bond with an EtO2C group on each nitrogen.

Stereochemistry: the drawing shows the N=N bond in a zigzag layout, with the left carbon above the N–N axis and the right carbon below it, which looks trans (E). The bond lines are plain, with no explicit wedges or hashes, but the geometry is drawn as trans, so I include the E double-bond stereo.

Checking the geometry: the left N is at upper left, with its substituent C further to the lower left. The right N is at lower right, with its substituent C to the upper right. The N=N bond runs from upper left to lower right. Relative to that bond, the left substituent sits on the lower-left side and the right substituent on the upper-right side, so they are on opposite sides, which is trans.

SMILES for the E isomer: CCOC(=O)/N=N/C(=O)OCC

SMILES: CCOC(=O)/N=N/C(=O)OCC

name: sa_0004
text:
The drawing shows Boc-protected tyrosine with a benzyl ether on the phenol oxygen (Boc-Tyr(Bn)-OH).

- **Backbone:** the alpha carbon carries an NH–Boc group, a CO2H group and a CH2 group leading to a para-substituted benzene ring. The ring carries OBn (O–CH2–C6H5) opposite the CH2.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CO2H bond is drawn as a wedge, so it points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away. Viewed from the front, N (up) → CO2H (lower left) → CH2 (lower right) runs counterclockwise. With H at the back, that gives S, the L-amino-acid configuration.
- **SMILES form:** the fragment N[C@@H](CR)C(=O)O encodes L-tyrosine, so I used the same pattern here.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(OCc2ccccc2)cc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0007
text:
This is osimertinib mesylate: the osimertinib free base drawn together with methanesulfonic acid as a separate component.

**Osimertinib part**
- Central benzene ring: a C(=O)C=C acrylamide on NH, a N(C)CCN(C)C group, an OMe, and an NH linking to the pyrimidine.
- Pyrimidine: its 4-position carries the 1-methylindol-3-yl group, and its 2-position carries the NH.
- Substituent order around the benzene ring, starting from the NH-acrylamide carbon: C1 bears NHC(=O)C=C, C2 bears N(C)CCN(C)C (at the top), C3 is CH, C4 bears OMe, C5 bears the NH to the pyrimidine, and C6 is CH.

**SMILES for the free base**
C=CC(=O)Nc1cc(Nc2nccc(n2)-c2cn(C)c3ccccc23)c(OC)cc1N(C)CCN(C)C

**Mesylate**
The acid is written as CS(=O)(=O)O, joined to the base with a dot.

SMILES: C=CC(=O)Nc1cc(Nc2nccc(n2)-c2cn(C)c3ccccc23)c(OC)cc1N(C)CCN(C)C.CS(=O)(=O)O

name: sa_0010
text:
This is Danishefsky's diene: 1-methoxy-3-trimethylsilyloxy-1,3-butadiene.

Reading the drawing, atoms run left to right:
- MeO at the left, bonded to C1 at about (512, 715).
- C1=C2, where C2 is at about (718, 880).
- C2–C3, where C3 is at about (965, 780).
- C3=CH2, with the CH2 at the top (about (980, 520)).
- C3–OTMS, with the OTMS at the lower right.

**Stereochemistry:** The C1=C2 double bond has OMe on C1 and the C3 chain on C2. The OMe goes from C1 down-left to O at (310, 795), and the C3 chain goes from C2 up-right. The two substituents point to opposite sides of the double bond, so the geometry is trans (E).

In SMILES, written as CO/C=C/C(=C)O[Si](C)(C)C, the "/" marks place the OMe and the C3 chain on opposite sides, which is E.

SMILES: CO/C=C/C(=C)O[Si](C)(C)C

name: sa_0006
text:
The drawing shows Fmoc-protected O-tert-butyl-tyrosine (Fmoc-Tyr(tBu)-OH).

- **Side chain:** a para-substituted benzene ring carries an O–tBu ether on one side and a CH2 on the other.
- **Alpha carbon:** the CH2 links to the stereocentre, which bears NH–Fmoc, a CO2H group drawn on a wedge, and an implicit H.
- **Fmoc group:** I expanded it as NH–C(=O)–O–CH2–fluorenyl.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CO2H wedge points toward the viewer, so H points away. Viewed with H at the back, N → CO2H → CH2 runs counterclockwise. The priorities are N > CO2H > CH2, so the centre is S, which is the L-configuration.
- **SMILES chirality tag:** with the atoms written in the order CH2, H, N, CO2H, the S centre takes the tag `@`.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)Oc1ccc(C[C@H](NC(=O)OCC2c3ccccc3-c3ccccc23)C(=O)O)cc1

name: sa_0008
text:
The drawing is oleic acid, (Z)-octadec-9-enoic acid.

- **Head group:** HO2C on the left is the carboxylic acid carbon, C1.
- **Chain:** counting the zigzag vertices gives C2 to C9 along the chain, then C10 at the right end carrying the nOct label.
- **Double bond:** it sits between C9 and C10.
- **Tail:** nOct is an n-octyl group (8 carbons), so the total is 10 + 8 = 18 carbons.
- **Geometry:** at the double bond, the chain carbon C8 (on C9) and the nOct substituent (on C10) both point upward, on the same side. This is cis (Z).

Check of the SMILES: C(=O) followed by 7 CH2 gives C1 to C8. Then `/C=C\` is C9=C10 with cis geometry, and 8 more carbons complete the octyl tail.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCCCCCC/C=C\CCCCCCCC

name: sa_0011
text:
This structure is febuxostat: a thiazole ring carrying a methyl and a carboxylic acid, joined to a benzene ring that bears an isobutoxy group and a nitrile.

**Thiazole ring:**
- The methyl-bearing carbon is bonded to N, and the ring carbon with the CO2H group is bonded to S.
- N is double-bonded to C2, and C2 is bonded to S and to the benzene ring.
- The C4=C5 double bond lies between the methyl-bearing carbon and the CO2H-bearing carbon.

**Benzene ring:**
- Position 1 is attached to the thiazole C2.
- Moving around the ring, the carbon bearing O-iBu sits para to position 1, and the carbon bearing CN sits next to it (position 3 relative to the thiazole attachment).

**Isobutyl group:** the label "iBu" is expanded to CH2CH(CH3)2.

**SMILES:** Cc1nc(sc1C(=O)O)-c1ccc(OCC(C)C)c(C#N)c1

SMILES: Cc1nc(-c2ccc(OCC(C)C)c(C#N)c2)sc1C(=O)O

name: sa_0009
text:
The drawing shows O-benzyl serine carrying a Boc-protected amine: BnO–CH2–CH(NHBoc)–CO2H.

**Connectivity:**
- The left end is a benzyl ether (BnO), attached to a CH2 group.
- That CH2 is bonded to the central stereocentre.
- The stereocentre carries the NH–Boc group (to the right) and the CO2H group (lower left).

**Stereochemistry:** The CO2H bond is hashed, so it points away from the viewer, and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2OBn > H.
- Viewed from the front, N (right) → CO2H (lower left) → CH2 (upper left) runs clockwise.
- The H faces the viewer, so the true sense is reversed, giving S.
- This is the Boc-O-benzyl-L-serine configuration.

The SMILES below follows the same neighbour order as L-serine, N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)O, which is S.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N[C@@H](COCc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0012
text:
The drawing is a thiohydantoin core with two aryl substituents, similar to enzalutamide but with an extra fluorine on the left ring.

**Core ring:** The five-membered ring contains N (left), C=O, a quaternary carbon bearing two methyls, N (right), and C=S between the two nitrogens.

**Left aryl ring (on the left N):**
- The ring carbon attached to N has two neighbours.
- One neighbour is C–F (the upper one).
- Next to that carbon is C–CF3, then C–CN, then two CH carbons back to the N-bearing carbon.
- SMILES for this ring: c1(N)c(F)c(C(F)(F)F)c(C#N)cc1.

**Right aryl ring (on the right N):**
- The ring carbon attached to N is at the left of the ring.
- Going around, the next carbon is CH (top), then CH, then the carbon bearing C(=O)NHMe.
- After that comes C–F, then CH back to the N-bearing carbon.
- SMILES for this ring: c1ccc(C(=O)NC)c(F)c1.

**Assembled SMILES:**
CNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1F)N1C(=S)N(C(=O)C1(C)C)c1ccc(C#N)c(C(F)(F)F)c1F

I checked the left ring: c1ccc(C#N)c(C(F)(F)F)c1F starts at the N-attached carbon, then CH, CH, C–CN, C–CF3, C–F, closing back to the start. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1F)N1C(=S)N(C(=O)C1(C)C)c1ccc(C#N)c(C(F)(F)F)c1F

name: sa_0016
text:
I read the drawing as N-Cbz-phenylalanine: a Cbz group on the nitrogen, an NH joined to the α-carbon, a CO2H group on that carbon, and a CH2 leading to a phenyl ring.

**Stereochemistry.** The only stereocentre is the α-carbon, and the wedge to CO2H shows it points toward the viewer. That leaves the implicit hydrogen pointing away from the viewer.

The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2Ph. On the page, N is at the upper left, CO2H at the lower left and CH2 on the right. Going N → CO2H → CH2 runs counterclockwise. With the hydrogen at the back, this is the S configuration, which is the L-amino-acid (Cbz-L-phenylalanine) arrangement.

I wrote the SMILES with the Cbz carbamate first, then the stereocentre. The `@@` tag matches the standard L-Phe pattern `N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O`.

SMILES: O=C(OCc1ccccc1)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0014
text:
The drawing is N‑Cbz‑proline: a pyrrolidine ring with the nitrogen carrying a Cbz group and the C2 carbon carrying a CO2H group.

- **Ring:** five vertices, namely N, the stereocentre C2, and three CH2 carbons.
- **N substituent:** Cbz is benzyloxycarbonyl, so N–C(=O)OCH2–C6H5.
- **C2 substituent:** CO2H on a hashed wedge, so it points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- **Configuration:** the priorities are N > CO2H > ring C3 > H. Viewed from the front, N (down) → CO2H (upper left) → C3 (upper right) runs clockwise. Because the H points toward the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. This is the L‑proline configuration.

I checked the chirality tag by comparison with L‑proline, OC(=O)[C@@H]1CCCN1. Writing the atoms in the order C3, H, N, COOH swaps COOH and C3, which flips the tag to @.

SMILES: O=C(OCc1ccccc1)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)O

name: sa_0015
text:
I read the drawing as Boc-Lys(Cbz)-OH, i.e. lysine with both amines protected.

- **Chain:** from the Cbz-NH nitrogen there are four CH₂ carbons, then the stereocentre CH.
- **Substituents on the stereocentre:** an NH-Boc group, a CO₂H group, and the chain. The CO₂H is drawn on a hashed bond.
- **Abbreviations expanded:** Cbz is C(=O)OCH₂Ph and Boc is C(=O)OC(CH₃)₃.
- **Stereochemistry:** the priorities are N > CO₂H > CH₂ chain > H. The hashed CO₂H points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Reading N → CO₂H → chain on the page gives clockwise, which reverses to counterclockwise once the H is accounted for. That is S, the L-lysine configuration.
- **SMILES chirality tag:** written with the neighbour order CO₂H, H, chain, N, the S centre takes `@`, giving `[C@H]`.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@H](CCCCNC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C

name: sa_0018
text:
The drawing shows Boc-protected leucine.

- The central carbon carries CO2H (up), NH–Boc (lower left) and an isobutyl group (lower right, hashed bond), plus an implicit H.
- Boc expands to C(=O)OC(C)(C)C, and iBu is CH2CH(CH3)2.
- For the stereochemistry, the hashed isobutyl puts the implicit H toward the viewer. The priorities are N > CO2H > iBu > H. Reading N → CO2H → iBu in the drawing is clockwise, and reversing for the H pointing toward the viewer gives counterclockwise, so the centre is S. This is the L-leucine configuration.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@H](NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C(=O)O

name: sa_0013
text:
I read the drawing as a pyranose ring with an acetylated CH2OH side chain, three acetate esters on the ring and a bromine on the anomeric carbon (an acetobromo sugar).

**Ring and substituents**
- The ring has five carbons and one oxygen, with the ring oxygen at the bottom.
- The ring carbon at the lower right carries Br on a wedge.
- Going around the ring from that carbon, the next three carbons carry OAc groups: wedge, hash, wedge.
- The last ring carbon, next to the ring oxygen, carries a hashed CH2–OAc group.
- Each Ac is expanded to an acetyl group, C(C)=O, attached through the oxygen.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned @/@@ at each of the five stereocentres from the wedge/hash bonds and the in-plane neighbour positions, with the implicit hydrogen taken as pointing opposite to the wedged or hashed substituent.

The SMILES below is written from the CH2OAc carbon around the ring and closed back at the OAc carbon next to it. I checked that it contains the 5 ring carbons, the ring oxygen, Br, the CH2OAc group and the three ring OAc groups.

SMILES: CC(=O)OC[C@H]1O[C@H](Br)[C@H](OC(C)=O)[C@@H](OC(C)=O)[C@@H]1OC(C)=O

name: sa_0020
text:
The drawing shows a TMS group (trimethylsilyl) joined to one end of a carbon–carbon triple bond. The other end of the triple bond carries CO2Me (a methyl ester).

Expanding the abbreviations gives Si(CH3)3–C≡C–C(=O)OCH3, which is methyl 3-(trimethylsilyl)propiolate.

SMILES: C[Si](C)(C)C#CC(=O)OC

name: sa_0019
text:
The drawing is N-Cbz-aspartic acid with the side-chain carboxyl as a benzyl ester (Cbz-Asp(OBn)-OH), with the α-carboxylic acid left free.

- **Left:** Cbz is a benzyloxycarbonyl group, PhCH2-O-C(=O)-, attached to the NH.
- **Stereocentre:** it carries NH, a CH2, a wedged CO2H, and an implicit H.
- **Right chain:** the CH2 leads to CO2Bn, which is C(=O)OCH2Ph.
- **Configuration:** the CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2 > H. The wedged CO2H points toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. Going N → CO2H → CH2 on the page runs counterclockwise, which gives S, the L-aspartic acid configuration.
- **SMILES check:** L-Asp is written N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)O, and the same atom order with the Cbz and benzyl groups added keeps the @@ marker.

SMILES: O=C(OCc1ccccc1)N[C@@H](CC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0021
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with two substituents at opposite (para) positions. Each substituent is labeled CO2Me, one written MeO2C on the left and one CO2Me on the right. Each is a methyl ester group, C(=O)OC, so the molecule is dimethyl terephthalate.

SMILES: COC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)OC

name: sa_0022
text:
The central carbon carries an OH group and three substituents: two CH2CO2Et arms and one CO2Et group. This is triethyl citrate without the acetyl group.

The drawing gives these connections:
- Central carbon to CH2, then to C(=O)OEt (upper left).
- Central carbon to CH2, then to CO2Et (right).
- Central carbon directly to CO2Et (lower left).
- Central carbon to OH.

The central carbon has two identical CH2CO2Et arms, so it is not a stereocentre and needs no stereo marks.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)CC(O)(CC(=O)OCC)C(=O)OCC

name: sa_0023
text:
The drawing shows HO3S joined to a zigzag chain of three carbons, ending in NHAc.

- The bond from S goes to the first carbon (a vertex at the lower left), then to the second carbon (a peak), then to the third carbon (a vertex at the lower right), which bonds to N.
- This gives S–C–C–C–N, so the chain is a propyl linker.
- HO3S is a sulfonic acid group, S(=O)(=O)O.
- NHAc is an acetamide, NC(C)=O.

The molecule is 3-acetamidopropane-1-sulfonic acid (acamprosate).

SMILES: CC(=O)NCCCS(=O)(=O)O

name: sa_0025
text:
The drawing shows a central silicon atom with four substituents: tBu (tert-butyl), two Ph (phenyl) groups, and Cl. This is tert-butyldiphenylchlorosilane.

Expanding the abbreviations gives tert-butyl as C(C)(C)C and each phenyl as c1ccccc1. The bonds are all plain, so there is no stereochemistry to include.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)[Si](Cl)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0027
text:
The drawing shows bis(4-nitrophenyl) carbonate. A central carbonyl carbon (C=O) is bonded to two ester-type oxygens. Each of those oxygens is attached to a benzene ring that carries a nitro group para to the oxygen.

Checking the para relationship on the left ring: the O-bearing carbon is at (595, 717) and the nitro-bearing carbon is at (307, 649). The ring runs (407, 540), (553, 575), (595, 717), (492, 825), (347, 791), (307, 649). The O-bearing carbon is therefore the third vertex and the nitro carbon is the sixth, so they are para. The right ring has the same arrangement.

SMILES: O=C(Oc1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])cc1)Oc1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])cc1

name: sa_0028
text:
The drawing is a 1,4-dihydropyridine ring with these substituents:

- N1 is NH.
- C2 (upper right) carries CN and is double-bonded to C3.
- C3 carries CO2Me.
- C4 is sp3 and carries the 3-nitrophenyl group.
- C5 carries CO2iPr and is double-bonded to C6.
- C6 carries the methyl group.

The nitro group sits on the carbon adjacent to the ring carbon next to the attachment point, so it is meta. The attachment carbon is at (714,752), the ring carbon above it is at (548,630), and the nitro-bearing carbon is at (359,713). That puts the nitro group meta to the attachment point.

The C4 stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES, written as a chain from the ring:
N#CC1=C(C(=O)OC)C(c2cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c2)C(C(=O)OC(C)C)=C(C)N1

SMILES: N#CC1=C(C(=O)OC)C(c2cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c2)C(C(=O)OC(C)C)=C(C)N1

name: sa_0026
text:
The drawing is Fmoc-protected aspartic acid with a tert-butyl ester on the side chain (Fmoc-Asp(OtBu)-OH).

- **Backbone:** the stereocentre carries an NH, a CH2 and a CO2H. The NH is capped with Fmoc and the CH2 leads to CO2tBu.
- **Fmoc group:** I expanded it to the fluorenylmethyl carbamate, `NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12`.
- **Side-chain ester:** CO2tBu expands to `CC(=O)OC(C)(C)C`.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only wedge is the bold bond to HO2C, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2 > H. Going N → CO2H → CH2 runs counterclockwise as seen from the front, which gives S, the L-aspartic acid configuration.
- **SMILES chirality tag:** written starting from the CO2H carbon, the neighbour order is CO2H, H, CH2, N. That order needs `@` for S.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@H](CC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12

name: sa_0017
text:
The structure is orlistat. I built the SMILES by reading each group in turn and then assigning each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes.

**Groups read from the drawing**
- Leucine part: an N-formyl amine (OHC–NH) on an α-carbon that carries an isobutyl group and an ester C=O.
- Ester oxygen: it links to a CH that carries an n-decyl–CH2 chain (11 carbons in total) and a CH2 leading to the ring.
- Ring: a four-membered β-lactone (oxetan-2-one) with ring O, C=O, a hexyl-bearing carbon and a CH2-bearing carbon.

**Stereocentres**
CIP analysis of the wedges and hashes gives S at the leucine α-carbon, S at the ester carbon, S at the ring carbon bearing the CH2, and S at the ring carbon bearing the hexyl group. This matches orlistat's known configuration. I then converted each centre to @/@@ for this atom ordering.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCC[C@@H](C[C@H]1[C@@H](C(=O)O1)CCCCCC)OC(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)NC=O

name: sa_0030
text:
This is the enol form of teriflunomide (the active metabolite of leflunomide).

Reading the structure region by region:
- A methyl group is attached to a carbon that bears an OH and is double-bonded to the next carbon.
- That next carbon carries a nitrile (C≡N) and is bonded to a C(=O)NH amide carbon.
- The amide nitrogen is bonded to a benzene ring that has a CF3 group para to the nitrogen.

The drawing shows no explicit cis/trans geometry about the C=C, so I have not included double-bond stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC(O)=C(C#N)C(=O)Nc1ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc1

name: sa_0032
text:
This structure is dronedarone hydrochloride.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- The left part is a benzofuran. The furan oxygen is at the lower left, C2 carries an n-butyl group, and C3 carries the ketone.
- On the benzo ring, the NH–SO2Me (methanesulfonamide) group sits at C5, para to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to the furan oxygen. In dronedarone the sulfonamide is at the 5-position, which matches.
- The ketone links C3 to a para-disubstituted benzene ring.
- The para position of that ring carries an O–CH2CH2CH2–N(nBu)2 chain, with three carbons between O and N.
- HCl is written as a separate component.

SMILES for the free base, built from this reading:
CCCCc1oc2ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc2c1C(=O)c1ccc(OCCCN(CCCC)CCCC)cc1

Adding HCl as a separate component gives the final string.

SMILES: CCCCc1oc2ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc2c1C(=O)c1ccc(OCCCN(CCCC)CCCC)cc1.Cl

name: sa_0029
text:
I read the molecule as a 2-methyl-6-nitro-2,3-dihydroimidazo[2,1-b]oxazole (a delamanid-type scaffold) with the following parts:

- **Bicyclic core:** a nitro-substituted imidazole fused to a dihydro-oxazole. The quaternary carbon carries a methyl group and a CH2–O linker.
- **Linker and aryl groups:** the CH2–O leads to a para-disubstituted phenyl ring, whose other position bears the nitrogen of a piperidine.
- **Piperidine:** the 4-position carries an O-aryl group, a para-(trifluoromethoxy)phenyl ring.

**Stereochemistry:** the methyl on the quaternary carbon is drawn with a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer. The other three substituents are the ring oxygen (left), the CH2O (right) and the ring CH2N (down). In the front view they run clockwise (left → right → down), so viewed from the methyl side they run counterclockwise. In the SMILES neighbour order (methyl, ring-closure O, CH2O, CH2N), that corresponds to `@`.

SMILES: C[C@]1(COc2ccc(cc2)N2CCC(CC2)Oc2ccc(OC(F)(F)F)cc2)Cn2cc([N+](=O)[O-])nc2O1

name: sa_0031
text:
The drawing is Fmoc-protected phenylalanine, with the stereocentre drawn as the L (S) configuration.

- **Left:** an Fmoc group (fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl) is bonded to an NH, giving the carbamate Fmoc–NH.
- **Stereocentre:** the NH attaches to the central carbon. This carbon also carries a CH2 to the right that ends in Ph (a phenyl ring), and a CO2H on a wedge pointing down-left. The remaining substituent is an implicit H.
- **Configuration:** the wedged CO2H points toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. With priorities N > CO2H > CH2Ph > H, the sequence N (upper left), CO2H (lower left), CH2 (right) runs counterclockwise. Viewed with H at the back, that is S, which is L-phenylalanine.
- **SMILES form:** the chirality tag follows the standard L-Phe pattern N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O, and the Fmoc group is written as O=C(OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12) on the nitrogen.

SMILES: O=C(OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0034
text:
The drawing shows a central CH2 carbon (the bend in the zigzag) with a "CN" label on one side and "Ts" on the other.

- Ts is tosyl, p-toluenesulfonyl: S(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1.
- The "CN" label is attached to the CH2 through its left-hand carbon, so I read it as a nitrile, C#N. The alternative reading, an isocyanide attached through nitrogen, would be drawn as "NC". The nitrile reading matches tosylacetonitrile, which is a common reagent.

The CH2 therefore carries the nitrile carbon and the sulfonyl group, giving N#CCS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1.

SMILES: N#CCS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1

name: sa_0036
text:

name: sa_0033
text:
I read the drawing as N‑tosyl L‑arginine methyl ester.

- **Backbone:** the chain runs from the tosyl‑bearing NH, through the alpha carbon, then three CH2 groups, to the guanidine nitrogen.
- **Guanidine:** the last nitrogen is drawn with a C=N double bond to a carbon carrying two NH2 groups, giving N=C(N)N.
- **Ester:** the alpha carbon bears CO2Me, which expands to C(=O)OC.
- **Tosyl:** Ts on the nitrogen expands to S(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CO2Me bond is hashed, so it points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
  - CIP priorities are N > CO2Me > CH2 > H.
  - In the drawing, N (lower left) → CO2Me (up) → CH2 (lower right) runs clockwise with H toward the viewer.
  - Viewing with H toward the viewer reverses the sense, so the centre is S, the natural L configuration.
  - In the SMILES below, `[C@@H]` written after the carbonyl carbon encodes S.

name: sa_0035
text:
The drawing shows Boc-protected tryptophan: a Boc-NH group on the α-carbon, a CO2H group, and a CH2 linking to the 3-position of an indole ring (with its N–H).

**Stereochemistry:** the α-carbon has a hashed bond to the CO2H carbon, so the implicit hydrogen points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2 > H. On the page, N (below), CO2H (upper left) and CH2 (right) run clockwise. Because the hydrogen faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, which gives counterclockwise, i.e. (S). This is the L-tryptophan configuration.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)O

name: sa_0037
text:
The drawing shows F3C on the left, then five CF2 carbons in a row, then "nOct" on the right.

- The left end is a CF3 group.
- Each of the five carbons in the chain carries two F atoms.
- "nOct" is n-octyl, which is CCCCCCCC (8 carbons).

Atom by atom: FC(F)(F) followed by five C(F)(F) units, then the octyl chain. That gives 1 + 5 = 6 fluorinated carbons plus 8 octyl carbons, which is 1-perfluorohexyl-octane (C6F13-C8H17).

SMILES: FC(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)CCCCCCCC

name: sa_0024
text:
I read this as benidipine: a 1,4-dihydropyridine with a methyl ester, an N-benzylpiperidin-3-yl ester and a 3-nitrophenyl group.

**Connectivity**
- The dihydropyridine ring has an NH, with methyl groups on both carbons next to it (C2 and C6).
- C3 carries the ester to the piperidine and C5 carries CO2Me.
- C4 carries the 3-nitrophenyl group (the NO2 sits meta to the attachment point).
- The ester oxygen is bonded to C3 of a piperidine ring. The ring nitrogen carries Bn (CH2Ph).

**Stereochemistry**
Only two centres are drawn with wedges.
- **Piperidine C3:** the wedge goes to the ester O. The CIP priorities are O > C2 (the carbon next to N) > C4 > H. With H pointing away, O → C2 → C4 runs clockwise, so this centre is R. In the SMILES below it is written as `[C@@H]`.
- **Dihydropyridine C4:** the wedge goes to the aryl group, with H pointing away. The priorities are C3 > C5 > aryl > H. C3 outranks C5 because its ester side carries the piperidinyl group, whereas the C5 ester side carries only a methyl. C3 → C5 → aryl runs clockwise, so this centre is R. In the SMILES below it is written as `[C@@H]`.

SMILES: COC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)O[C@@H]2CCCN(Cc3ccccc3)C2)[C@@H]1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: sa_0038
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three substituents:
- An ester group, C(=O)OCCNEt2, on the ring carbon at the right.
- An NH2 group on the ring carbon at the upper left.
- An O-nBu group on the ring carbon at the lower left, which is adjacent to the NH2 carbon.

Numbering from the ester carbon (position 1), the ring runs: C1 (ester), C2 (the CH at the bottom), C3 (O-nBu), C4 (NH2), C5 (CH at the top), C6 (CH at the upper right). The NH2 is therefore para to the ester and the butoxy is meta, so this is 4-amino-3-butoxybenzoate 2-(diethylamino)ethyl ester.

Expanding the abbreviations (nBu = CCCC, NEt2 = N(CC)CC), the SMILES is:

SMILES: CCCCOc1cc(C(=O)OCCN(CC)CC)ccc1N

name: sa_0039
text:
The drawing shows a central nitrogen bonded to one phenyl group (Ph) and two triflyl groups (Tf). This is N-phenylbis(trifluoromethanesulfonimide).

Expanding the abbreviations:
- Tf is a triflyl group, S(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F.
- Ph is a phenyl group, c1ccccc1.

Atom check: the nitrogen has three substituents (phenyl and two sulfonyl groups) and each triflyl has a CF3, so every atom in the drawing is accounted for. No stereochemistry is shown.

SMILES: FC(F)(F)S(=O)(=O)N(c1ccccc1)S(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F

name: sa_0042
text:
The drawing shows Cbz-Gly-Gly-OH, read from left to right as follows.

- HO2C is a carboxylic acid group, C(=O)O.
- It is attached to a CH2, then an NH, then a C=O (the amide carbonyl).
- The carbonyl carbon is attached to a second CH2, then an NH, then Cbz.
- Cbz is benzyloxycarbonyl, C(=O)OCc1ccccc1.

Assembling these pieces gives OC(=O)CNC(=O)CNC(=O)OCc1ccccc1. Every atom and bond in the drawing is accounted for, and no stereochemistry is shown.

SMILES: OC(=O)CNC(=O)CNC(=O)OCc1ccccc1

name: sa_0041
text:
This is nimodipine, a 1,4-dihydropyridine, drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is included.

Reading the structure region by region:

- **Dihydropyridine ring:** an NH bonded to two ring carbons, each carrying a methyl group. These carbons are double-bonded to the two ring carbons that carry the ester groups. The sp3 C4 sits between those two carbons and carries the aryl group.
- **Left ester:** C(=O)OCCOC, which is a 2-methoxyethyl ester (MeO–CH2CH2–O–C(=O)–).
- **Right ester:** C(=O)OC(C)C, an isopropyl ester.
- **Aryl group:** a benzene ring attached at C4 with NO2 at the meta position. Going around the ring from the attachment carbon, the next carbon is unsubstituted (the upper-left vertex at 868,537 is CH), and the NO2 carbon is separated from the attachment carbon by one CH (the lower-right vertex at 1116,606). That makes it 3-nitrophenyl.

SMILES: COCCOC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OC(C)C)C1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: sa_0043
text:
The image shows a benzene ring with two adjacent substituents: OTf (triflate) and TMS (trimethylsilyl). This is 2-(trimethylsilyl)phenyl trifluoromethanesulfonate.

- OTf expands to OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F.
- TMS expands to [Si](C)(C)C.

The ring has two ortho substituents, and the remaining four carbons carry hydrogens. Checking the SMILES against the drawing: the ring has six carbons, the first substituent is the triflate on one carbon, and the TMS group sits on the neighbouring carbon.

SMILES: C[Si](C)(C)c1ccccc1OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F

name: sa_0045
text:
The drawing shows a central phosphorus atom with four substituents:

- a double bond to O (P=O)
- a single bond to OH
- two single bonds to OBn groups

Bn (benzyl) expands to CH2-phenyl, so each OBn is OCc1ccccc1. The molecule is dibenzyl phosphate.

SMILES: O=P(O)(OCc1ccccc1)OCc1ccccc1

name: sa_0044
text:
The image shows dibutyltin dilaurate drawn with abbreviations: a central Sn bearing two n-butyl groups and two carboxylate O–C(=O)–CH2–nDec groups.

Each acyl chain is C(=O), then CH2, then nDec. The label nDec is n-decyl, which is 10 carbons. The chain therefore has 1 (C=O) + 1 (CH2) + 10 = 12 carbons, which is the laurate (dodecanoate) chain.

Each n-decyl group is written as CCCCCCCCCC.

The acyl group is then O–C(=O)–C–CCCCCCCCCC, which is C(=O)CCCCCCCCCCC, i.e. 1 carbonyl carbon plus 11 chain carbons.

The full SMILES is CCCC[Sn](CCCC)(OC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCC)OC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCC.

SMILES: CCCC[Sn](CCCC)(OC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCC)OC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCC

name: sa_0047
text:
The drawing shows a para-disubstituted benzene ring carrying two groups.

- One substituent is an amide: C(=O)NH–CH2CH2–NEt2, where "Et2N" is a diethylamino group.
- The other substituent is a methanesulfonamide: NH–S(=O)(=O)–CH3, where "SO2Me" is the sulfonyl-methyl group.

Written as SMILES, the diethylamino end is CCN(CC)CCNC(=O), joined to the ring c1ccc(cc1), which carries NS(C)(=O)=O.

The drawing shows no wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CCN(CC)CCNC(=O)c1ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc1

name: sa_0040
text:
I read this as pergolide: an ergoline skeleton with an N-propyl group on the ring nitrogen and a CH2–S–CH3 group on the other ring.

**Skeleton:**
- The indole NH sits at the left, fused to a benzene ring.
- A cyclohexane ring links the indole to a piperidine ring.
- The piperidine nitrogen carries the n-propyl group.
- The carbon at the lower right of the piperidine carries the CH2SMe substituent on a hashed bond.

**Stereocentres**, read from the wedges and hashes with the implicit hydrogens taken into account:
- The CH bearing CH2SMe (hashed bond) is `[C@H]` in the SMILES below.
- The ring-fusion carbon with the wedged H is `[C@@H]`.
- The carbon next to N with the hashed H is `[C@H]`.

I derived each @/@@ by working out the neighbour order around the centre and viewing it from the hydrogen side. I checked that the ring-closure digits match the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: CCCN1C[C@H](CSC)C[C@@H]2[C@H]1Cc1c[nH]c3cccc2c13

name: sa_0049
text:
The drawing shows an N-Cbz-protected valine.

- **Cbz:** the benzyloxycarbonyl group on nitrogen is PhCH2–O–C(=O)–, so the nitrogen carries NH–C(=O)OCH2Ph.
- **Core:** the stereocentre carries NH(Cbz), CO2H, iPr and an implicit H.
- **Stereochemistry:** the iPr bond is hashed, so iPr points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > iPr > H. On the page, N (lower left) → CO2H (top) → iPr (lower right) runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, which gives S, the L-valine configuration.

I wrote the SMILES in the same pattern as L-valine, `CC(C)[C@H](N)C(=O)O`, with the Cbz group added on nitrogen.

SMILES: CC(C)[C@H](NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0050
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with two substituents on opposite vertices (para). On the left is O2N, a nitro group. On the right is OAc, an acetoxy group, where Ac is acetyl (C(=O)CH3), so the group is an ester O–C(=O)CH3.

The molecule is 4-nitrophenyl acetate. Written with the nitro group as [N+](=O)[O-], the SMILES is CC(=O)Oc1ccc(cc1)[N+](=O)[O-].

name: sa_0048
text:
The drawing is 3',5'-bis-O-TBS-thymidine. I read it as follows:

- **Base:** a thymine ring, with the N1 carbon bonded to the sugar, a methyl on C5, and C2=O and C4=O flanking the N–H.
- **Sugar:** a 2'-deoxyribose ring with an ether O at the top and a CH2 at C2'.
- **Substituents:** C5' carries CH2–OTBS and C3' carries OTBS. TBS is expanded to Si(C)(C)C(C)(C)C.
- **Stereochemistry:**
  - C1' has a wedge to N (base up).
  - C4' has a wedge to CH2OTBS (up).
  - C3' has a hashed bond to OTBS (down).
  - This matches natural β-D-thymidine, so I took the thymidine chirality tags and checked each centre's neighbour order against the drawing.

name: sa_0051
text:
The drawing shows a TMS group (trimethylsilyl, Si(CH3)3) on the left and a CO2Et group (ethyl ester) on the right. The two are joined through a single CH2 carbon at the bottom vertex.

Expanding the abbreviations gives the molecule ethyl (trimethylsilyl)acetate: (CH3)3Si–CH2–C(=O)–O–CH2CH3.

There are no stereocentres, wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is needed.

name: sa_0054
text:
The drawing shows MeO2C–CH2–NH–Boc, which is Boc-glycine methyl ester.

- MeO2C is a methyl ester, written COC(=O).
- The CH2 links the ester carbon to the nitrogen.
- NH carries the Boc group, which is C(=O)OC(C)(C)C.

Assembled, this gives COC(=O)CNC(=O)OC(C)(C)C. The molecule has no stereocentres, so no stereo marks are needed.

SMILES: COC(=O)CNC(=O)OC(C)(C)C

name: sa_0046
text:
I read the drawing as an isopropyl ester of a prostaglandin F-type structure, in four parts.

- **Ester end:** the isopropyl group (iPr) is attached through O to a C=O.
- **Upper chain:** three CH2 groups lead to a cis (Z) C=C, then one more CH2 reaches the ring. This chain is drawn with a wedge bond.
- **Ring:** a cyclopentane carries two OH groups, both on wedge bonds. Its second chain is on a hashed bond.
- **Lower chain:** from the ring, two CH2 groups lead to a ketone C=O, which carries an n-heptyl group (seven carbons).

For stereochemistry, the wedge chain and both wedge OH groups sit on one face of the ring, and the hashed chain sits on the other. I worked out the configuration of the ring carbon bearing the upper chain directly from the drawing, which gave `[C@H]`. I then set the other three ring centres from the relative wedge/hash pattern, which matches the standard prostaglandin F (latanoprost-type) arrangement. The double bond is written Z.

SMILES: CC(C)OC(=O)CCC/C=C\C[C@H]1[C@@H](O)C[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1CCC(=O)CCCCCCC

name: sa_0056
text:
The drawing shows a central sulfur with two double-bonded oxygens (left and right), a CF3 group below, and an OTMS group above.

TMS is trimethylsilyl, Si(CH3)3, so OTMS expands to O[Si](C)(C). This gives trimethylsilyl trifluoromethanesulfonate (TMSOTf).

The SMILES is C[Si](C)(C)OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F. It has one sulfur, three oxygens, one silicon and four carbons, which matches the drawing atom for atom. There are no stereocentres.

SMILES: C[Si](C)(C)OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F

name: sa_0052
text:
I read the drawing as Boc-L-glutamic acid 5-benzyl ester, Boc-Glu(OBn)-OH.

- **Chain:** BnO2C–CH2–CH2–CH, so the benzyl ester sits on the far end of a two-carbon chain.
- **Stereocentre:** the α-carbon carries NH-Boc, a CO2H drawn on a hashed bond (pointing away from the viewer), the chain, and an implicit H (pointing toward the viewer).
- **Configuration:** the priorities are N > CO2H > CH2 chain > H. Going N → CO2H → chain appears clockwise on the page. The H points toward the viewer, so the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. This matches the L-glutamic acid configuration.
- **SMILES chirality:** I checked that `[C@H]` in `CC[C@H](N...)C(=O)O` corresponds to S by comparing it with L-Glu written as `N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O`. Swapping the chain and N positions flips `@@` to `@`, so the two agree.

SMILES: O=C(OCc1ccccc1)CC[C@H](NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C(=O)O

name: sa_0055
text:
The drawing is acebutolol, with the abbreviations written out in full.

- **Left side:** nPr–C(=O)–NH– is a butanamide, CCCC(=O)N, attached to the benzene ring.
- **Ring:** the amide N sits on one ring carbon. Going around the ring, there is a CH, then a carbon bearing Ac (acetyl, C(C)=O), then a carbon bearing the O. The ring then continues through two more CH carbons back to the N-bearing carbon. The acetyl and the ether O are therefore adjacent (ortho), and the amide N is para to the ether O.
- **Side chain:** the ring O links to CH2, then CH(OH), then CH2, then NH, then iPr (isopropyl, C(C)C).
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so none is included.

SMILES for the chain and ring: CCCC(=O)Nc1ccc(OCC(O)CNC(C)C)c(C(C)=O)c1

Checking the ring atoms: c1 (N-bearing), c, c, c(O…) is para to c1, then c(Ac), then c1. The ring is c1 (N), c, c, c(OR), c(Ac), c, closing back to c1. That gives six atoms: N-C, CH, CH, C-O, C-Ac, CH. The drawing agrees: the Ac carbon is adjacent to the CH, which is adjacent to the N-bearing carbon.

SMILES: CCCC(=O)Nc1ccc(OCC(O)CNC(C)C)c(C(C)=O)c1

name: sa_0058
text:
This is a 1,4-dihydropyridine with a 2,3-dichlorophenyl group at C4, which matches felodipine.

**Dihydropyridine ring.** The ring atoms are N1 (drawn as HN), C2 (bearing a methyl), C3 (bearing CO2Me), C4 (sp3, bearing the aryl group), C5 (bearing CO2Et) and C6 (bearing a methyl). C2=C3 and C5=C6 are the two double bonds.

**Aryl group.** The ring carbon attached to C4 is flanked by a carbon bearing Cl and, next to that, a second carbon bearing Cl. This gives a 2,3-dichlorophenyl group.

**Stereochemistry.** C4 is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is specified.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)OC)C1c1cccc(Cl)c1Cl

name: sa_0057
text:
The image shows Boc-protected tyrosine (Boc-Tyr-OH).

- **Left side:** a Boc group on an NH, attached to the α-carbon, which also carries the CO2H group.
- **Side chain:** a CH2 links the α-carbon to a benzene ring, with an OH on the carbon para to the CH2.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only stereocentre is the α-carbon, and the CO2H bond is drawn as a wedge. The H is implicit and points away from the viewer. Taking the substituents in priority order, N, then CO2H, then CH2, they run counterclockwise, so the centre is S. This matches L-tyrosine.

I wrote the SMILES with the same atom order as standard L-tyrosine (N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)O), which is the S form.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(O)cc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0059
text:
The image shows N‑Cbz‑serine (Cbz = benzyloxycarbonyl, C(=O)OCH2Ph), with the stereocentre drawn as a hashed bond to the CO2H group.

- **Skeleton:** HO–CH2–CH(NH–Cbz)–CO2H, which is a serine backbone.
- **Cbz group:** expanded to C(=O)OCc1ccccc1 on the nitrogen.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CO2H is on a hashed bond, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2OH > H. Reading N → CO2H → CH2OH in the drawing goes clockwise, and reversing for the H facing the viewer gives S, which is the L‑serine configuration.
- **SMILES chirality:** writing the centre as OC[C@H](NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)C(=O)O gives the S configuration. This follows from L‑serine being N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)O, and swapping the N and CH2 neighbours flips @@ to @.

SMILES: OC[C@H](NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0062
text:
The drawing shows a linear chain with F3C at the left end and SO3H at the right end.

Counting the chain carbons from the left: the F3C carbon is the first, followed by six carbons that each carry two F atoms (the six vertical F pairs, at x = 288, 433, 579, 724, 870, 1015, and 1160). That is seven vertical F pairs, so there are seven CF2 carbons plus the CF3 carbon, giving 8 carbons in total.

The fluorine count is 3 + 7×2 = 17, so the chain is C8F17.

The right-hand end is SO3H, which I read as a sulfonic acid, written S(=O)(=O)O. This molecule is perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS).

SMILES: OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)F

name: sa_0060
text:
This structure is lacosamide, (R)-2-acetamido-N-benzyl-3-methoxypropanamide.

- **Chain:** a methoxy group (MeO) is attached to a CH2, which is bonded to the stereocentre. The stereocentre carries an NHAc group (acetamide) on a wedge, and is also bonded to a C(=O) carbon.
- **Amide end:** that carbonyl carbon is bonded to NH, and the NH carries a benzyl group (Bn, CH2–C6H5).
- **Stereochemistry:** the wedge marks the NHAc nitrogen as pointing toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. The CIP priorities are N > C(=O)N > CH2OMe > H. Reading N → C(=O) → CH2 in the drawing runs clockwise with H at the back, which gives R.
- **SMILES check:** I checked that `COC[C@@H](NC(C)=O)C(=O)NCc1ccccc1` encodes R. With the CH2 as the first neighbour, `@@` means H → N → C(=O) runs clockwise. Moving H to the front costs one swap, so viewed from the side opposite H, CH2 → N → C(=O) runs clockwise, which is the same cycle as N → C(=O) → CH2. That is R.

SMILES: COC[C@@H](NC(C)=O)C(=O)NCc1ccccc1

name: sa_0061
text:
The drawing shows Cbz-NH on a central carbon that also carries a CH2Ph group and a CO2Me group, which is the methyl ester of N-Cbz-phenylalanine.

- **Substituents:** Cbz is a benzyloxycarbonyl group, so the nitrogen carries C(=O)OCH2Ph. Ph is a phenyl ring, and CO2Me is a methyl ester.
- **Stereochemistry:** Only the CO2Me bond is a wedge, so the centre is defined and the implicit hydrogen points away from the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CO2Me > CH2Ph > H. On the page, N (lower left) → CO2Me (right) → CH2 (upper left) runs counterclockwise, which gives S. This is the L-phenylalanine configuration.
- **SMILES:** Writing the centre as C(=O)[C@H](CH2Ph)N reproduces the S configuration, which I checked against the known L-Phe SMILES N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O by swapping the N and carbonyl neighbours.

SMILES: COC(=O)[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1

name: sa_0063
text:
The drawing shows a central CH carbon with three substituents: NEt2 (up), Bz (lower left), and a methyl (lower right). HCl is drawn separately as a salt.

Bz is the benzoyl group, C(=O)c1ccccc1. The alternative reading, benzyl, is normally abbreviated Bn. Benzoyl fits well here, because the molecule is then 2-(diethylamino)propiophenone, which is amfepramone (diethylpropion), a known drug that is sold as the hydrochloride.

Connectivity: CC(N(CC)CC)C(=O)c1ccccc1, with .Cl for the hydrochloride.

The central carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but the bonds are drawn plain, so I give no stereochemistry. The bond to NEt2 looks like it changes shade partway along, but this is just a rendering effect and not a wedge.

name: sa_0053
text:
I read the structure as a steroid-type skeleton (a fused 6-6-6-5 ring system) and assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond.

- That quaternary ring-fusion carbon carries a hashed methyl.
- The adjacent CH2 in the next ring is followed by a CH bearing NMe2 (wedge).
- The A ring carries OEt (hashed) on one carbon and OH (wedge) on the adjacent carbon.
- The second ring-fusion quaternary carbon carries a hashed methyl.
- Four ring-fusion hydrogens are drawn explicitly: two wedged, one hashed, and one more wedged.

**Stereo assignment**
I wrote the SMILES by walking the rings, then worked out @/@@ for each centre from the 2D geometry, treating the wedged or hashed group as toward or away from the viewer. The implicit H takes the opposite side.

I did not run the SMILES through a parser; the ring-closure digits and valences were checked by hand against the drawing.

name: sa_0066
text:
The drawing is a 20-carbon acid, 5,12-dihydroxy-eicosa-6,8,10,14-tetraenoic acid. This is the skeleton of leukotriene B4, and I read the stereochemistry from the wedges and double-bond geometry in the image.

**Chain, from the CO2H end:**
- C1 is the carboxylic acid, followed by C2–C4 as three CH2 groups.
- C5 carries an OH on a wedge bond.
- The C6=C7 double bond is Z, and C8=C9 and C10=C11 are both E.
- C12 carries an OH on a wedge bond.
- C13 is a CH2, then the C14=C15 double bond is Z.
- C16–C20 are the n-pentyl group drawn as "nPent", which I expanded to CCCCC.

**Stereocentres:**
- At C5 the priorities are OH > C6 (the vinyl carbon) > C4. With the H pointing away, the sequence runs counterclockwise, so C5 is S.
- At C12 the priorities are OH > C11 (the vinyl carbon) > C13. With the H pointing away, the sequence runs clockwise, so C12 is R.

This is (5S,12R)-dihydroxy-6Z,8E,10E,14Z-eicosatetraenoic acid, which is LTB4. I took the SMILES below from the known LTB4 string rather than deriving the @/@@ marks atom by atom, but it agrees with the R/S assignments above.

name: sa_0091

name: sa_0088
text:
I read this as a prostaglandin E2-type skeleton. The ring is a five-membered ketone with a hydroxyl, a Z-alkenyl carboxylic acid chain, and an E-alkenyl chain carrying a hydroxyl and an n-pentyl group.

**Ring (five carbons, going round):**
- C9 is the ketone carbon, C=O.
- C10 is CH2.
- C11 carries an OH on a wedge.
- C12 carries the lower chain on a hash.
- C8 carries the upper chain on a wedge, and is bonded to C9.

**Upper chain (from C8):** CH2, then a cis C=C (drawn as Z), then three CH2 groups, then CO2H.

**Lower chain (from C12):** a trans CH=CH (drawn as E), then a CH(OH) on a wedge, then an n-pentyl group.

**Stereo assignment:** I derived each centre's @/@@ by hand from the wedge and hash geometry, treating the implicit H as pointing opposite the drawn wedge or hash.
- C11 is `[C@@H]`.
- C12 is `[C@H]`.
- C8 is `[C@H]`.
- The hydroxyl-bearing carbon in the lower chain is `[C@@H]`.

I did not check the result against a canonical PGE2 SMILES, so the stereo labels rest on that manual derivation.

name: sa_0090
text:
I read the molecule as a 2,3,4,6-tetra-O-benzyl pyranose with a free anomeric hydroxyl, and worked out the chirality at each ring carbon from the wedge and hash bonds.

**Connectivity**
- The six-membered ring has one ring oxygen and five carbons.
- C1 is the anomeric carbon. It carries an OH and has plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.
- C2, C3 and C4 each carry an OBn group.
- C5 carries a CH2OBn group.
- Bn is expanded to CH2–C6H5.

**Stereochemistry, read from the drawing**
- C2: OBn on a wedge, giving `[C@H]` in the SMILES order used below.
- C3: OBn on a hash, giving `[C@H]`.
- C4: OBn on a wedge, giving `[C@@H]`.
- C5: CH2OBn on a hash, giving `[C@H]`.

I wrote the SMILES starting from the anomeric carbon and going round the ring through O, C5, C4, C3 and C2. The chirality symbols were assigned with the neighbour order that this writing produces, including the ring-closure digit at C2.

SMILES: OC1O[C@H](COCc2ccccc2)[C@@H](OCc2ccccc2)[C@H](OCc2ccccc2)[C@H]1OCc1ccccc1

name: sa_0096
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with substituents at opposite (para) positions.

- The left substituent is O2N, a nitro group attached to the ring through nitrogen: [N+](=O)[O-].
- The right substituent is CO2Et, an ethyl ester attached through the carbonyl carbon: C(=O)OCC.

This is ethyl 4-nitrobenzoate.

name: sa_0093
text:
Reading the drawing from left to right:

- The left end is a methanesulfonate ester, MsO–CH2, with Ms = CH3SO2.
- The first stereocentre has an OH on a wedge bond pointing down, so its implicit H points away from the viewer.
- The second stereocentre has an OH on a wedge bond pointing up, so its implicit H also points away from the viewer.
- The right end is CH2–OMs, another methanesulfonate ester.

This gives a butane-2,3-diol with a mesylate on each terminal carbon, 1,4-bis(methylsulfonyloxy)butane-2,3-diol.

I worked out the @/@@ labels from the wedge directions by looking at each centre with its H pointing away, then converting to SMILES neighbour order. Both centres come out as S, which matches treosulfan, (2S,3S)-configured.

name: sa_0095
text:
I read this as Fmoc-L-tryptophan with a Boc group on the indole nitrogen, Fmoc-Trp(Boc)-OH.

- **Backbone:** the stereocentre carries an NH–Fmoc group, a CO2H group on a wedge, and a CH2 that leads to the indole C3. The fourth substituent is an implicit H.
- **Indole:** the nitrogen is substituted with Boc, which expands to C(=O)OC(C)(C)C. The ring is fused to a benzene ring.
- **Fmoc:** this expands to the carbamate C(=O)OCH2–fluorenyl on the amine.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2 > H. The wedged CO2H points toward the viewer, so the H points away. Going N → CO2H → CH2 runs counterclockwise, which gives S, as in L-tryptophan.

For the SMILES, I wrote the centre as OC(=O)[C@H](Cc…)N… and checked the chirality symbol against the standard L-Trp SMILES, N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)O. Reordering the neighbours to put CO2H first swaps N and CO2H, which flips @@ to @.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@H](Cc1cn(C(=O)OC(C)(C)C)c2ccccc12)NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12

name: sa_0094
text:
I read the drawing as a 1,5-benzothiazepine 1,1-dioxide core carrying a glycine-terminated side chain. I assigned the stereocentre by hand from the hashed bond.

**Core ring:** a seven-membered ring containing a sulfonyl sulfur (S with two =O) and an N-phenyl nitrogen. Between them lie a CH2 and a quaternary carbon bearing two n-butyl groups, and the ring is fused to a benzene ring.

**Benzene substituents:** going round the ring from the carbon bonded to S, there is a CH, then a carbon bearing the O–CH2 ether, then a carbon bearing SMe, then a CH, then the carbon bonded to N.

**Side chain:**
- The ether chain is O–CH2–C(=O)–NH.
- The NH is attached to a stereocentre carrying a phenyl group (hashed bond).
- That carbon continues to C(=O)–NH–CH2–CO2H.

**Stereochemistry:** the CIP priorities at the stereocentre are N, then C(=O)N, then phenyl, then H. The phenyl is on a hashed bond, so H points toward the viewer. From the front, N → C(=O) → Ph runs counterclockwise, which reverses to clockwise once H is accounted for, giving R. In the SMILES below, `[C@H]` written as N[C@H](Ph)C(=O) corresponds to R, so it matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCCCC1(CCCC)CS(=O)(=O)c2cc(OCC(=O)N[C@H](c3ccccc3)C(=O)NCC(=O)O)c(SC)cc2N(c2ccccc2)C1

name: sa_0099
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring carrying an O–nOct (n-octyloxy) group ortho to a carbonyl.
- **Linker:** that carbonyl is part of an amide, C(=O)NH, which connects to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Right side of the para ring:** the ring bears an ester, C(=O)O–CH2CH2–N⁺.
- **Nitrogen:** N⁺ carries two ethyl groups and one methyl, so it is a quaternary ammonium.
- **Counterion:** Br⁻.

The abbreviations expand as follows: nOct is n-octyl, CCCCCCCC, and Et is ethyl, CC.

Assembled SMILES: CCCCCCCCOc1ccccc1C(=O)Nc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)OCC[N+](C)(CC)CC.[Br-]

name: sa_0097
text:
The drawing shows N-tosyl phenylalanine: a Ph–CH2 group, a central stereocentre bearing NH–Ts, and a hashed bond to CO2H.

**Stereocentre.** The CO2H bond is hashed (pointing away), so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2Ph > H. Reading N (right), then CO2H (lower left), then CH2 (upper left) runs clockwise on the page. With H toward the viewer, that reverses to counterclockwise, so the centre is S. This matches the L-phenylalanine configuration.

**SMILES.** L-Phe is written N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O, and the tosyl group (4-methylphenylsulfonyl) goes on the nitrogen without changing the neighbour order. The result is Cc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0100
text:
This is celiprolol. I read the structure region by region.

- **Urea end:** Et2N–C(=O)–NH–, attached to the aromatic ring.
- **Ring:** a benzene ring with three substituents. The NH sits at the lower-left carbon. The Ac group sits at the top carbon. The O-alkyl group sits at the right carbon, adjacent to the Ac carbon.
- **Ring connectivity:** going around the ring, C1 (bearing NH) is bonded to C2 (an unsubstituted CH), then to C3 (bearing Ac), then to C4 (bearing O). C4 is bonded to C5 (CH), then C6 (CH), and back to C1. The Ac group is therefore ortho to the O, and the NH is para to the O.
- **Side chain:** O–CH2–CH(OH)–CH2–NH–C(CH3)3.
- **Acetyl:** Ac is expanded to C(C)=O.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows only plain bonds, so no stereo is included.

SMILES written from the NH-bearing carbon: CCN(CC)C(=O)Nc1ccc(OCC(O)CNC(C)(C)C)c(C(C)=O)c1

Check: c1 (NH), c, c, c(O), c(Ac), c1 closes the ring. The ring has 6 atoms, and c(Ac) is adjacent to both c(O) and the final CH, which closes back to c1. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCN(CC)C(=O)Nc1ccc(OCC(O)CNC(C)(C)C)c(C(C)=O)c1

name: sa_0102
text:
The drawing shows amiodarone, with these parts:

- **Benzofuran:** a 2-butyl-benzofuran, with the n-butyl group on C2 and the carbonyl attached at C3.
- **Linker:** a ketone (C=O) joining C3 of the benzofuran to the phenyl ring.
- **Phenyl ring:** it carries two iodines at positions 3 and 5. The 4-position bears an O–CH2CH2–NEt2 group.

Writing it out: CCCCc1oc2ccccc2c1C(=O)c1cc(I)c(OCCN(CC)CC)c(I)c1

Atom check:
- The butyl chain is CCCC, attached to c1, which is C2 and is bonded to the ring O.
- The ring O is bonded to the fused carbon c2, then ccccc2 completes the benzo ring.
- c1 then closes the furan at C3, which carries the C(=O).
- The aryl ring is c1cc(I)c(OCCN(CC)CC)c(I)c1, with the iodines flanking the ether oxygen.

SMILES: CCCCc1oc2ccccc2c1C(=O)c1cc(I)c(OCCN(CC)CC)c(I)c1

name: sa_0098
text:
I read the molecule as an apremilast-like thieno[2,3-c]pyrrole-4,6-dione, and wrote the SMILES in pieces.

- **Aryl ring:** a benzene ring carries OEt (ethoxy) and OMe (methoxy) on adjacent carbons. The ring is attached through its third position to the stereocentre.
- **Side chain:** the stereocentre carries the aryl ring, the imide nitrogen, an implicit H, and a CH2–SO2–Me arm.
- **Bicyclic core:** an imide N is flanked by two C=O groups and fused to a thiophene. The thiophene runs S–CH=C(fused)–C(fused)=C(NHAc)–S, with NHAc expanded to NC(C)=O.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CH2 bond is a wedge, so it points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away. Viewed from the front, N → aryl → CH2 runs clockwise. This corresponds to `[C@@H]` when the SMILES is written as aryl–[C@@H](CH2…)–N.

SMILES: CCOc1cc(ccc1OC)[C@@H](CS(C)(=O)=O)N1C(=O)C2=CSC(NC(C)=O)=C2C1=O

name: sa_0101
text:
This structure matches aprepitant, and I wrote the SMILES from the known stereochemistry of that compound rather than deriving each centre from the wedges. I did not check the chirality of each wedge independently.

- **Triazolone:** a 1,2,4-triazol-5-one ring joined through a CH2 to the morpholine nitrogen.
- **Morpholine:** a ring with the 4-fluorophenyl group on the carbon next to N, drawn with a wedge. The adjacent carbon, next to the ring oxygen, carries an O–CH(CH3)–aryl ether, also drawn with a wedge.
- **Aryl group:** a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl ring on the CH(CH3) carbon, whose methyl is drawn with a wedge.

SMILES: C[C@H](c1cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c1)O[C@H]1OCCN(CC2=NNC(=O)N2)[C@@H]1c1ccc(F)cc1

name: sa_0103
text:
This looks like the fostemsavir structure: a 4-methoxy-7-(3-methyl-1,2,4-triazol-1-yl)-6-azaindole core carrying an N-CH2-O-phosphate group and a 3-glyoxylyl piperazine bearing a benzoyl group.

"Bz" is benzoyl, so it expands to C(=O)c1ccccc1.

Reading the rings:

- **Triazole:** N1 is attached to the pyridine ring carbon. Going around the ring, N1 is bonded to CH, then =N, then C(CH3)=N, then back to N1. The ring is n1cnc(C)n1, with the methyl on the carbon between the two nitrogens N4 and N2. The drawing has N (top left) = CH, and that CH is bonded to N1. The top-left N is bonded to the C(CH3), which is double bonded to the bottom N, and that bottom N is bonded to N1. The ring is therefore N1–CH=N–C(CH3)=N–N1, which is a 1,2,4-triazole with a 3-methyl group.

- **Azaindole:** The pyrrole N bears the CH2OP(=O)(O)O group. The ring-fusion carbon C7a is bonded to that N. C7 carries the triazole and is bonded to the pyridine N6. The CH (C5) follows, then C4 carrying OMe, then C3a. The pyrrole CH (C2) is bonded to N1, and C3 carries the C(=O)C(=O)N group.

SMILES: COc1cnc(-n2cnc(C)n2)c2n(COP(=O)(O)O)cc(C(=O)C(=O)N3CCN(C(=O)c4ccccc4)CC3)c12

Checking the SMILES: c1 (C4, OMe), then c (C5, H), n (N6), c(-triazole) (C7), c2 (C7a), n(COP...) (N1), c (C2), c(...) (C3), c12 (C3a, closing to C4 and C7a). This is consistent with the drawing.

SMILES: COc1cnc(-n2cnc(C)n2)c2n(COP(=O)(O)O)cc(C(=O)C(=O)N3CCN(C(=O)c4ccccc4)CC3)c12

name: sa_0104
text:
The drawing shows Fmoc-protected alanine: an Fmoc group on the nitrogen, an NH, a central carbon bearing a methyl group, and a CO2H group on a wedge bond.

**Stereocentre.** The central carbon has N at lower left, CH3 straight up and CO2H on a wedge toward the viewer. The implicit hydrogen therefore points away from the viewer.
- CIP priorities: N > CO2H > CH3 > H.
- Viewed from the front, N (lower left) → CO2H (lower right) → CH3 (top) runs counterclockwise.
- With H at the back, counterclockwise means S, so this is the L-alanine configuration.

**SMILES.** The Fmoc group is the carbamate C(=O)OCH2 attached to the 9-fluorenyl system. L-Alanine written as C[C@H](N)C(=O)O is S, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@H](NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12)C(=O)O

name: sa_0107
text:
The drawing shows nilutamide: a hydantoin ring (5,5-dimethylimidazolidine-2,4-dione) whose N3 is bonded to a phenyl ring.

**Hydantoin ring:** HN is bonded to a C=O carbon (top) and to a quaternary carbon carrying two methyl groups. The other N is bonded to both C=O carbons (top and bottom) and to the aryl ring. The bottom C=O is bonded to the quaternary carbon.

**Aryl ring:** Number the carbon attached to N as C1. Going around the ring from C1, the vertices are:
- C2, the top-left vertex (CH)
- C3, the top-right vertex (CH)
- C4, the right vertex, bearing NO2
- C5, the bottom-right vertex, bearing CF3
- C6, the bottom-left vertex (CH)

The NO2 group is therefore para to N, and the CF3 group is meta to N and ortho to NO2.

**SMILES:** CC1(C)NC(=O)N(C1=O)c1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])c(C(F)(F)F)c1

SMILES: CC1(C)NC(=O)N(C1=O)c1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])c(C(F)(F)F)c1

name: sa_0106
text:
The drawing is Fmoc-protected O-tert-butyl threonine (Fmoc-Thr(tBu)-OH).

- **Backbone:** the α-carbon carries the NH-Fmoc group and the CO2H. It is bonded to a β-carbon that carries a methyl group and an O-tBu ether.
- **α-carbon:** CO2H is on a wedge with H implied at the back. The priorities are N > CO2H > Cβ, and N → CO2H → Cβ runs counterclockwise, so this centre is S.
- **β-carbon:** the methyl is on a wedge with H implied at the back. The priorities are O > Cα > CH3, and O → Cα → CH3 runs clockwise, so this centre is R.
- **Result:** (2S,3R) is the L-threonine configuration, which matches the SMILES pattern C[C@@H](O…)[C@H](N…)C(=O)O.
- **Fmoc group:** the carbamate is written as NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12, with the fluorenyl CH attached to the CH2.

SMILES: C[C@@H](OC(C)(C)C)[C@H](NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12)C(=O)O

name: sa_0109
text:
The drawing shows Fmoc-protected leucine: an Fmoc-NH group on the α-carbon, a CO2H group, and an isobutyl (iBu) group on a hashed bond.

**Stereochemistry:** the α-carbon has the hashed iBu bond pointing away from the viewer, so its implicit hydrogen points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > iBu > H. In the drawing, N (lower left), CO2H (up) and iBu (lower right) run clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. This is the L-leucine configuration.

**SMILES check:** in `CC(C)C[C@H](N...)C(=O)O`, the neighbours of the stereocentre are written in the order CH2, H, N, COOH. This matches the standard L-leucine form `N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)O` after one swap, which flips @@ to @. The Fmoc group is the carbamate N–C(=O)–O–CH2 attached to the fluorenyl C9.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@H](NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12)C(=O)O

name: sa_0111

name: sa_0110
text:
This is Fmoc-Glu(OtBu)-OH, the N-Fmoc-protected L-glutamic acid with a tert-butyl ester on the side chain.

- The CIP priorities at the stereocentre are N > CO2H > CH2 > H.
- The CO2H is hashed (pointing away), so the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- Going N → CO2H → CH2 appears clockwise in the drawing. With H toward the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is S, which is the L configuration.

name: sa_0105
text:
I read this as an open-chain muramyl dipeptide analogue. From left to right it has a glutamine n-butyl ester, an alanine, and a lactyl ether joined to an open-chain amino sugar. The sugar carries a CHO, an NHAc, and two OH groups plus a terminal CH2OH.

- **Alanine:** NH–C(=O)–CH(CH3)–NH, with the methyl drawn on a wedge.
- **Lactyl ether:** C(=O)–CH(CH3)–O, with the methyl drawn on a hash.
- **Sugar chain:** O–CH–CH(NHAc)–CHO on one side. The other side continues CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH2OH.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash, taking the implicit H as opposite the drawn wedge or hash. The CHO carbon is not a stereocentre.

name: sa_0114
text:
The drawing shows a sulfur atom with two double-bonded oxygens (S=O), a CF3 group, and an O–Et group. This is ethyl trifluoromethanesulfonate (ethyl triflate).

name: sa_0108
text:
I read the molecule as a 2-amino-benzothiazole joined through a tropane ether to a substituted isoxazole.

- **Benzothiazole core:** the benzene ring carries F and CO2H. It is fused to the thiazole ring, which has S and N and a C2 carbon.
- **Bicyclic amine:** the benzothiazole C2 is bonded to the nitrogen of an 8-azabicyclo[3.2.1]octane (tropane). Its two bridgehead carbons carry hashed H atoms, both pointing away from the viewer.
- **Ether link:** the C3 carbon of the tropane bears an O–CH2 group. The drawing overlaps the bonds here, so the line from that carbon passes through the ring crossing to O.
- **Isoxazole:** the CH2 is attached to C4 of an isoxazole. C5 carries a cyclopropyl group, and C3 carries a 2-(trifluoromethoxy)phenyl group.

I assigned the stereo marks only to the two hashed bridgeheads. The C3 carbon of the tropane is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo mark.

name: sa_0113
text:
This structure is apalutamide.

**Pyridine ring.** The ring atoms are N, C(CN), C(CF3), CH, C(attached to the thiohydantoin N), and CH. The nitrile carbon is bonded to the ring carbon adjacent to the ring N. The CF3 sits on the next ring carbon. The ring carbon bearing the thiohydantoin N lies between a CH on the CF3 side and a CH on the ring-N side.

**Spiro thiohydantoin.** A 5-membered ring containing N, C(=O), a spiro carbon, N, and C(=S). The spiro carbon is part of a cyclobutane. One N is bonded to the pyridine and sits between C=O and C=S. The other N is bonded to the fluorobenzamide aryl group and the spiro carbon.

**Benzamide ring.** The carbon attached to N is para to the carbon bearing C(=O)NHMe. The fluorine is on the carbon ortho to the amide carbon and meta to the N-bearing carbon.

**SMILES.**
- Pyridine: c1(C#N)ncc(cc1C(F)(F)F) with the ring N attached at the position para to the nitrile-bearing carbon... checking the ring order: N–C(CN)–C(CF3)–CH–C(N-sub)–CH–back to N. Written as N#Cc1ncc(cc1C(F)(F)F)N2...
- Thiohydantoin: N2C(=S)N(...)C3(CCC3)C2=O. The pyridine-bearing N is bonded to C(=O) and C(=S). The aryl-bearing N is bonded to C(=S) and the spiro carbon.
- Aryl: c4ccc(C(=O)NC)c(F)c4.

SMILES: N#Cc1ncc(cc1C(F)(F)F)N1C(=S)N(c2ccc(C(=O)NC)c(F)c2)C2(CCC2)C1=O

name: sa_0117
text:
The drawing shows a central sulfur with two double-bonded oxygens, a CF3 group, and an O–TIPS group. This is triisopropylsilyl triflate, TIPS-OTf.

TIPS is the triisopropylsilyl group, Si(CH(CH3)2)3. The silicon is bonded to the oxygen that is attached to sulfur.

Written as SMILES: FC(F)(F)S(=O)(=O)O[Si](C(C)C)(C(C)C)C(C)C

This has the S(=O)(=O) core, one CF3 on sulfur, and the O–Si bond, with three isopropyl groups on silicon. The drawing has no wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: FC(F)(F)S(=O)(=O)O[Si](C(C)C)(C(C)C)C(C)C

name: sa_0116
text:
The drawing matches dutasteride: N‑[2,5‑bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]‑3‑oxo‑4‑aza‑5α‑androst‑1‑ene‑17β‑carboxamide. I identified it from the overall structure and did not re-derive each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes, so the stereo descriptors are taken from the known dutasteride SMILES.

- **Aryl ring:** a benzene ring bears the amide NH on one carbon, with CF3 groups at the ortho position (top) and at the position para to the ring carbon next to the NH (bottom). That is a 2,5‑bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl pattern.
- **Amide:** the NH is joined to a C(=O) that carries a wedge bond to the five‑membered D ring.
- **Steroid core:** the four fused rings carry two wedged methyl groups at the ring junctions. Several ring‑fusion hydrogens are drawn with wedges or hashes.
- **A ring:** this ring is a lactam. It contains an NH next to a C(=O) and a C=C double bond (the 4‑aza‑1‑en‑3‑one pattern).

SMILES: C[C@]12CC[C@H]3[C@H]([C@@H]1CC[C@@H]2C(=O)NC4=C(C=CC(=C4)C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F)CC[C@@H]5[C@@]3(C=CC(=O)N5)C

name: sa_0120
text:
The image shows two separate components: diethylamine and a dihydroxybenzenesulfonic acid.

**Diethylamine:** Et–NH–Et, which is CCNCC.

**Aromatic component:** a benzene ring carrying an SO3H group and two OH groups.
- The SO3H sits at the upper-left ring carbon, which I'll call C1.
- Moving around the ring, the carbon at the lower left is C2 and bears an OH, adjacent to C1.
- The next carbon is the bottom one (C3), then the lower right (C4), then the right carbon (C5) bearing the second OH, and finally the top carbon (C6), which links back to C1.
- The OH-bearing carbon at the right is therefore para to the OH-bearing carbon at the lower left, which is the 2,5-dihydroxybenzenesulfonic acid pattern.

The ring SMILES is OS(=O)(=O)c1cc(O)ccc1O.

Combined, with the two components separated by a dot:

SMILES: CCNCC.OS(=O)(=O)c1cc(O)ccc1O

name: sa_0118
text:
The drawing shows Ph–CH2–CH(NHBoc)–CO2H, which is Boc-protected phenylalanine. The stereocentre carries a hashed bond to the CO2H group.

**Connectivity:**
- Ph is a phenyl ring, `c1ccccc1`, attached to a CH2 group.
- The CH2 is bonded to the central CH, which carries NH–Boc.
- Boc expands to C(=O)OC(C)(C)C.
- The remaining substituent on the central carbon is the carboxylic acid, C(=O)O.

**Stereochemistry:**
- The CO2H is hashed, so it points away from the viewer, and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2 > H.
- Viewed from the front, N (right) → CO2H (lower left) → CH2 (upper left) runs clockwise.
- Because the lowest-priority H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is S. This is the L-phenylalanine configuration.

The SMILES for Boc-L-Phe, which I checked against this S assignment, is:

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0119
text:
The drawing shows Cbz-protected alanine (Cbz-Ala-OH).

- **Backbone:** the central carbon carries a methyl group (the plain bond going up), an NH bonded to Cbz (lower left), and a CO2H group (lower right, drawn as a wedge).
- **Cbz expanded:** Cbz is benzyloxycarbonyl, so the nitrogen substituent is C(=O)OCc1ccccc1.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CO2H wedge points toward the viewer, so the implicit hydrogen points away. The priorities are N > CO2H > CH3 > H. Going N (lower left) → CO2H (lower right) → CH3 (top) is counterclockwise with H at the back, so the centre is S, which is the L-alanine configuration.
- **SMILES:** C[C@H](N)C(=O)O is the L-alanine chirality, and adding the Cbz group on nitrogen gives the answer below.

SMILES: C[C@H](NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0122
text:
The structure is flutamide: an isobutyramide on an aniline nitrogen, with a benzene ring carrying CF3 and NO2.

Reading the drawing:
- The left group is iPr (isopropyl) attached to C(=O), which is bonded to NH. The acyl group is therefore isobutyryl, written CC(C)C(=O)N.
- The NH attaches to a ring carbon. Going around the ring, the next carbon (up and right) is an unsubstituted CH, then the carbon bearing CF3. After that comes the carbon bearing NO2, then two more CH carbons back to the start.
- This puts CF3 meta to the NH and NO2 para to the NH, with CF3 and NO2 adjacent to each other.

SMILES for the ring: c1(NC(=O)C(C)C)cc(C(F)(F)F)c([N+](=O)[O-])cc1

SMILES: CC(C)C(=O)Nc1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])c(C(F)(F)F)c1

name: sa_0115
text:
I read the drawing as a tri-O-benzoyl-1-O-acetyl pentofuranose.

**Ring and substituents**
- The five-membered ring is O, C1, C2, C3, C4.
- C1 carries OAc on a hashed bond (pointing away from the viewer).
- C2 and C3 each carry OBz on a wedge (toward the viewer).
- C4 carries CH2–OBz on a hashed bond.
- Every other bond is plain.

**Stereo assignment**
For each ring carbon I took the implicit hydrogen as pointing opposite to the drawn wedge or hash. I then read the rotation of the other three neighbours from the 2D positions and converted it to @/@@ for the SMILES neighbour order.

The result is C1 `@@`, C4 `@`, C3 `@@`, C2 `@`. I derived these by hand and did not run the SMILES through a toolkit to confirm them.

SMILES: CC(=O)O[C@@H]1O[C@H](COC(=O)c2ccccc2)[C@@H](OC(=O)c2ccccc2)[C@H]1OC(=O)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0125
text:
The drawing shows a central CH carbon bearing two Ph groups, bonded to an O. The O connects to a CH2CH2 chain that ends in NMe2. This is diphenhydramine.

Expanding the abbreviations (Ph to phenyl, NMe2 to dimethylamino) gives CN(C)CCOC(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1. The central carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity only if its two substituents differ, and here both are phenyl, so it is not a stereocentre. The drawing also shows no wedges or hashes, so no stereo is needed.

SMILES: CN(C)CCOC(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0124
text:
This is nicardipine, a 1,4-dihydropyridine, drawn with no stereochemistry.

**Dihydropyridine core:**
- The ring contains NH, a C(CH3)= carbon, a C(CO2R)= carbon, the sp3 CH carrying the aryl group, a second C(CO2Me)= carbon, and a second C(CH3)= carbon.
- The top C(CH3)=C is joined to the ester carbon that bears the O-linked chain.
- The bottom C=C(CH3) carries CO2Me.

**Aryl group:** a 3-nitrophenyl ring. The ring carbon bonded to the CH is flanked by one CH on the nitro side, and the nitro-bearing carbon is meta to the attachment point.

**Side chain:** C(=O)OCCN(C)Bn, where Bn is benzyl (CH2Ph).

**Assembly:**
- Ring: C1(C)=C(C(=O)OCCN(C)Cc2ccccc2)C(c2cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c2)C(C(=O)OC)=C(C)N1
- Nitrophenyl check: c2cccc(N(=O)=O)c2 puts the nitro group at position 3 relative to the attachment carbon, so it is meta.

SMILES: CC1=C(C(=O)OCCN(C)Cc2ccccc2)C(c2cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c2)C(C(=O)OC)=C(C)N1

name: sa_0126
text:
The drawing is a benzene ring with three substituents: a methyl group, a nitro group next to it, and a second nitro group further round the ring.

Ring vertices, read from the image:
- C1 at (368, 914) carries the methyl group.
- C2 at (456, 627) carries the O2N group.
- C3 at (748, 557) has no substituent.
- C4 at (955, 778) carries the NO2 group.
- C5 at (866, 1066) has no substituent.
- C6 at (574, 1136) has no substituent.

The methyl-bearing carbon C1 is adjacent to C2 (nitro). C4 (nitro) is separated from C2 by C3, so the two nitro groups are meta to each other. C4 is para to C1. This gives a 1-methyl-2,4-dinitrobenzene pattern, which is 2,4-dinitrotoluene.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1[N+](=O)[O-])[N+](=O)[O-]

name: sa_0127
text:
The drawing is a 1,4-dihydropyridine, which is the nifedipine structure.

- **Dihydropyridine ring:** NH, then C(CH3)=C(CO2Me), then the sp3 CH at C4, then C(CO2Me)=C(CH3) back to NH.
- **C4 substituent:** a 2-nitrophenyl group. The benzene carbon attached to C4 is adjacent to the carbon bearing NO2.
- **Ester groups:** each MeO2C is a methyl ester, written C(=O)OC in the SMILES.
- **Stereochemistry:** C4 is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is included.
