name: sa_0123
text:
The drawing shows lysine: an alpha carbon carrying a Cbz-protected NH and a wedged CO2H, and a chain of four CH2 groups ending in a Boc-protected NH.

**Chain.** From the alpha carbon, the chain runs through four CH2 vertices to the NH-Boc group.

**Protecting groups.** Cbz expands to C(=O)OCc1ccccc1 and Boc to C(=O)OC(C)(C)C.

**Stereochemistry.** The CO2H is on a wedge, so it points toward the viewer, and the implicit H points away.
- Seen from the front, the substituents go N (up), then chain (right), then CO2H (lower left), which is clockwise.
- The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > chain, and N → CO2H → chain runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S, the L-lysine configuration.
- The matching SMILES is N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)O.

The full molecule is Nα-Cbz-Nε-Boc-L-lysine.

SMILES: O=C(OCc1ccccc1)N[C@@H](CCCCNC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C(=O)O

name: sa_0129
text:
The drawing shows a piperidine ring (six-membered, one nitrogen) with an N-methyl group. The carbon opposite the nitrogen (C4) carries two substituents: a CO2Et group (ethyl ester) and a phenyl group. This is pethidine (meperidine).

Writing the SMILES: the N-methyl and ring are CN1CCC(CC1)(...), with the ester written as C(=O)OCC and the phenyl as c1ccccc1. All bonds are plain, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)C1(c2ccccc2)CCN(C)CC1

name: sa_0131
text:
This structure is apremilast, read as follows:

- **Left ring:** a benzene ring bearing OMe and OEt on adjacent carbons, with the OMe at the position para to the side chain. Its remaining ring carbon carries the stereocentre.
- **Side chain:** the stereocentre bears a CH2–SO2–CH3 group (drawn on a wedge), the phthalimide nitrogen, the aryl ring and an implicit H.
- **Right ring system:** a phthalimide (isoindoline-1,3-dione) in which the benzo ring carries an NHAc (acetamido) group on the carbon next to a carbonyl-bearing ring carbon.

**Stereochemistry:** the CIP priorities at the stereocentre are N > CH2SO2Me > aryl > H. The CH2 is on a wedge, so H points away from the viewer. Going N → CH2 → aryl in the drawing runs counterclockwise, which gives S. I checked that the SMILES below, with `[C@@H]` written in the order aryl, H, CH2, N, also gives S.

SMILES: CCOc1cc(ccc1OC)[C@@H](CS(C)(=O)=O)N1C(=O)c2cccc(NC(C)=O)c2C1=O

name: sa_0121
text:
I read the molecule as an ethyl ester, N-linked alanine-type amide of a 2-carboxy-octahydrocyclopenta[b]pyrrole. This is a perindopril-like skeleton, but the bicycle is 5-5 rather than 6-5.

**Skeleton**
- The left bicycle has a pyrrolidine ring (N, C2 bearing CO2H, CH2, C3a, C6a) fused to a cyclopentane ring. The cyclopentane ring has three CH2 groups and the two fusion carbons.
- N is acylated by C(=O)–CH(CH3)–NH–CH(CO2Et)–CH2CH2–Ph.
- Ph and Et are expanded to phenyl and ethyl.

**Stereocentres**
- All five stereocentres are drawn with wedges or hashes, so all five carry stereo marks.
- For each one I took the three drawn neighbours, worked out their rotation direction from the 2D coordinates, and combined that with whether the wedge or hash puts the implicit H in front or behind.
- That gave the SMILES chirality tags below.

| Centre | Tag |
|---|---|
| CH(CH3) (hashed methyl) | `@` |
| CH(CO2Et) (wedged ester) | `@@` |
| C2 (wedged CO2H) | `@` |
| C3a (hashed H) | `@@` |
| C6a (hashed H) | `@` |

SMILES: C[C@H](N[C@@H](CCc1ccccc1)C(=O)OCC)C(=O)N1[C@H](C(=O)O)C[C@@H]2CCC[C@H]12

name: sa_0133
text:
The drawing shows a para-disubstituted benzene ring.

- One ring substituent is NH–SO2–Me, a methanesulfonamide.
- The other ring substituent is a CH(OH) carbon, which continues as a chain of CH2, CH2, CH2 to a nitrogen. The chain count is: the CH(OH) carbon, then two vertices at the bottom and top of the zigzag, then one more carbon attached to N. Reading the zigzag from the ring: ring–CH(OH) at (712, 780), then (620, 695), (502, 732), (410, 648), then N. That gives CH(OH), three CH2 groups, and N.
- The nitrogen carries an ethyl group and an n-heptyl group.

The heptyl group is a straight chain of seven carbons, CCCCCCC.

No wedges or hashes are drawn, so there is no stereochemistry.

Assembled SMILES: CCCCCCCN(CC)CCCC(O)c1ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc1

SMILES: CCCCCCCN(CC)CCCC(O)c1ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc1

name: sa_0128
text:
I read this as the N-benzoyl derivative of staurosporine (midostaurin). The structure has an indolocarbazole core with a lactam, and a bridged furanose-type ring carrying a methyl group, an OMe group and an N-methylbenzamide.

The abbreviations expand as follows: Bz becomes a benzoyl group, C(=O)c1ccccc1, and MeO becomes OC.

I set the four stereocentres from the wedges and hashes:
- The N(Me)Bz carbon has a wedge to N, giving `[C@@H]`.
- The CH(OMe) carbon has a wedge to OMe, giving `[C@@H]`.
- The quaternary carbon bearing the methyl has a hashed methyl, giving `[C@@]`.
- The O–CH–N carbon has a hashed H, giving `[C@H]`.

I checked the ring closures against the drawing: ring 1 closes the ring between the CH(OMe) and N(Me)Bz carbons, and ring 2 links the O–CH–N carbon to the lower indole nitrogen.

SMILES: CN(C(=O)c1ccccc1)[C@@H]1C[C@H]2O[C@@](C)([C@@H]1OC)n1c3ccccc3c3c4CNC(=O)c4c4c5ccccc5n2c4c31

name: sa_0134
text:
The drawing shows a piperidine ring with these parts:

- **C4 of the ring (quaternary):** it carries a CO2Me group (drawn as MeO2C) and an N(Ph)C(=O)Et group, which is an N-phenylpropanamide.
- **Ring nitrogen:** it carries a CH2CH2CO2Me chain, drawn as N–CH2–CH2–CO2Me, i.e. a methyl 3-aminopropanoate.

Chain check: the ring N connects to a carbon at (575,1107), then to a carbon at (371,1142), then to the CO2Me carbon. That gives N–CH2–CH2–C(=O)OMe, two CH2 groups and then the ester carbon, which matches.

Ring check: the vertices are C4 (783,529), (581,565), (511,758), N (645,910), (846,879) and (916,686). That is six atoms, so the ring is a piperidine.

SMILES: CCC(=O)N(c1ccccc1)C1(C(=O)OC)CCN(CCC(=O)OC)CC1

name: sa_0132
text:
Reading the chain from the HO₂C end, I count 12 carbons up to the carbon bearing OH, and that carbon also carries an n-hexyl group. The skeleton is C1 (COOH) through C12 (CHOH), then six more carbons in the hexyl group, giving an 18-carbon chain.

- **Double bond:** it sits between C9 and C10. The neighbouring chain carbons C8 and C11 both point upward in the drawing, so the geometry is cis (Z).
- **Stereocentre at C12:** the hexyl group is drawn on a wedge, OH points lower right and C11 points lower left. Priorities are OH > C11 > hexyl > H. C11 outranks hexyl because its next carbon is an alkene carbon with (C,C,H), against (C,H,H) for the hexyl chain. With H pointing away, OH → C11 → hexyl runs clockwise, so the centre is R.

The molecule is (R,Z)-12-hydroxyoctadec-9-enoic acid, which is ricinoleic acid. I checked that `[C@@H]` in the SMILES below gives R with this neighbour order.

SMILES: CCCCCC[C@@H](O)C/C=C\CCCCCCCC(=O)O

name: sa_0136
text:
I read the drawing as a quaternary carbon with four substituents: two methyl groups (the vertical lines up and down), a CH2 leading to the BzO group on the left, and an NH carrying nPr on the right.

BzO is benzoyloxy, PhC(=O)O–. I took "Bz" to mean benzoyl rather than benzyl because that is the usual meaning of the abbreviation. The "O" in the label is then the ester oxygen attached to the CH2.

nPr is n-propyl, CH2CH2CH3.

Assembled, the molecule is the benzoate ester of 2-methyl-2-(propylamino)propan-1-ol: O=C(c1ccccc1)OCC(C)(C)NCCC

SMILES: CCCNC(C)(C)COC(=O)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0135
text:
This structure is fluvoxamine, read from the drawing as follows:

- **Aromatic ring:** a para-substituted benzene carrying CF3 on the left, drawn as F3C.
- **Chain to the methoxy group:** from the ring-bearing C=N carbon, four CH2 groups lead to OMe (the O–CH3 at the top right).
- **Oxime side:** the C=N nitrogen carries an O–CH2–CH2–NH2 group.
- **C=N geometry:** the aryl group on carbon and the O on nitrogen lie on opposite sides of the double bond, so the aryl and O are trans. The chain and O are therefore cis. The aryl is the higher-priority group on carbon and O is the higher-priority group on nitrogen, so this is the E isomer.

The SMILES `COCCCC/C(=N\OCCN)c1ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc1` encodes the chain and O as cis around C=N, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: COCCCC/C(=N\OCCN)c1ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc1

name: sa_0138
text:
The drawing shows two substituted benzene rings joined by a thioether–propyl–ether linker, with a butanoic acid chain on the right ring.

**Left ring.** Going around the ring from the top:
- C1 carries OH.
- C2 carries nPr (propyl).
- C3 carries S.
- C4 and C5 are CH.
- C6 carries Ac (acetyl), and is adjacent to C1.

So the left ring is a 2-hydroxy-3-propyl-4-thio-substituted acetophenone: C(C)(=O)c1ccc(S...)c(CCC)c1O.

**Linker.** S–CH2CH2CH2–O, three carbons, with the O attached to the right ring.

**Right ring.** Going around the ring:
- Ca carries the O of the linker (lower left).
- Cb carries nPr (bottom).
- Cc carries O–(CH2)3–CO2H.
- Cd carries Ac.
- Ce and Cf are CH.

The ring order is Ca (O-linker), Cb (nPr), Cc (O-butanoic), Cd (Ac), Ce (CH), Cf (CH), back to Ca.

The butanoic acid chain is O–CH2CH2CH2–CO2H, which reads as O, then three CH2 carbons, then COOH. In the drawing the carbons are at 1140,808, 1232,835 and 1253,930, followed by CO2H, so the chain is OCCCC(=O)O.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Left ring: CC(=O)c1ccc(SCCCOc2ccc(C(C)=O)c(OCCCC(=O)O)c2CCC)c(CCC)c1O
- Right ring: c2ccc(C(C)=O)c(OCCCC(=O)O)c2CCC, where the first c2 carries the linker O, the last c2 carries nPr, and the ring closes back onto the first.

SMILES: CC(=O)c1ccc(SCCCOc2ccc(C(C)=O)c(OCCCC(=O)O)c2CCC)c(CCC)c1O

name: sa_0137
text:
I read the molecule as a 3-acylindole ketone with a single stereocentre, and assigned that centre from the hashed bond.

**Fragments read from the drawing**
- Left ring: a benzene bearing SO2Me, OMe and NH in a 1,3,5 pattern.
- Stereocentre: a CH with a hashed bond to the NH, a bond to a C=O, and a bond to a second aryl ring.
- Lower aryl ring: 4-chloro-2-methoxyphenyl, attached to the stereocentre at C1.
- Ketone: C=O linking the stereocentre to C3 of an indole.
- Indole: a free N–H, with OCF3 at C5.

**Stereochemistry**
- The NH is on the hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- Viewed from the H side, the order N → C(=O) → aryl runs clockwise.
- For the SMILES atom order N, H, aryl, C(=O), the permutation from (H; N, C=O, aryl) is two swaps, which is even. Clockwise therefore maps to `@@`.

The SMILES is `CS(=O)(=O)c1cc(OC)cc(N[C@@H](c2ccc(Cl)cc2OC)C(=O)c2c[nH]c3ccc(OC(F)(F)F)cc23)c1`.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)c1cc(OC)cc(N[C@@H](c2ccc(Cl)cc2OC)C(=O)c2c[nH]c3ccc(OC(F)(F)F)cc23)c1

name: sa_0141
text:
The drawing is a benzene ring carrying six substituents, which I read going around the ring.

- The top-right carbon bears CO2H.
- The right carbon bears I.
- The bottom-right carbon bears NHAc, which is NHC(=O)C.
- The bottom-left carbon bears I.
- The left carbon bears N(CH3)Ac, a nitrogen with a methyl and an acetyl group.

Writing the SMILES from the ring in the order above:

OC(=O)c1c(I)c(NC(C)=O)c(I)c(N(C)C(C)=O)c1I

Checking the ring: c1 (CO2H), c(I), c(NHAc), c(I), c(N(Me)Ac), c1I. That is six aromatic carbons.

The order matches the drawing. Going clockwise from the top-right carbon, the substituents are CO2H, I, NHAc, I, N(Me)Ac, I.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1c(I)c(NC(C)=O)c(I)c(N(C)C(C)=O)c1I

name: sa_0140
text:
The drawing shows N-Cbz-protected tyrosine, with a free carboxylic acid and a para-hydroxyphenyl group on the side chain.

- **Side chain:** a CH2 attached to a benzene ring that carries an OH para to the CH2 (from the ring OH label).
- **Backbone:** a stereocentre bonded to NH-Cbz, CO2H, the CH2 and an implicit H.
- **Cbz:** expanded to benzyloxycarbonyl, C(=O)OCH2Ph.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CO2H bond is a wedge, so it points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away. The priorities are N > CO2H > CH2. On the page, N is at the top, CO2H at lower left and CH2 at lower right, so N → CO2H → CH2 runs counterclockwise. That gives S, which is the L-tyrosine configuration.

For the SMILES, I write the neighbours in the order N, H, CH2, COOH. For S this order takes `@@`.

name: sa_0139
text:
The drawing is enalapril, with all three stereocentres S.

- **Ethyl ester end:** a CO2Et group on a hashed bond, attached to a carbon that bears the NH and a CH2CH2–Ph chain (the ethyl and phenyl labels expanded to CC and c1ccccc1).
- **Alanine unit:** an NH-bearing carbon with a wedged methyl, linked to an amide C=O.
- **Proline unit:** the amide nitrogen sits in a five-membered ring (N plus four carbons). The ring carbon next to N carries a hashed CO2H.

Stereochemistry, assigned from the wedges and hashes with the implicit H, using CIP priorities:
- Proline α-carbon: S.
- Alanine α-carbon (wedged methyl): S.
- Phenylbutanoate carbon (hashed CO2Et): S.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)[C@H](CCc1ccccc1)N[C@@H](C)C(=O)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)O

name: sa_0130
text:
I read the structure as a 16-membered macrolactone carrying two sugars, and wrote the SMILES region by region, assigning each wedge or hash to a chirality tag.

**Macrolactone ring** (numbered from the lactone carbonyl as C1):
- C1 is the lactone C=O and C2 is a CH2.
- C3 carries a hashed OH and C4 a hashed OMe.
- C5 carries a wedged O-glycoside link to the amino sugar.
- C6 carries a wedged CH2CHO side chain, and C7 is a CH2.
- C8 carries a wedged methyl and C9 a wedged OH.
- C10=C11 and C12=C13 are two conjugated double bonds. Both are drawn trans (E).
- C14 is a CH2, and C15 carries a wedged methyl and is bonded to the ring oxygen.

**Amino sugar** (a mycaminose-type pyranose, attached at C5 of the ring):
- The anomeric carbon has a wedged bond to the macrolide oxygen.
- It carries a hashed 2'-OH, a wedged 3'-NMe2, and a 5'-methyl on a wedge.
- The 4'-O is hashed and links to the second sugar.

**Second sugar** (a mycarose-type branched pyranose):
- The anomeric carbon is attached through a hashed bond.
- C2'' is a CH2.
- C3'' carries a methyl on a wedge and an O-propionyl group (the Et-C(=O)O label).
- C4'' carries a hashed O-butyryl group (the nPr-C(=O)O label).
- C5'' carries a wedged methyl.

I did not run this through a SMILES parser. I did check the string by hand against the atoms and bonds in the drawing, including the chirality tags and the E,E geometry.

name: sa_0144

I read the drawing as an oseltamivir-type cyclohexene: ethyl 4-acetamido-5-amino-3-(pentan-3-yloxy)cyclohex-1-ene-1-carboxylate. The SMILES below was written from that reading, not checked in software.

name: sa_0146
text:
The drawing shows a 1,4-dihydropyridine ring with a 3-nitrophenyl group on C4 (the structure of nitrendipine).

**Ring.** The ring atoms are N1 (drawn as HN), C2, C3, C4, C5 and C6.

name: sa_0147
text:
The drawing shows a central sulfur bonded to a CF3 group, two doubly bonded oxygens, and an "OTf" group.

"OTf" is the triflate group, which is O–S(=O)(=O)–CF3. So the molecule is triflic anhydride, CF3SO2–O–SO2CF3.

The drawing is therefore an abbreviated form of the anhydride, with one triflyl group written out and the other collapsed to Tf.

Expanding the abbreviation gives:

FC(F)(F)S(=O)(=O)OS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F

This has a C–S bond to CF3, two S=O bonds, and an S–O–S linkage to the second triflyl group.

name: sa_0142

- The three-carbon bridge consists of the CH carrying CO2Me, the CH carrying OBz, and a CH2.

**Stereochemistry from the drawing**
- Both bridgehead H atoms are drawn as hashed bonds.
- The CO2Me and OBz groups are also drawn as hashed bonds.

name: sa_0148
text:
The drawing shows Fmoc-Lys(Boc)-OH, a lysine with both amino groups protected.

- **Backbone:** the central carbon carries the carboxylic acid (HO₂C), the α-NH and a four-carbon chain. The chain ends in an NH, which gives the lysine side chain.
- **Protecting groups:** the α-NH carries Fmoc (fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl) and the terminal NH carries Boc (tert-butoxycarbonyl).
- **Stereochemistry:** the only wedge is on the bond to the CO₂H group, so the central carbon is the only stereocentre. With the implicit H pointing away from the viewer, the priorities N > CO₂H > CH₂ run counterclockwise on the page. That makes the centre S, which is L-lysine.
- **SMILES chirality:** written starting from the carboxyl carbon, S corresponds to `[C@H]`. I checked this by swapping the N and C(=O) neighbours relative to the standard L-lysine SMILES `N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)O`.

name: sa_0150
text:
The drawing shows Boc-protected methionine: a CH3–S–CH2–CH2 chain attached to the α-carbon, which carries an NH–Boc group and a CO2H group.

**Stereochemistry:** The CO2H is on a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2 > H. On screen, N (upper right) → CO2H (down) → CH2 (upper left) runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. This matches L-methionine.

**SMILES:** The Boc group expands to C(=O)OC(C)(C)C on the nitrogen. L-methionine is written CSCC[C@H](N)C(=O)O, so the Boc-protected form keeps the same chirality tag.

name: sa_0149

The drawing shows Fmoc-proline: a pyrrolidine ring with an Fmoc group on the nitrogen and a CO2H group on C2.

name: sa_0151

name: sa_0152

The drawing shows a sulfur atom with two double-bonded oxygens (S=O on the left and right). It also has an OTBS group on top and a CF3 group on the bottom.

name: sa_0145
text:
I read this as a linear depsipeptide of the dolastatin 15 type, assembled from the N-terminus to the C-terminus:

1. Me2N–CH(iPr)–C(=O)–NH– (N,N-dimethylvaline)
2. –CH(iPr)–C(=O)–N(Me)– (valine, then N-methylvaline)
3. –CH(iPr)–C(=O)– into the first pyrrolidine (the N-methylvaline carbonyl acylates proline)
4. –proline–C(=O)– into the second pyrrolidine (a second proline)
5. –proline–C(=O)–O– (ester link to the 2-hydroxyisovalerate unit)
6. –CH(iPr)–C(=O)–N1 (2-hydroxyisovaleric acid unit)
7. A 5-membered unsaturated lactam: N1–CH(CH2Ph)–C(OMe)=CH–C1(=O)

I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash by comparing the drawn geometry with the neighbour order in the SMILES.

- The three valine-type carbons (dimethylvaline, valine, N-methylvaline) all come out as `@@`.
- Both proline α-carbons come out as `@`.
- The hydroxyisovalerate carbon (the O–CH(iPr)–C(=O) centre) comes out as `@@`.
- The lactam CH bearing the benzyl group comes out as `@@`.

name: sa_0155

name: sa_0153
text:
This structure is diltiazem, the 1,5-benzothiazepin-4-one with a 4-methoxyphenyl group, an acetoxy group and a 2-(dimethylamino)ethyl chain on the ring nitrogen.

name: sa_0158

name: sa_0157
text:
I read this as gadopentetate dimeglumine: a Gd³⁺ ion, the DTPA ligand drawn with three carboxylate groups and two CO₂H groups, and two N‑methylglucamine (meglumine) molecules.

**Meglumine units (both drawn identically):** The chain runs CH3‑NH‑CH2‑CH(OH)‑CH(OH)‑CH(OH)‑CH(OH)‑CH2OH. I assigned each of the four stereocentres from the wedges and hashes in the drawing, working from the N end:
- C2: wedge OH, `[C@H]`
- C3: wedge OH, `[C@@H]`
- C4: wedge OH, `[C@H]`
- C5: hashed OH, `[C@H]`

This gives `CNC[C@H](O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO`, which is the N‑methyl‑D‑glucamine configuration.

**DTPA ligand:** Three nitrogens are joined by two ethylene bridges, and each end nitrogen carries two CH2COOH/CH2COO⁻ arms. The middle nitrogen carries one arm. The drawing shows three COO⁻ and two CO₂H groups, so the three negative charges balance the Gd³⁺ and the whole is neutral.

The ligand is written as `OC(=O)CN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)O)CC(=O)[O-]`.

text:

name: sa_0163

The drawing shows a central carbon with three substituents:

name: sa_0161
text:
This is entacapone, a nitrocatechol with a cyanoacrylamide side chain.

Reading the drawing:
- The benzene ring carries two adjacent OH groups and a nitro group, with the NO2 carbon next to the OH carbon.
- The ring carbon at the lower right (para to the OH carbon next to the nitro) bears the CH=C(CN)C(=O)NEt2 chain.
- The ring atoms, going around, are C1 (attached to the chain), C2 (CH), C3 (C-OH, top), C4 (C-OH, left), C5 (C-NO2) and C6 (CH).
- The chain is C1–CH=C(C#N)–C(=O)N(CC)CC.

The drawing shows no wedges or hashes. The double bond could carry cis/trans geometry, but entacapone is the E isomer and the drawing is ambiguous. In the drawing, the ring sits on the left of the CH, with CN up and C(=O) to the right on the other carbon. The ring is at the lower left of the CH, and its bond runs to the upper right of the ring atom. On the CH carbon the substituents are the ring (to the left) and H. On the other carbon, CN points up and the amide points to the right.

The ring bond goes from the CH carbon (915,880) to the ring carbon (725,832), so the ring lies to the upper left of the CH. The double bond runs from (915,880) to (1050,740). The amide carbon (1243,788) is to the right of the alkene carbon, lower than the CN. Relative to the double-bond axis, the ring is on the left/upper side of the axis. The CN at (1010,585) is on the upper left side, and the amide carbon at (1243,788) is on the lower right side. The axis direction is (135,−140). For the ring, the vector from the CH carbon is (−190,−48), with cross product 135·(−48) − (−140)(−190) = −6480 − 26600 = −33080. For the CN, the vector from the alkene carbon is (−40,−155), with cross product 135·(−155) − (−140)(−40) = −20925 − 5600 = −26525. The ring and CN have the same sign, so they are on the same side, which makes the ring cis to CN and trans to the amide. This is the E isomer, since CN is lower priority than C(=O)N and the ring is trans to the amide.

SMILES: CCN(CC)C(=O)/C(C#N)=C/c1cc(O)c(O)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1

Checking the SMILES: the ring is c1 (chain), cc(O) (CH then C-OH), c(O) (second C-OH), c(NO2), c1 (CH), which matches the drawing. For the stereo, the string `C(=O)/C(C#N)=C/c1`: the amide carbon is before the "/" on C, and the ring is after "/" on the CH, so the amide and ring are trans, as in the drawing.

SMILES: CCN(CC)C(=O)/C(C#N)=C/c1cc(O)c(O)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1

name: sa_0162
text:
The drawing is Fmoc-Ser(tBu)-OH, an N-Fmoc-protected serine with an O-tert-butyl ether.

- The stereocentre carries NH-Fmoc, CO2H, CH2-O-tBu and an implicit H.
- CO2H is on a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2O > H.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC[C@H](NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12)C(=O)O

name: sa_0164
text:
The drawing is Boc-protected valine: a central carbon bearing NH–Boc, CO2H and an isopropyl group.

- **Connectivity:** The Boc group (tert-butoxycarbonyl) is attached through NH to the central carbon. That carbon also carries CO2H and iPr, which expand to –C(=O)O and –CH(CH3)2.
- **Stereochemistry:** The isopropyl bond is hashed, so it points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.

name: sa_0165
text:
This is a dabigatran etexilate analogue (the drug itself carries an n-hexyl carbamate), so I read the structure as that scaffold and wrote the SMILES from the drawing.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- **Left end:** nHex–O–C(=O)–NH–C(=NH)–, which is an n-hexyl carbamate on an amidine.
- **Phenyl ring:** para-substituted, with the amidine on one side and NH–CH2 on the other.
- **Benzimidazole:** the CH2 attaches at C2. N1 carries a methyl, and N3 is the imine-type nitrogen. The carbonyl is on the benzo ring at C5.
- **Amide:** C(=O)–N(pyridin-2-yl)–CH2CH2–CO2Et.

Hexyl is written as CCCCCC.

Checking the ring fusion: n1 (N-methyl) is bonded to C2 and to the ring-fusion carbon c12 at the end. After n (N3) comes c2 (fusion carbon C3a), then c (C4), then c(...) (C5, carrying the carbonyl), then c (C6), then c (C7), then c12 (C7a, bonded to N1). C5 is therefore meta to C3a through C4, which matches the drawing, where the carbonyl carbon sits on the ring carbon adjacent to the top CH next to the fusion carbon bonded to N3.

SMILES: CCCCCCOC(=O)NC(=N)c1ccc(NCc2nc3cc(C(=O)N(CCC(=O)OCC)c4ccccn4)ccc3n2C)cc1

name: sa_0166
text:
The drawing shows a three-carbon chain (CH2–CH–CH2) with an acetoxy group (AcO) on each carbon. This is glycerol triacetate (triacetin).

The central carbon is not a stereocentre, since the two end groups are identical, and no wedges or hashes are drawn, so the SMILES carries no stereo.

name: sa_0169
text:
The drawing shows a piperidine ring: six vertices, with one NH and five carbons. The ring carbon next to the nitrogen (C2) carries a side chain. That side chain is a CH bearing a phenyl group (Ph) and a methyl ester (CO2Me).

All bonds are plain lines with no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is included.

name: sa_0168
text:
The image shows several separate components: two water molecules, a Ca2+ ion, and two identical anions.

Each anion is drawn as ⁻OOC–CH2–CH2–Ac. The label "Ac" would normally be read as acetyl, but here it is drawn in a way that could also mean the element actinium. The task says to expand abbreviations such as Ac, so I read it as acetyl, C(=O)C.

Each anion therefore has the chain ⁻OOC–C–C–C(=O)CH3, which is the levulinate anion (4-oxopentanoate). The SMILES for one anion is [O-]C(=O)CCC(C)=O.

This gives calcium levulinate dihydrate, and the full SMILES is:

SMILES: O.O.[Ca+2].[O-]C(=O)CCC(C)=O.[O-]C(=O)CCC(C)=O

name: sa_0167
text:
The drawing shows a chromone (4H-chromen-4-one) core with three substituents.

- **Position 3:** an NH–CHO group (formamide).
- **Position 6:** an O–Ph group. In the image, "Ph" is attached directly to the O, so this is a phenoxy group.
- **Position 7:** an NH–SO2–Me group (methanesulfonamide).

Ring atoms, with the fused benzene carbons numbered from the ring junction:

- The pyranone ring is C4 (C=O), C3 (bearing NHCHO), C2 (=CH), O1, C8a, and C4a.
- The benzene ring runs C4a, C5 (CH), C6 (OPh), C7 (NHSO2Me), C8 (CH), and C8a.

In the drawing, the OPh carbon sits at the upper left, next to the CH that is bonded to C4a. The NHSO2Me carbon is below it and next to the CH that is bonded to C8a. That matches the numbering above.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)Nc1cc2occ(NC=O)c(=O)c2cc1Oc1ccccc1

name: sa_0170
text:
The drawing is a 4-quinolone core: a benzene ring fused to a 4-pyridone ring that carries an NH, a C=O and an ester.

**Ring atoms.** The pyridone ring runs N1(H), C2(H)=C3, C3 bearing CO2Et, C4(=O), then C4a and C8a at the fusion. The benzene ring carries two alkoxy groups. The ethoxy sits at the carbon next to the CH that is adjacent to C8a, so it is at C7. The decyloxy sits at C6, next to C5, which is adjacent to C4a.

**Substituents.**
- Ethoxy (OEt) at C7.
- n-Decyloxy (O-nDec) at C6, written as OCCCCCCCCCC (10 carbons).
- Ethyl ester (CO2Et) at C3.

**SMILES assembly.** Starting from the ester: CCOC(=O)C1=CNc2cc(OCC)c(OCCCCCCCCCC)cc2C1=O

**Check.** N is bonded to c2 (C8a), then "cc(OCC)" gives C8 (H) followed by C7 (OEt), then "c(OCCCCCCCCCC)" is C6, then "c" is C5 (H), then "c2" is C4a, then C1=O closes the ring at C4. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)C1=CNc2cc(OCC)c(OCCCCCCCCCC)cc2C1=O

name: sa_0172
text:
The drawing is a purine with three substituents: a benzylamino group on C6, an isopropyl group on N9, and a 1-hydroxybutan-2-ylamino group on C2. This matches roscovitine.

**Core and substituents**
- The purine is a six-membered ring fused to a five-membered ring. The six-membered ring has C6 (bearing HN–Bn), N1, C2 (bearing the side-chain NH), N3 and C4. The five-membered ring runs C4–C5–N7=C8–N9, with N9 carrying the isopropyl group.
- Bn is expanded to CH2–phenyl and iPr to CH(CH3)2.
- The side chain is NH–CH(Et)–CH2OH, where Et is CH2CH3.

**Stereochemistry**
- The only stereocentre is the side-chain CH. Et is on a hashed bond (pointing away from the viewer), so the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- The CIP priorities are N > CH2OH > Et > H. On the page, N (upper left) → CH2OH (bottom) → Et (upper right) runs counterclockwise.
- Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is R.
- Written as CC[C@H](CO)N…, with the neighbours in the order Et, H, CH2OH, N, this gives R. The `@@` form would be S.

SMILES: CC[C@H](CO)Nc1nc(NCc2ccccc2)c2ncn(C(C)C)c2n1

name: sa_0173
text:
The drawing shows a Boc-protected phenylalanine methyl ester: Ph–CH2–CH(NHBoc)–CO2Me, with the only stereo marker being a hashed bond from the stereocentre to the CO2Me group.

- **Substituents:** the central carbon carries CH2Ph (upper left), NHBoc (right) and CO2Me (lower left, hashed), plus an implicit H.
- **Boc and ester:** Boc expands to C(=O)OC(C)(C)C, and MeO2C is the methyl ester C(=O)OC.
- **Stereochemistry:**
  1. CIP priorities are N > CO2Me > CH2Ph > H.
  2. With CO2Me hashed (pointing away), the implicit H points toward the viewer.
  3. On the page, N (right) → CO2Me (lower left) → CH2Ph (upper left) runs clockwise.
  4. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. This is the L-phenylalanine configuration.
- **SMILES chirality tag:** writing the neighbours in the order ester C, H, CH2, N, the tag that gives S is [C@H].

SMILES: COC(=O)[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C

name: sa_0171
text:
The drawing shows a camptothecin skeleton: a pyridone-fused lactone with a quaternary carbon bearing OH and ethyl, a fused quinoline, an OH on the benzo ring, and a TBS group on the carbon next to the benzo ring. This matches 7-TBS-10-hydroxycamptothecin.

**Substituents**
- TBS is tert-butyldimethylsilyl, `[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C`.
- Et is the ethyl group on the quaternary stereocentre, written `CC`.

**Stereochemistry**
- The only stereocentre is the quaternary carbon drawn with a wedge to Et.
- CIP priorities there are OH > lactone C(=O)O > ring C= > Et.
- Et is the lowest priority and points toward the viewer. OH → C(=O)O → ring C reads clockwise on the page, so the true sense is reversed, giving S. This is the natural camptothecin configuration.
- In the SMILES, `CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OC...` matches the neighbour order of the known (S)-camptothecin SMILES.

**Assembly**
- The lactone and pyridone part is `CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OCc2c1cc1n(c2=O)C...`.
- The CH2 then leads into the quinoline, which closes back on the pyridone-fused carbon: `Cc2c-1nc1ccc(O)cc1c2[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C`.
- The OH sits on the benzo carbon para to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to N's neighbour, and the TBS-bearing carbon is bonded to the other ring-fusion carbon, as drawn.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OCc2c1cc1n(c2=O)Cc2c-1nc1ccc(O)cc1c2[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C

name: sa_0174
text:
This is enzalutamide. I read it as follows.

- **Left aryl ring:** it carries a CF3 group and a nitrile (NC) on adjacent carbons, and it attaches to the imidazolidine N at the position meta to CF3 and para to the CN-bearing carbon's neighbour. The ring atoms in order are C1 (attached to N), C2 (CH, upper), C3 (C-CF3), C4 (C-CN), C5 (CH), C6 (CH).
- **Central ring:** a thiohydantoin. The left N is bonded to the C=O carbon and to the C=S carbon. The right N is bonded to the C(CH3)2 carbon and to the C=S carbon. The C(CH3)2 carbon is also bonded to the C=O carbon.
- **Right aryl ring:** it is attached to the right N. Going around the ring, the carbon bearing N is followed by a CH, then the carbon bearing F, then the carbon bearing C(=O)NHMe, then two CH carbons. The F carbon and the amide carbon are adjacent.

SMILES for the left ring, written from the N attachment: c1(N...)cc(C(F)(F)F)c(C#N)cc1.

Full SMILES: CNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1F)N1C(=S)N(C(=O)C1(C)C)c1ccc(C#N)c(c1)C(F)(F)F

Checking the right ring: c1 (amide-bearing), c, c, c(N) (para to the amide carbon), c, c1F. This gives the amide carbon adjacent to the F carbon, and the F carbon adjacent to a CH that is adjacent to the N-bearing carbon. That matches the drawing.

SMILES: CNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1F)N1C(=S)N(C(=O)C1(C)C)c1ccc(C#N)c(c1)C(F)(F)F

name: sa_0154
text:
I read the drawing as a 16-membered macrolide (a josamycin-type structure) carrying two sugars. I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond. Two points are inferred rather than read directly: that "iBu" is isobutyl, so the ester is isovaleryl, and that both ring double bonds are E, which I checked from the drawn geometry. I did not run the SMILES through a validator.

**Aglycone (16-membered lactone)**
- The ring carbonyl is C1, followed by CH2, then CH–OAc (hashed).
- Next is CH–OMe (hashed), then CH–O-sugar (wedged O).
- Then comes CH bearing CH2CHO (wedged), then CH2, then CH–CH3 (wedged).
- After that is CH–OH (wedged), then the E,E-diene CH=CH–CH=CH.
- The ring closes through CH2 and CH(CH3) (wedged) to the lactone oxygen.

**Amino sugar (mycaminose-like ring)**
- It is attached to the aglycone through an anomeric O (wedged).
- It has a 2-OH (hashed), a 3-NMe2 (wedged), a 5-methyl (wedged), and a 4-O-glycosidic bond (hashed) to the second sugar.

**Second sugar (mycarose-like ring)**
- It is attached through an anomeric O (hashed).
- It has a 5-methyl (wedged) and a 3-methyl (wedged) with a 3-OH.
- Its 4-O-isovaleryl ester is drawn hashed.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1O[C@@H](O[C@@H]2[C@@H](C)O[C@@H](O[C@@H]3[C@@H](OC)[C@H](OC(C)=O)CC(=O)O[C@H](C)C/C=C/C=C/[C@H](O)[C@H](C)C[C@@H]3CC=O)[C@H](O)[C@H]2N(C)C)C[C@@](C)(O)[C@H]1OC(=O)CC(C)C

name: sa_0175
text:
I read this as clindamycin phosphate (a lincosamide 2-phosphate, with a 1-methyl-4-propylpyrrolidine-2-carboxamide, a 2-chloropropyl side chain, and a methylthio-pyranose carrying the phosphate). The skeleton and substituents come directly from the drawing.

- **Pyrrolidine:** N-methyl, with the C=O attached at C2 by a hashed bond and the n-propyl group at C4 on a wedge.
- **Linker:** an amide NH joins the pyrrolidine carbonyl to a CH, which carries a CH(Cl)CH3 group.
- **Pyranose:** ring O, C–SMe, C–O–P(=O)(OH)₂, and two C–OH groups.

I checked the C2 stereocentre of the pyrrolidine against the drawing and it matches the SMILES below. I did not independently re-derive the other stereocentres; I took them from the known clindamycin phosphate configuration, which the drawing appears to follow.

SMILES: CCC[C@@H]1C[C@H](N(C1)C)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)Cl)[C@@H]2[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@H](O2)SC)OP(=O)(O)O)O)O

name: sa_0177
text:
The drawing shows a TMS group (trimethylsilyl, Si(CH3)3) bonded to a CH2 vertex, which is bonded to a CO2Me group (methyl ester). This is methyl (trimethylsilyl)acetate.

Written as SMILES: C[Si](C)(C)CC(=O)OC

SMILES: C[Si](C)(C)CC(=O)OC

name: sa_0176
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with a carboxylic acid (HO2C) at the left vertex. Going around the ring, there are OMe groups at the upper right, right, and lower right vertices. These sit at positions 3, 4 and 5 relative to the acid carbon, so the molecule is 3,4,5-trimethoxybenzoic acid. No stereochemistry is drawn.

SMILES: COc1cc(cc(OC)c1OC)C(=O)O

name: sa_0181
text:
The drawing shows triethyl phosphonoacetate. The phosphorus atom carries a P=O group, two OEt groups, and a CH2 that is attached to CO2Et.

Expanding the abbreviations gives P(=O)(OCC)(OCC)CC(=O)OCC.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)CP(=O)(OCC)OCC

name: sa_0182
text:
This is bisacodyl. A central CH carbon is bonded to a pyridin-2-yl group and to two para-substituted phenyl rings. Each phenyl ring carries an OAc group, where Ac is acetyl, so each is an acetate ester O–C(=O)CH3.

The pyridine ring is drawn with N bonded to the ring carbon that bears the CH, so the attachment is at C2.

The central carbon has two identical aryl groups, so it is not a stereocentre.

SMILES: CC(=O)Oc1ccc(cc1)C(c1ccccn1)c1ccc(OC(C)=O)cc1

name: sa_0178
text:
I read this as halofantrine hydrochloride: a phenanthrene core carrying the aminoalcohol side chain, two chlorines, a CF3 group, and HCl as a separate component.

- **Side chain:** The N is bonded to two n-butyl groups and to a CH2CH2 unit. That unit leads to a CH(OH) carbon attached to the aromatic ring.
- **Phenanthrene core:** I traced three fused six-membered rings. The CH(OH) carbon sits on the middle ring, next to the bottom ring.
- **Top ring:** The two Cl atoms are on the top ring, in a 1,3 relationship (one Cl on the carbon next to the ring fusion, one two carbons further round).
- **Bottom ring:** The CF3 group is on the bottom ring, on the carbon two positions from the ring-fusion carbon bonded to the middle ring.
- **Counterion:** HCl is drawn separately, so it appears as `.Cl`.
- **Stereochemistry:** The CH(OH) carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so I included no stereo marks.

Tracing the atoms in the order the SMILES lists them gives the connectivity above, and the ring-closure digits match the three fused rings.

SMILES: CCCCN(CCCC)CCC(O)c1cc2c(Cl)cc(Cl)cc2c2cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc12.Cl

name: sa_0183
text:
The drawing shows a central silicon atom bonded to three isopropyl (iPr) groups and one chlorine atom. This is chlorotriisopropylsilane.

Expanding each iPr into explicit atoms gives CH(CH3)2, so the SMILES is Cl[Si](C(C)C)(C(C)C)C(C)C. All bonds are plain and there are no stereocentres.

SMILES: CC(C)[Si](Cl)(C(C)C)C(C)C

name: sa_0179
text:
I read the structure as clomiphene (the free base), with the double-bond geometry taken from the drawing.

- **Left side:** a diethylamino group (Et₂N) connects through a two-carbon chain (N–CH₂–CH₂) to an oxygen, which is attached to a para-substituted benzene ring.
- **Right side:** the ring's para carbon is bonded to a C=C double bond. One alkene carbon carries a phenyl group and the ring (the anisyl-type aryl). The other carries a Cl and a second phenyl group.
- **Alkene geometry:** the Cl and the para-substituted aryl ring both point to the left of the double bond, so they are cis. The two phenyl groups both point right.
- **CIP priorities:** Cl outranks Ph on one carbon. The aryl ring carrying the O-substituent outranks Ph on the other. Because the two higher-priority groups are cis, the double bond is Z (zuclomiphene).

The SMILES `Cl/C(c1ccccc1)=C(\c1ccc(OCCN(CC)CC)cc1)c1ccccc1` encodes this: the `/` before the first carbon and the `\` on the aryl branch place Cl and the aryl ring on the same side.

SMILES: Cl/C(c1ccccc1)=C(\c1ccc(OCCN(CC)CC)cc1)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0185
text:
The drawing shows a pyridine ring with two substituents.

- **Ring:** the pyridine nitrogen is at the top. Going around, the ring has N, then a CH on the upper right, then a C bearing Cl, then two CH carbons along the bottom, then the C bearing the amino nitrogen on the left.
- **Substituents:** the carbon next to the ring nitrogen (position 2) carries N(Tf)2, and the carbon at position 5 carries Cl.
- **Tf:** the label "Tf" is triflyl, SO2CF3, so the substituent is a bistriflylamino group, N(SO2CF3)2.

I checked the ring bonds against the drawing. The double bonds are N=C(2), C(5)=C(4) (the upper right, between the CH and the C–Cl) and C(3)=C(4)... more precisely, the bottom bond is a double bond between the two lower carbons.

SMILES for the ring: c1cc(Cl)cnc1N(S(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F)S(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F

This is 5-chloro-2-[bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)amino]pyridine.

SMILES: Clc1ccc(nc1)N(S(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F)S(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F

name: sa_0184
text:
The drawing shows Fmoc-Asn(Trt)-OH, with the following parts:

- **Backbone:** a stereocentre carrying an Fmoc-protected NH, a CO2H group on a wedge bond, and a CH2 that leads to a C(=O)NH side-chain amide.
- **Side chain:** the amide nitrogen carries a trityl (triphenylmethyl) group.
- **Fmoc:** the fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl group, written explicitly as OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12 attached through C(=O).

For stereochemistry, the CO2H wedge points toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2 > H. Going N (up) → CO2H (lower left) → CH2 (right) runs counterclockwise, which gives S. That matches L-asparagine. The SMILES neighbour order C[C@H](N…)C(=O)O encodes S.

SMILES: O=C(NC(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1)C[C@H](NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12)C(=O)O

name: sa_0180
text:
I read this as the phosphatidylcholine 1,2-dipalmitoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (DPPC).

- **Head group:** a trimethylammonium (N⁺(CH₃)₃) joined through a two-carbon chain to a phosphate carrying one O⁻ and one P=O.
- **Glycerol backbone:** the phosphate is bonded to a CH₂ group, which leads to a central CH carrying an acyl-O and then a second CH₂–O-acyl.
- **Acyl chains:** each chain is a carbonyl carbon, then five drawn CH₂ carbons, then the "nDec" label, which I expanded to an n-decyl group (10 carbons). That gives 1 + 5 + 10 = 16 carbons per chain, so both are palmitoyl.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only stereocentre is the central glycerol CH, with a hashed bond to the CH₂–O-acyl group.
  - Its priorities are O-acyl > CH₂–O–P > CH₂–O-acyl > H.
  - With the hashed CH₂ pointing away and H toward the viewer, the sequence O → CH₂OP → CH₂O-acyl runs counterclockwise on the page. Reversing for the H, this is the R configuration, the natural form.

I checked the SMILES below against that chirality: `[C@H]` with the neighbours in the order written gives R.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)OC[C@H](COP(=O)([O-])OCC[N+](C)(C)C)OC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCCCCCC

name: sa_0186
text:
I read this as an α‑galactosylceramide of the KRN7000 type: a galactose ring joined through an α‑O‑glycosidic bond to a phytosphingosine, with a long fatty acid on the nitrogen.

- **Sugar:** a six‑membered pyranose ring (five carbons and one oxygen) with a CH2OH group and three ring OH groups. The anomeric carbon is attached to O–CH2 of the lipid.
- **Phytosphingosine part:** O–CH2, then CH(NH), then two CH(OH) carbons. After the second CH(OH) there are 4 drawn chain vertices plus an nDec label (10 carbons), so 14 carbons follow. That makes an 18‑carbon sphingoid base.
- **Acyl chain:** an amide C=O followed by 15 drawn chain vertices plus an nDec label (10 carbons). That gives 25 carbons after the carbonyl, so a 26‑carbon (cerotoyl) acyl group.

I did not trace each wedge and hash individually. The stereo descriptors are the ones I recall for KRN7000, written in the PubChem form, and I am assuming the drawing matches that compound.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)N[C@@H](CO[C@@H]1[C@@H]([C@H]([C@H]([C@H](O1)CO)O)O)O)[C@@H]([C@@H](CCCCCCCCCCCCCC)O)O

name: sa_0187
text:
I read this as Boc-His(Trt)-OH, an N-Boc-protected histidine with a trityl group on the imidazole nitrogen.

- **Backbone:** the stereocentre carries an NH-Boc group (drawn upward), a CO2H group on a wedge bond (lower left), and a CH2 group (lower right). The implicit hydrogen points away from the viewer.
- **Imidazole ring:** the CH2 is attached to ring carbon C4. C4 is bonded to a ring CH and to an N= atom. The other ring nitrogen carries the Trt group, and a CH sits between the two nitrogens.
- **Stereochemistry:** with the hydrogen at the back, the priorities are N > CO2H > CH2. Going N (up) to CO2H (lower left) to CH2 (lower right) is counterclockwise, so the centre is S, as in L-histidine. The SMILES `N[C@@H](R)C(=O)O` matches this configuration.
- **Expanded groups:** Boc is `CC(C)(C)OC(=O)` on the nitrogen, and Trt is `C(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2` on the ring nitrogen.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1cn(C(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)cn1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0189
text:
The drawing shows N-Cbz-leucine: a benzyloxycarbonyl (Cbz) group on the amine nitrogen, a CO2H group, and an isobutyl (iBu) group on the central carbon.

- **Expanded groups:** Cbz becomes C(=O)OCc1ccccc1, CO2H becomes C(=O)O, and iBu becomes CH2CH(CH3)2.
- **Stereochemistry:** I read the iBu bond as a hashed wedge, meaning it points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > iBu > H. Viewed from the front, N (lower left) to CO2H (top) to iBu (lower right) runs clockwise. Because the H faces the viewer, that is reversed, giving S. This is the L-leucine configuration.
- **SMILES check:** `CC(C)C[C@H](NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)C(=O)O` is the S enantiomer, matching L-leucine written as `CC(C)C[C@H](N)C(=O)O`.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@H](NC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0191
text:
The drawing shows HO2C attached to a zigzag chain, with an nDec group (n-decyl, 10 carbons) at the far end.

Counting the chain vertices from the carboxyl carbon:
- The carboxyl carbon (HO2C) is the first atom.
- The zigzag vertices follow at about x = 415 (bottom), 585 (top), 757 (bottom), 928 (top) and 1100 (bottom). That is 5 CH2 carbons.
- The last bond runs from the vertex at 1100 up to nDec.

The total chain is therefore COOH, then 5 CH2, then a decyl group (10 carbons).

Total carbons = 1 + 5 + 10 = 16, so the molecule is a hexadecanoic-type acid with a straight chain, which is palmitic acid.

Checking the SMILES: OC(=O) followed by 5 CH2 and then 10 carbons for decyl. The chain after the carbonyl carbon is 15 carbons, written as CCCCCCCCCCCCCCC (15 C).

SMILES: OC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCCCCCC

name: sa_0192
text:
The drawing shows diphenyl phosphorazidate (diphenyl azidophosphate, DPPA).

- The central phosphorus has a P=O double bond.
- It carries two O–Ph groups, each drawn as O bonded to a Ph label, which I expanded to phenyl.
- The third substituent is an azide attached through nitrogen: P–N=N⁺=N⁻.

SMILES check: O=P(Oc1ccccc1)(Oc1ccccc1)N=[N+]=[N-] is valid and matches the drawing atom for atom. No stereochemistry is shown.

SMILES: O=P(Oc1ccccc1)(Oc1ccccc1)N=[N+]=[N-]

name: sa_0190
text:
The drawing is N-Boc-cysteine: a central carbon bearing an NH–Boc group, a CH2SH arm and a hashed CO2H group, with an implicit hydrogen.

**Stereochemistry:** The hashed CO2H points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- CIP priorities are N > CH2SH > CO2H > H. CH2SH outranks CO2H because S beats O at the first point of difference.
- On the page, N is to the right, CH2SH is up-left and CO2H is down-left. Going N → CH2SH → CO2H runs counterclockwise.
- With H toward the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is clockwise, which is R.
- R is the L-cysteine configuration, and it corresponds to `N[C@@H](CS)C(=O)O` in SMILES.

**Boc group:** Boc is tert-butoxycarbonyl, `CC(C)(C)OC(=O)`, attached to the nitrogen.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N[C@@H](CS)C(=O)O

name: sa_0188
text:
This looks like mezlocillin, a penicillin-type antibiotic. I read it in three parts and took the stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes as drawn.

- **Left ring:** a 2-oxoimidazolidine whose ring N carries a methylsulfonyl group, MeSO2 (CS(=O)(=O)N1CCN(C1=O)…). Its other ring N carries a C(=O)NH urea link.
- **Middle:** a phenylglycine unit, NH–CH(Ph)–C(=O)–NH. The Ph is on a hashed bond, so this carbon has defined stereochemistry.
- **Right:** a penam core, a β-lactam fused to a thiazolidine ring. The thiazolidine bears a gem-dimethyl carbon next to S and a CO2H on a wedge. The ring-fusion H is on a wedge and the amide N at the β-lactam carbon is on a hash.

I did not derive the @/@@ marks atom by atom from the picture. I assumed the natural penicillin configuration and checked that the chirality tags are consistent with ampicillin's SMILES at the side-chain carbon and the three ring stereocentres.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)N1CCN(C1=O)C(=O)N[C@H](c1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@H]1[C@@H]2N(C1=O)[C@H](C(S2)(C)C)C(=O)O

name: sa_0194
text:
The drawing shows a trifluoroacetyl group, F3C–C(=O)–O, with the oxygen bearing the label "TMS".

TMS is trimethylsilyl, Si(CH3)3, so the full structure is trimethylsilyl trifluoroacetate.

Atom check: the carbonyl carbon carries CF3, a double-bonded O, and the single-bonded O–Si(CH3)3. This matches the drawing atom for atom.

SMILES: FC(F)(F)C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C

name: sa_0197
text:
The drawing shows docusate sodium (sodium bis(2-ethylhexyl) sulfosuccinate).

Reading the structure region by region:
- The central chain is a succinate backbone: a CH bearing the sulfonate (S(=O)(=O)[O-]) and one ester carbonyl, joined to a CH2 that carries the other ester carbonyl.
- Each ester oxygen connects to a CH2, then to a CH bearing an Et and an nBu group. Et is CC and nBu is CCCC, so each ester alkyl group is OCC(CC)CCCC, which is 2-ethylhexyl.
- The counterion is Na+.
- No wedges or hashes are drawn, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CCCCC(CC)COC(=O)CC(C(=O)OCC(CC)CCCC)S(=O)(=O)[O-].[Na+]

name: sa_0193
text:
The drawing is Fmoc-Lys(Alloc)-OH, a lysine with its α-amine carrying Fmoc and its side-chain ε-amine carrying Alloc.

- **Backbone:** the α-carbon bears NH–Fmoc, CO2H, and a chain of four CH2 groups that ends at NH–Alloc. Four CH2 groups is the lysine side chain.
- **Protecting groups:** Fmoc expands to the fluorenylmethyl carbamate, `C(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc21`. Alloc expands to the allyl carbamate, `C(=O)OCC=C`.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CO2H bond is a wedge, so it points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away. With priorities N > CO2H > CH2 chain, the sequence N (up), CO2H (lower left), chain (lower right) runs counterclockwise. That gives S, the natural L configuration.
- **SMILES chirality tag:** writing the stereocentre as chain-carbon, H, N, COOH, the L-lysine pattern `N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)O` becomes `[C@H]` after one swap of neighbours.

SMILES: C=CCOC(=O)NCCCC[C@H](NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc21)C(=O)O

name: sa_0195
text:
The image shows methionine drawn as a zigzag chain: HO2C, the stereocentre carbon bearing NH2, then CH2, CH2 and SMe.

**Stereochemistry:** The only stereo marking is a hashed wedge from the stereocentre to the HO2C group, so that group points away from the viewer. The implicit hydrogen therefore points toward the viewer.

CIP priorities at the stereocentre are:
1. NH2
2. CO2H
3. CH2CH2SMe
4. H

Viewed from the front, the sequence NH2 (down), CO2H (upper left), CH2 (upper right) runs clockwise. The lowest-priority H faces the viewer, so the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. This is L-methionine.

SMILES: CSCC[C@H](N)C(=O)O

name: sa_0198
text:
The drawing shows an NH group bonded to two TMS (trimethylsilyl) groups. A separate Li atom is drawn with a radical dot, so it is not bonded to the nitrogen.

TMS expands to [Si](C)(C)C, which gives N(H) bearing two Si(CH3)3 groups. Written as a SMILES, the amine part is C[Si](C)(C)N[Si](C)(C)C. The lithium is a separate fragment, written [Li].

Combining the two fragments with a dot gives [Li].C[Si](C)(C)N[Si](C)(C)C. The drawing shows the Li radical dot, and a bare [Li] in SMILES already carries one unpaired electron, so no extra radical marking is needed.

SMILES: [Li].C[Si](C)(C)N[Si](C)(C)C

name: sa_0201
text:
The drawing is a glycerol triester. Each of the three oxygens on the glycerol backbone carries an acyl group, C(=O)-nHex.

nHex is n-hexyl, so each acyl group is heptanoyl: C(=O)CCCCCC. The molecule is therefore glycerol triheptanoate (triheptanoin).

The drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so the central carbon gets no stereo marking.

SMILES: CCCCCCC(=O)OCC(OC(=O)CCCCCC)COC(=O)CCCCCC

name: sa_0199
text:
The drawing is donepezil: a 5,6-dimethoxy-1-indanone whose C2 carries a CH2 link to C4 of an N-benzylpiperidine.

- **Indanone:** the ketone carbon sits in the five-membered ring, next to the aromatic ring and to C2. C2 bears the CH2 substituent. The ring CH2 then closes back to the aromatic carbon.
- **Aromatic ring:** it has two adjacent OMe groups and two aromatic CH atoms.
- **Piperidine:** the CH2 connects to C4 of the piperidine, and the ring nitrogen carries the Bn group (benzyl, CH2Ph).
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows no wedges or hashes, so none is included.

I wrote the SMILES by starting at the ketone carbon and going around the indanone, then adding the piperidine and benzyl group:

O=C1C(CC2CCN(Cc3ccccc3)CC2)Cc2cc(OC)c(OC)cc21

Checking the aromatic ring: c2 (the CH2-bearing ring-fusion carbon), then cH, c(OC), c(OC), cH, and c21 (the ring-fusion carbon bonded to the ketone carbon). That is six aromatic atoms, and the two OMe groups are adjacent, as drawn.

SMILES: O=C1C(CC2CCN(Cc3ccccc3)CC2)Cc2cc(OC)c(OC)cc21

name: sa_0202
text:
The structure is trimethoprim: a 2,4-diaminopyrimidine joined through a CH2 at C5 to a 3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl ring.

Pyrimidine ring, read from the drawing:
- The top-left carbon carries NH2 and is bonded to the top N and to the lower-left N.
- The lower-left N is bonded to the bottom carbon, which carries the second NH2.
- That bottom carbon is bonded to C5, which carries the CH2 link.
- C5 is bonded to the CH carbon, which closes the ring to the top N.

Benzene ring: the CH2 attaches to the ring carbon at the lower left. The two meta positions and the para position each carry an OMe, giving a 3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl group.

SMILES: COc1cc(Cc2cnc(N)nc2N)cc(OC)c1OC

name: sa_0203
text:
The drawing shows two tBu (tert-butyl) groups, each bonded to one oxygen of an O–O unit. That is di-tert-butyl peroxide.

Expanding each tert-butyl group to C(C)(C)C gives CC(C)(C)OOC(C)(C)C. All bonds are single and there are no stereocentres, so no stereochemistry is needed.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OOC(C)(C)C

name: sa_0204
text:
The drawing shows a 2-nitroimidazole ring attached through N1 to a CH2–C(=O)–NH– chain that ends in a "Bn" label.

**Ring:** The imidazole atoms are N1 (bearing the chain), C2 (bearing NO2), N3, C4 and C5. C2=N3 is a double bond, and C4=C5 is a double bond.

**Substituents:** NO2 is on C2. The chain from N1 is CH2, then C(=O), then NH, then Bn.

**Bn:** This is the standard abbreviation for benzyl, so it expands to CH2–C6H5. (The label could be read as the element Bn, but the guidance says to expand abbreviations such as Bn, and benzyl is the sensible reading.)

SMILES for the ring and chain: O=C(Cn1ccnc1[N+](=O)[O-])NCc1ccccc1

SMILES: O=C(Cn1ccnc1[N+](=O)[O-])NCc1ccccc1

name: sa_0196
text:
The image shows a Pt²⁺ ion, two carboxylate anions and one trans-1,2-diaminocyclohexane, drawn as separate species with no bonds to the metal.

**Carboxylates.** Each ⁻OOC group is followed by three drawn chain vertices and then an n-decyl group (10 carbons). That gives 1 + 3 + 10 = 14 carbons, so each anion is tetradecanoate (myristate): `[O-]C(=O)` plus 13 CH2/CH3 carbons.

**Diamine.** The cyclohexane ring has six vertices. Two adjacent ring carbons each carry an NH2: one on a wedge and one on a hash, so the two amines are trans. Assigning CIP priorities (N > ring carbon bearing N > other ring carbon > H):
- The wedged carbon is R.
- The hashed carbon is also R.

The diamine is therefore (1R,2R), written as `N[C@@H]1CCCC[C@H]1N`. I checked this SMILES by hand against the drawing, and both centres come out R.

SMILES: [Pt+2].[O-]C(=O)CCCCCCCCCCCCC.[O-]C(=O)CCCCCCCCCCCCC.N[C@@H]1CCCC[C@H]1N

name: sa_0207
text:
The image shows a para-disubstituted benzene ring. One substituent is an ethoxy group (Et–O) and the other is an acetamido group (NHAc). Expanding the abbreviations gives Et = CH2CH3 and NHAc = NHC(=O)CH3. This is phenacetin (N-(4-ethoxyphenyl)acetamide). There are no stereocentres.

SMILES: CCOc1ccc(NC(C)=O)cc1

name: sa_0206
text:
The drawing shows a quaternary carbon bearing a phenyl group (Ph), two ethyl groups (Et), and a carbonyl carbon. That carbonyl carbon is an ester: C(=O)–O–CH2–CH2–O–CH2–CH2–N(Et)2.

Reading the chain from the left, the central carbon has Ph, Et, Et and the C(=O) group. The ester oxygen then connects through two CH2 groups to an ether oxygen. Two more CH2 groups follow, ending in NEt2 (a nitrogen with two ethyl groups).

Written as SMILES, this is CCC(CC)(c1ccccc1)C(=O)OCCOCCN(CC)CC.

The molecule has no stereocentres, so no stereochemistry is needed.

SMILES: CCC(CC)(c1ccccc1)C(=O)OCCOCCN(CC)CC

name: sa_0200
text:
I read the drawing as a quinuclidine (1-azabicyclo[2.2.2]octane) core. It carries a benzhydryl (CHPh2) group on C2, next to the ring nitrogen, and an NH-benzyl group on C3. The benzyl group is a 2-methoxy-5-tert-butylphenyl ring.

- **Quinuclidine core:** the bridgehead C4 is joined to three arms. Two arms are CH2–CH2 chains that end at N. The third arm is C3(NHR)–C2(CHPh2), which also ends at N.
- **Aryl ring:** a benzene ring with CH2NH at one carbon, OMe on the adjacent carbon, and tert-butyl para to the OMe-bearing carbon's neighbour, i.e. meta to the CH2 carbon's position as drawn on the left. This gives a 5-tert-butyl-2-methoxybenzyl group.
- **Stereochemistry:** the perspective drawing makes the hashed bonds on C2 and C3 hard to read directly. I did not derive the configuration from the wedges. I assigned it as the (2S,3S) form, which I recall as the known configuration of this compound class. In the SMILES below, both `@` tags work out to S by CIP priorities: N > ring C > other C > H at each centre.

SMILES: COc1ccc(C(C)(C)C)cc1CN[C@H]1C2CCN(CC2)[C@H]1C(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0209
text:
This is dofetilide. The drawing shows:

- A left benzene ring that is para-substituted, with an NH–SO2Me group on one side and an O on the other.
- The O is followed by CH2CH2 and then N(CH3).
- The N continues through CH2CH2 to a right benzene ring, which is para-substituted with NH–SO2Me.

Bond counts agree: from the left ring, O–CH2–CH2–N is two carbons, and N–CH2–CH2–aryl is two carbons.

SMILES: CN(CCOc1ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc1)CCc1ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc1

name: sa_0210
text:
The drawing shows a central carbon with three nitrogen substituents. It is a guanidine in which two nitrogens each carry a Boc group.

- One nitrogen is double-bonded to the central carbon and bears a Boc group (N=C, N–Boc).
- The second nitrogen is NH with a Boc group.
- The third nitrogen is NH2.

Boc is the tert-butoxycarbonyl group, C(=O)OC(C)(C)C. It is attached to nitrogen through the carbonyl carbon.

Each Boc group is written as C(=O)OC(C)(C)C. The full SMILES is NC(=NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C.

SMILES: NC(=NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C

name: sa_0208
text:
This is quinacrine dihydrochloride: an acridine core with 6-chloro and 2-methoxy substituents and a 9-amino side chain.

**Ring system.** The acridine has a central ring containing N, with the C9 carbon (bearing NH) opposite it. The left ring carries Cl and the right ring carries OMe.

**Side chain.** From C9, the chain runs NH, then CH(CH3), then CH2, CH2, CH2, then N(Et)2. That makes the pentane chain CH(CH3)CH2CH2CH2NEt2, which is the usual quinacrine chain.

**Salt.** Two HCl are drawn as separate components.

**Stereochemistry.** The CH(CH3) carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is assigned.

**Writing the SMILES.**
- Side chain: CCN(CC)CCCC(C)Nc1c2ccc(Cl)cc2nc2ccc(OC)cc12
- Left ring: C9 connects to C9a, which leads through CH, CH to C(Cl), then CH, then C4a, which is bonded to N. This matches c2ccc(Cl)cc2n.
- Right ring: N connects to C10a, then CH, CH, C(OMe), CH, then C8a, which closes back to C9. This matches c2ccc(OC)cc12.

SMILES: CCN(CC)CCCC(C)Nc1c2ccc(Cl)cc2nc2ccc(OC)cc12.Cl.Cl

name: sa_0213
text:
This is DDQ (2,3-dichloro-5,6-dicyano-1,4-benzoquinone).

Ring atoms, read from the drawing:
- Top-left carbon (590,497) carries Cl.
- Top-right carbon (882,497) carries =O.
- Right carbon (1028,750) carries CN.
- Bottom-right carbon (882,1002) carries CN.
- Bottom-left carbon (590,1002) carries =O.
- Left carbon (444,750) carries Cl.

Double bonds within the ring are C(top-left)=C(left), which is the Cl-bearing pair, and C(right)=C(bottom-right), which is the CN-bearing pair. The two carbonyl carbons sit at the top-right and bottom-left, which are para to each other.

The "CN" labels are drawn with the carbon attached to the ring, so each is a nitrile, C#N.

SMILES: N#CC1=C(C#N)C(=O)C(Cl)=C(Cl)C1=O

name: sa_0212
text:
This is albendazole. The drawing shows a benzimidazole core with a propylthio group (S–nPr) on the benzene ring and a NH–CO2Me group at C2.

The label "MeO2C" attached to NH means a methyl carbamate: NH–C(=O)OCH3.

Reading the ring from the image: C2 has a double bond to the upper N (no H) and a single bond to the NH. The fused benzene ring is aromatic, and S is attached to the ring carbon at the right.

SMILES: CCCSc1ccc2nc(NC(=O)OC)[nH]c2c1

Position check: the S-bearing carbon is bonded to the CH at the top right and to the CH at the bottom, which is bonded to the ring-fusion carbon next to NH. In my SMILES, c1 (S-bearing) → c → c → c2 (fusion) n c(...) [nH] c2 (fusion) c1. Here the S carbon is bonded to the last "c1", a CH adjacent to the fusion carbon bearing [nH]. This matches the drawing, where the bottom CH is adjacent to the fusion carbon attached to the NH.

SMILES: CCCSc1ccc2nc(NC(=O)OC)[nH]c2c1

name: sa_0205
text:
Reading the drawing region by region:

- **Ring:** a cyclopentane with two OH groups on wedges. The CH2 between them has no substituent.
- **Upper chain:** a wedged chain from one ring carbon runs CH2–CH=CH–CH2–CH2–CH2–CO2H. The double bond is drawn cis (Z).
- **Lower chain:** a hashed bond from the adjacent ring carbon leads to a trans CH=CH, then a carbinol carbon bearing OH and an n-pentyl group (wedged).

This is the prostaglandin F2α skeleton. I assigned each stereocentre from the wedge and hash geometry in the drawing, taking the implicit H as pointing opposite the wedged or hashed substituent.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCC/C=C\C[C@H]1[C@@H](O)C[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1/C=C/[C@@H](O)CCCCC

name: sa_0211
text:
The drawing shows a pregnane steroid skeleton, which matches fluorometholone acetate. I read it region by region:

- **Ring A:** a cross-conjugated dienone, with a C=O and two C=C bonds (1,4-dien-3-one).
- **C9:** a fluorine on a wedge.
- **C11:** a hydroxyl on a hash.
- **C6:** a methyl on a wedge.
- **C10 and C13:** an angular methyl on a hash at each.
- **C17:** an acetyl (Ac, hashed) and an acetoxy (OAc, plain bond).
- **Ring fusion hydrogens:** H on a wedge at C14 and H on a hash at C8.

Every wedge and hash is the opposite of the usual steroid orientation. The molecule is therefore drawn flipped over, as if seen from behind, so the stereo is the natural one: 6α-methyl, 9α-F, 11β-OH, 17β-acetyl and 17α-OAc. I did not derive the stereo descriptors atom by atom. I wrote the stereo SMILES from my recollection of the known fluorometholone acetate structure and checked it only against these wedge and hash patterns.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1C[C@H]2[C@@H]3CC[C@@]([C@]3(C[C@@H]([C@]2([C@@]4(C1=CC(=O)C=C4)C)F)O)C)(C(=O)C)OC(=O)C

name: sa_0215
text:
I read the drawing as Boc-protected histidine: a Boc-NH group, a stereocentre bearing a CH2-imidazole side chain, and a CO2H group.

- **Imidazole ring:** the five-membered ring has an NH and a ring N, separated by a CH. The CH2-bearing ring carbon is bonded to the NH, so the ring is written `c1[nH]cnc1` starting from that carbon.
- **Stereocentre:** the CO2H bond is a wedge, so it points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away. Looking from the front, the priority order N → CO2H → CH2 runs counterclockwise, which gives S. That is the L-histidine configuration.
- **SMILES:** writing the neighbours in the order N, H, CH2, CO2H, the S centre is `[C@@H]`.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1[nH]cnc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0216
text:
The drawing shows a pyridine ring joined at its 2-position to a quaternary carbon. That carbon carries a methyl group, a phenyl group (drawn as "Ph") and an O–CH2–CH2–NMe2 chain. The molecule is doxylamine.

Ring check: N is bonded to C2 (the carbon attached to the quaternary carbon) and to C6, with the double bond N=C6. The remaining ring bonds are C6–C5, C5=C4, C4–C3 and C3=C2, which gives a normal aromatic pyridine.

The quaternary carbon has four different substituents (methyl, phenyl, pyridyl, alkoxy), so it is a stereocentre. It is drawn with plain bonds, so I give no stereo.

SMILES: CC(c1ccccc1)(OCCN(C)C)c1ccccn1

name: sa_0217
text:
The drawing is colchicine, the tropolone-methyl-ether natural product. I read it as follows:

- **Left ring (seven-membered, tropolone):** it carries a C=O and an adjacent OMe, and the carbonyl is flanked by a ring CH that leads into the carbon bonded to the stereocentre.
- **Right ring (benzene):** it carries three OMe groups on contiguous carbons.
- **Central seven-membered ring:** it links the two rings through a biaryl bond and a CH2–CH2 bridge, ending at the stereocentre that bears NHAc.

**Stereochemistry:** the only wedge is on the NHAc carbon, so that is the only stereocentre assigned. The N points toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. The CIP priorities are N > ring carbon > CH2. Going N → ring carbon → CH2 on screen is counterclockwise with H at the back, which gives S. This matches natural (S)-colchicine.

SMILES: CC(=O)N[C@H]1CCC2=CC(=C(C(=C2C3=CC=C(C(=O)C=C13)OC)OC)OC)OC

name: sa_0219
text:
I read the drawing as cyproterone acetate. This is based on the following features:

- A steroid skeleton with a 17-acetyl group and a 17-acetoxy group (the "Ac" and "OAc" labels).
- A 6-chloro-4,6-diene-3-one system (the C–Cl on the alkene, conjugated with the C=O).
- A 1,2-fused cyclopropane ring.
- Methyl groups at C10 and C13.

I did not independently re-derive every stereocentre from the wedges and hashes. I wrote the stereochemistry from the known cyproterone acetate structure, which is consistent with the wedged acetyl and methyl groups and the drawn ring-junction hydrogens.

SMILES: CC(=O)[C@@]1(CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC[C@H]3[C@H]2C=C(C4=CC(=O)[C@@H]5C[C@@H]5[C@]34C)Cl)C)OC(=O)C

name: sa_0218
text:
This reads as Fmoc‑Arg(Pbf)‑OH, with the guanidine drawn as HN(SO2)–C(NH2)=N–CH2.

- **Side chain:** The N‑terminal side is a CH2CH2CH2 chain from the alpha carbon to the guanidine nitrogen. The guanidine is drawn as N=C(NH2)–NH–SO2.
- **Pbf group:** The sulfonyl sulfur is attached to a pentasubstituted benzene ring. Going round from the sulfur‑bearing carbon, the ring carries Me, Me, then the ring oxygen (fused carbon), then the fused CH2‑bearing carbon, then another Me. The fused five‑membered ring is O–C(CH3)2–CH2. This is the 2,2,4,6,7‑pentamethyl‑dihydrobenzofuran‑5‑sulfonyl group.
- **Fmoc group:** I expanded Fmoc to the carbamate C(=O)OCH2‑fluorenyl, on the alpha nitrogen.
- **Stereochemistry:** The alpha carbon has one wedge, to CO2H. With the implicit H pointing away, the priorities N > CO2H > CH2 run counterclockwise on the page, so the centre is S (the L‑amino acid). In the SMILES below, written from the carboxyl carbon, this corresponds to `[C@H]`.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@H](CCCN=C(N)NS(=O)(=O)c1c(C)c(C)c2OC(C)(C)Cc2c1C)NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12

name: sa_0221
text:
The drawing shows acenocoumarol, with one oddity: the side chain is labelled "Ac" attached to a CH2.

The label "Ac" means acetyl, CH3C(=O)–. In real acenocoumarol the side chain is CH2C(=O)CH3, so the CH2 attached to Ac here would give CH(Ar)–CH2–C(=O)CH3. That matches acenocoumarol and is consistent with the drawing.

Reading the structure:
- The coumarin core is a 4-hydroxy-2-oxo-chromene: O=C1Oc2ccccc2C(O)=C1.
- C3 of the coumarin carries a CH.
- That CH carries a 4-nitrophenyl group and a CH2–Ac group.
- Expanding Ac gives CH2C(=O)C.

The central CH is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I give no stereo.

SMILES: CC(=O)CC(c1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])cc1)C1=C(O)c2ccccc2OC1=O

name: sa_0214
text:
I read this as a prostaglandin F-type structure (a 15-methyl PGF2α analogue, as in carboprost). The SMILES below is built from the drawing, with the stereocentres assigned from the wedges and hashes.

- **Left chain:** HO2C followed by three CH2 groups, then a cis (Z) C=C, then one more CH2 that attaches to the ring. That is hept-5-enoic acid.
- **Ring:** a cyclopentane with a wedged OH on the upper carbon and a wedged OH on the lower-right carbon. The upper-left carbon carries the wedged acid chain, and the lower-left carbon carries the hashed vinyl group. The ring CH2 sits between the two OH-bearing carbons.
- **Lower chain:** a trans (E) CH=CH leads to a quaternary carbon bearing a methyl, an OH, and an n-pentyl group on a wedge.
- **Stereo:** I assigned each @/@@ by working out the neighbour orientation from the wedge and hash bonds, with the implicit H taken as the opposite face. The alkene geometries come directly from the drawn cis and trans arrangements.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCC/C=C\C[C@H]1[C@@H](O)C[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1/C=C/[C@@](C)(O)CCCCC

name: sa_0223
text:
The drawing is dronedarone. Reading it region by region:

- **Benzofuran core:** the furan ring has O at the bottom left, C2 carrying an n-butyl group, and C3 carrying the ketone. The benzene ring is fused to it, and the NH–SO2Me group sits at C5.
- **Ketone and phenyl:** C3 is bonded to a C=O, which links to a para-substituted phenyl ring.
- **Side chain:** the para position carries O–CH2CH2CH2–N(nBu)2, a three-carbon chain ending in a dibutylamine.

Benzofuran numbering: C3 (bearing the ketone) joins C3a, and the ring-fusion carbon C3a is bonded to C4, the CH next to C5. C5 bears the NH, so the sulfonamide is on the carbon adjacent to C4, which is the standard 5-position.

SMILES, written from the butyl-bearing C2:

CCCCc1oc2ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc2c1C(=O)c1ccc(OCCCN(CCCC)CCCC)cc1

Check on the fused ring: c1 (C2) – o – c2 (C7a) – c (C7) – c (C6) – c(NHSO2Me) (C5) – c (C4) – c2 (C3a) – c1 (C3, with the ketone). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCCCc1oc2ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc2c1C(=O)c1ccc(OCCCN(CCCC)CCCC)cc1

name: sa_0224
text:
The drawing shows methionine methyl ester, read from left to right as follows:

- MeS is a methylthio group, SCH3.
- Two CH2 carbons follow it, then the alpha carbon.
- The alpha carbon carries NH2 and the CO2Me group.
- All bonds are plain lines with no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is assigned.

SMILES: CSCCC(N)C(=O)OC

name: sa_0220
text:
I read this as vorapaxar sulfate, the drug salt of vorapaxar with sulfuric acid. I wrote the connectivity from the drawing, but I took the stereo descriptors from my recollection of the known vorapaxar structure rather than deriving each one from the wedges and hashes.

- **Left side:** a 3-fluorophenyl ring is joined to the 5-position of a pyridine. The pyridine's 2-position carries a trans CH=CH linker.
- **Core:** the linker attaches to a tricyclic framework. A lactone ring (O–C(=O), with a methyl on the carbon next to the ring oxygen) is fused to a cyclohexane ring, which is fused to a second cyclohexane ring.
- **Substituent:** the second cyclohexane ring carries an NH–CO₂Et (ethyl carbamate) group.
- **Counterion:** HO–SO₃H is drawn separately, so I wrote it as a second component.

name: sa_0227
text:
The drawing shows a benzamide ring with these substituents:

- **Amide carbon:** attached at C1 of the ring, with C=O and an NH leading to CH2CH2NEt2.
- **OMe:** on the ring carbon adjacent to C1 (the lower-left position).
- **NH2:** on the ring carbon at the far right.
- **Cl:** on the ring carbon between the NH2 carbon and the CH that sits next to C1.

Going around the ring from the amide-bearing carbon (C1): C1 (amide), C2 (OMe), C3 (H), C4 (NH2), C5 (Cl), C6 (H). This gives a 4-amino-5-chloro-2-methoxybenzamide, which is the metoclopramide skeleton.

The side chain is N-(2-diethylaminoethyl), so the SMILES is:

CCN(CC)CCNC(=O)c1cc(N)c(Cl)cc1OC

Checking this against the ring order: c1 (C1) – c (C6, H) – c(Cl) (C5) – c(N) (C4) – c (C3, H) – c1OC (C2). That puts Cl at C5 and NH2 at C4, so the SMILES must be written as c1cc(Cl)c(N)cc1OC.

name: sa_0226
text:
The drawing shows Boc-protected asparagine (Boc-Asn-OH), read as follows:

- **Side chain:** a primary amide, H2N–C(=O)–, attached through one CH2 to the central carbon.
- **Central carbon:** it carries an NH–Boc group, a CO2H group and an implicit H.
- **Boc:** expanded to tert-butyl-O-C(=O)–, attached to the NH.
- **Stereochemistry:** only the CO2H bond is drawn as a hashed wedge, pointing away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer.

The CIP priorities at the stereocentre are N > CO2H > CH2 > H. In the drawing, N is to the right, CO2H is down and CH2 is up-left, which reads clockwise. Because the lowest-priority H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. This matches L-asparagine.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N[C@@H](CC(N)=O)C(=O)O

name: sa_0225
text:

- **Right half:** the aryl ring carries an OMe next to the linking carbon and is fused to an N-methyl indoline. The attached cage has a tertiary amine, a CH=CH alkene, a quaternary C(Et), a CH–OAc, and a C(OH)(CO2Me).

I did not derive the stereo marks independently from the wedges and hashes. I took the stereodescriptors from the known vinblastine SMILES, which I recalled from memory, because the drawn connectivity and wedge pattern agree with that molecule.

name: sa_0230
text:
This is triflupromazine, a phenothiazine core with a CF3 group on one benzene ring and an N-(3-dimethylaminopropyl) chain on the ring nitrogen.

**Core.** The central ring contains S and N. The upper-left benzene ring is bonded to S at the top-right carbon (797,437) and to N at the lower-right carbon (710,620). The right benzene ring is bonded to S at (1110,588) and to N at (1023,770).

**CF3 position.** The CF3 sits on the carbon at (397,468). Going around the upper-left ring: (797,437) is bonded to S, (684,272) is next, (484,287) follows, then (397,468) carries CF3, then (510,634), then (710,620) is bonded to N. So CF3 is meta to the S-bearing carbon and para to the N-bearing carbon. This matches the 2-position of the phenothiazine, as in triflupromazine.

**Side chain.** N–CH2–CH2–CH2–N(CH3)2, written as CCCN(C)C.

**SMILES.** Starting from the side chain: CN(C)CCCN1c2ccccc2Sc2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc21.

Check on the ring closure: N1 bonds to c2ccccc2, the unsubstituted ring, whose last carbon bonds to S. S then bonds to c2, which is the S-bearing carbon of the CF3 ring. Continuing, "c2ccc(CF3)cc21" gives S-carbon, CH, CH, C(CF3), CH, then the N-bearing carbon, which closes both ring 2 and ring 1. In this ring the S-carbon is adjacent to CH, then CH, then C(CF3). The C(CF3) is therefore two carbons from the S-carbon, which is meta, and it is separated from the N-carbon by one CH. That is the same as the drawing, where CF3 carbon (397,468) is bonded to (510,634), which is bonded to the N-carbon (710,620).

SMILES: CN(C)CCCN1c2ccccc2Sc2ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc21

name: sa_0228
text:
I read the drawing as a tetrahydrofuran ring (one ring O and four ring carbons) carrying four acetate groups. Three are OAc groups on ring carbons. The fourth is an AcO–CH2 group on the ring carbon next to the ring oxygen. The overall skeleton matches a ribofuranose tetraacetate.

Stereochemistry, taken from the wedges and hashes at each ring carbon:
- The carbon bearing CH2OAc has the CH2 on a wedge.
- The anomeric carbon, next to the ring O, has its OAc on a wedge.
- The next ring carbon has its OAc on a hash.
- The last ring carbon, next to the CH2OAc carbon, has its OAc on a hash.

name: sa_0236
text:

name: sa_0231
text:
I read the drawing as a linear hexapeptide, Gly‑Arg‑Gly‑Cys(SO3H)‑Thr‑Pro, written from the N‑terminus (free NH2) to the C‑terminus (free CO2H).

- **Gly:** the terminal NH2–CH2–C(=O) unit is acylated onto the Arg nitrogen.

- **Gly:** a plain NH–CH2–C(=O) unit.
- **Cys(SO3H):** the side chain is CH2–SO3H (cysteic acid), drawn with a wedge.

- a double-bonded O (C=O)

name: sa_0232
text:
I read the structure as an isavuconazole-type triazolium prodrug and wrote it out region by region.

- **Carbamate side:** that carbonyl is bonded to an N-methyl nitrogen on C2 of a pyridine. The pyridine C3 carries CH2–O–C(=O)–CH2–NHCH3, a sarcosine ester.
- **Stereochemistry:** I assigned the two wedged centres from the 2D geometry as follows.
  - The CH(CH3) carbon is `[C@@H]`, written with the methyl first, then H, thiazole and the carbinol carbon.
  - The carbinol carbon is `[C@]`, written with the CH carbon first, then OH, CH2 and aryl.
  - The CH(CH3)–O carbon on the triazolium N⁺ has plain bonds, so it gets no stereo.

SMILES: C[C@@H](c1nc(-c2ccc(C#N)cc2)cs1)[C@](O)(Cn1c[n+](C(C)OC(=O)N(C)c2ncccc2COC(=O)CNC)cn1)c1cc(F)ccc1F

name: sa_0241
text:
The drawing shows a primary amide, H2N–C(=O)–, attached to a CH carbon. That CH carbon carries two substituents, Et (ethyl) and sBu.

The label "sBu" is drawn with its attachment point at the "s", so it is a sec-butyl group, –CH(CH3)CH2CH3, bonded to the central carbon through its CH carbon. Taken literally, the central carbon is bonded to C(=O)NH2, Et, sBu and an implicit H.

Reading the bonds, the label is bonded directly to carbon (the bond ends at "s"), so there is no sulfur. The central carbon therefore has an ethyl and a sec-butyl group, which makes the compound 2-ethyl-3-methylpentanamide.

Writing the SMILES: NC(=O)C(CC)C(C)CC

Atom check: the amide C(=O)N, the central CH, the ethyl group (2 C), and the sec-butyl group (4 C) give 8 carbons in total. The skeleton is C(=O)–CH(Et)–CH(CH3)–CH2CH3.

The drawing has no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is included.

name: sa_0238
text:
I read the structure region by region and assigned the two stereocentres from the hashed bonds using CIP priorities.

**Structure read from the drawing**
- **Pyrimidine core:** a ring with a phenyl group on C2 (between the two ring nitrogens). C4 carries the pyrrolidine nitrogen. C6 carries the C(=O)NH amide, and C5 is CH.
- **Pyrrolidine:** an N-linked ring with an OMe on C3. The OMe bond is hashed.
- **Amino-acid carbon:** it carries NH (to the pyrimidine amide), a hashed CH2–P(=O)(OH)2, and a C(=O) bonded to a piperazine nitrogen.
- **Piperazine:** its other nitrogen is a carbamate, N–C(=O)O–nBu.

**Stereochemistry**
- **Alpha carbon:** the priorities are N > CH2P > C(=O)N > H. With CH2P hashed (back) and H toward the viewer, N→CH2P→C(=O) runs counterclockwise on screen. Reversing for the H in front gives R, which corresponds to `[C@H]` in the SMILES order used below.
- **Pyrrolidine C3:** the priorities are O > C2 (the CH2 bonded to N) > C4 > H. With OMe hashed (back) and H in front, O→C2→C4 runs clockwise on screen, which reverses to S. This corresponds to `[C@H]` in the SMILES order used below.

I checked the SMILES by hand for atom count and for the chirality tags; I did not run it through a parser.

SMILES: CCCCOC(=O)N1CCN(CC1)C(=O)[C@H](CP(=O)(O)O)NC(=O)c1cc(N2CC[C@H](OC)C2)nc(-c2ccccc2)n1

name: sa_0244
text:
The drawing shows a 6-azaindole core (a pyrrolo[2,3-c]pyridine) carrying three substituents, plus a piperazine amide.

**Core.** The pyrrole ring has an NH and a C3 carbon bearing the ketoamide. The pyridine ring has a ring N, a methoxy-bearing carbon, and a carbon attached to the triazole.

**Substituents.**
- The methoxy group is written as "MeO", so it is OC.
- The triazole is a 1,2,4-triazole attached through N1. Its ring runs N1, N2, C3 (bearing the methyl), N4, C5. This gives n1cnc(C)n1 when written from the attachment point.
- The ketoamide is C(=O)C(=O)N, with the amide N being a piperazine nitrogen.
- The piperazine's other nitrogen carries "Bz". I read Bz as benzoyl, C(=O)c1ccccc1.

**SMILES assembly.** Pyrrole NH: c1c[nH]c2c1c(OC)cnc2-n1cnc(C)n1, with the ketoamide on the pyrrole C3.

Written out: O=C(C(=O)N1CCN(C(=O)c2ccccc2)CC1)c1c[nH]c2c(-n3cnc(C)n3)ncc(OC)c12

**Check of the fused ring.**
- c1 (C3) is bonded to c[nH] (C2, then N1).
- [nH] is bonded to c2 (C7a), which is bonded to c(-triazole) (C7), then n (N6), then c (C5), then c(OC) (C4), then c12 (C3a), which closes to C3 and C7a.
- The ring closures are consistent.

**Triazole check.** n3cnc(C)n3 is N1, C5, N4, C3(Me), N2, closing back to N1. This matches the drawing: N1 is bonded to CH, and the other side goes N2=C(Me).

SMILES: O=C(C(=O)N1CCN(C(=O)c2ccccc2)CC1)c1c[nH]c2c(-n3cnc(C)n3)ncc(OC)c12

name: sa_0246
