Reading the structure region by region:
- Left end: a tBu group on a para-substituted benzene ring.
- The ring carbon opposite the tBu carries CH(OH).
- Chain: CH(OH), then CH2, CH2, CH2, then the piperidine N. That is 3 CH2 groups after the carbinol carbon, so 4 carbons in total counting the carbinol.
- Piperidine: the N sits in the ring, and the carbon opposite it bears C(OH)(Ph)2.

The ring's tBu and chain substituents are para to each other, as drawn.

name: sa_0245
text:
The drawing is Boc-protected threonine: a three-carbon chain with the Boc-NH group on C2, a hydroxyl on C3, a methyl on C3 and a carboxylic acid on C2.

**Connectivity:**
- The alpha carbon carries NH–Boc, the CO2H group and the beta carbon.
- The beta carbon carries OH, the CH3 and the alpha carbon.
- Boc expands to C(=O)OC(C)(C)C, attached through the carbamate carbon to N.

**Stereochemistry:** the wedges are on the CO2H bond (alpha carbon) and the CH3 bond (beta carbon). The implicit hydrogen on each stereocentre points away from the viewer.
- Alpha carbon: the priorities are N > CO2H > CB. Viewed from the front, N → CB → CO2H runs clockwise, so N → CO2H → CB runs counterclockwise, giving S.
- Beta carbon: the priorities are OH > Cα > CH3. Going OH → Cα → CH3 runs clockwise, giving R.

This is the (2S,3R) configuration, as in L-threonine. The SMILES below is L-threonine written with the Boc group on nitrogen, with the neighbour order unchanged so the chirality tags carry over.

SMILES: C[C@@H](O)[C@H](NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C(=O)O

name: sa_0234
text:
I read the structure as a macrocycle with a diethylaminoethylsulfonyl pyrrolidine, an oxazole and a conjugated polyene lactone. This is the dalfopristin-type skeleton.

**Connectivity, traced around the ring**
- The side chain Et2N–CH2CH2–SO2– is attached to C3 of the pyrrolidine. The pyrrolidine N is acylated by the oxazole C4 carbonyl, and C2 carries the ester C=O.
- The oxazole is C4=C5–O–C2(=N), with C2 bearing CH2–C(=O)–CH2–CH(OH).
- The CH(OH) leads into CH=C(CH3)–CH=CH–CH2–NH–C(=O)–CH=CH–CH(CH3)–CH(iPr)–O–C(=O), which closes back onto pyrrolidine C2.

**Double bonds, judged from the drawn geometry**
- The trisubstituted C=C(CH3) has the CH(OH) and the next CH= on opposite sides, so the methyl is cis to CH(OH).
- The CH=CH–CH2N double bond is trans.
- The CH=CH next to the amide carbonyl is trans.

**Stereocentres**
- Pyrrolidine C3 (hashed S) is `[C@@H]`.
- Pyrrolidine C2 (hashed H) is `[C@@H]`.
- CH(OH) (wedged OH) is `[C@H]`.
- CH(CH3) (hashed methyl) is `[C@H]`.
- CH(iPr)–O (wedged iPr) is `[C@@H]`.

I derived each chirality tag by hand from the wedge and hash positions, so the tags are the part most open to error.

name: sa_0247
text:
The drawing shows three parts joined in a row: a substituted benzene ring, an OCH2 linker, and a pyridine bearing an N-isopropylpyrazole.

**Benzene ring.** Going around the ring, the vertices are:
- C1, bearing the ether O (at about 627,768)
- C2, bearing CHO (at 463,847)
- C3, bearing OH (at 313,745)
- C4 (327,565)
- C5 (490,485)
- C6 (640,587)

So the ring has an OH at C3, a CHO at C2 between the OH and the ether oxygen, and the OCH2 at C1.

**Linker.** The ether oxygen connects to a CH2 (at 940,792), which attaches to the pyridine at C3 (1092,894).

**Pyridine ring.** Its atoms are:
- C3 (1092,894), carrying the CH2
- C2 (1255,816), carrying the pyrazole
- N (1405,918)
- C6 (1392,1099)
- C5 (1228,1177)
- C4 (1078,1075)

**Pyrazole ring.** The attachment carbon (1268,633) is bonded to N1, which carries the isopropyl group. N1 is bonded to N2 (=N), which connects to CH (1380,361), then CH (1422,538), and back to the attachment carbon. This is a 1-isopropylpyrazol-5-yl group.

**SMILES assembly:**
- Benzene ring: `Oc1cccc(OCc2cccnc2-c2ccnn2C(C)C)c1C=O`
- Check of the benzene substitution: c1(O) is C3, then c, c, c are C4, C5, C6, then c(OCH2…) is C1, then c1(C=O) is C2, which closes the ring to C3. This matches the drawing.
- Pyridine: `c2cccnc2` starts at C3 with the CH2, runs through C4, C5, C6 and N, and ends at C2 bearing the pyrazole. This matches.
- Pyrazole: `-c2ccnn2C(C)C` reads C5, C4, C3, N2, N1 with the isopropyl on N1. This matches.

SMILES: Oc1cccc(OCc2cccnc2-c2ccnn2C(C)C)c1C=O

name: sa_0249
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three features:

- An ester group, C(=O)OCCN(Et)2, attached at one ring carbon.
- An NH2 group on the ring carbon that is meta to the ester.
- An O-nPr group on the ring carbon that is para to the ester.

The ring numbering, going around from the ester carbon, is:

- C1 at (830, 718) bears the ester.
- C2 at (888, 863) is an aromatic CH.
- C3 at (1043, 885) bears NH2.
- C4 at (1138, 762) bears OPr.
- C5 at (1080, 617) is an aromatic CH.
- C6 at (926, 596) is an aromatic CH.

So the substituents are 1-ester, 3-amino and 4-propoxy. This is the compound proparacaine, whose full name is 2-(diethylamino)ethyl 3-amino-4-propoxybenzoate. The image shows it as the hydrochloride salt, written as a separate HCl component.

The SMILES for the free base with HCl as a second component is:

SMILES: CCCOc1ccc(cc1N)C(=O)OCCN(CC)CC.Cl

name: sa_0250
text:
The drawing shows a central silicon atom bonded to three isopropyl (iPr) groups and one SH group. This is triisopropylsilanethiol.

Each iPr group is CH(CH3)2, written as C(C)C in SMILES. The SH group is a sulfur with one hydrogen, so it is written as S.

Putting these together on silicon gives CC(C)[Si](S)(C(C)C)C(C)C. This has Si with four substituents (three isopropyl groups and one S) and no stereochemistry is drawn.

SMILES: CC(C)[Si](S)(C(C)C)C(C)C

name: sa_0251
text:
The drawing shows a central carbon with three substituents: a Ph label (phenyl), a double bond to O (carbonyl), and a single bond to an O labelled BzO.

BzO is benzoyloxy, written O-C(=O)-Ph. The Bz abbreviation here stands for benzoyl, so the molecule is Ph-C(=O)-O-Bz, which is benzoic anhydride: O=C(c1ccccc1)OC(=O)c1ccccc1.

The alternative reading of Bz as benzyl is less likely, because benzyl is normally abbreviated Bn. With benzyl, the molecule would be benzyl benzoate instead.

SMILES: O=C(c1ccccc1)OC(=O)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0252
text:
The drawing shows diethyl 2-(ethoxymethylene)malonate.

- The central alkene is C(=CH–OEt), where the CH carbon bears an OEt group.
- The other alkene carbon carries two CO2Et groups, one labelled EtO2C and one labelled CO2Et.
- Each CO2Et group is a carbonyl carbon bonded to O–ethyl.
- The double bond has two identical substituents (the two CO2Et groups) on one end, so it has no E/Z stereochemistry.

SMILES: CCOC=C(C(=O)OCC)C(=O)OCC

name: sa_0253
text:
The image shows a central nitrogen bonded by plain single bonds to three groups labelled Ph. Expanding each Ph to a phenyl ring (c1ccccc1) gives triphenylamine.

SMILES: c1ccc(cc1)N(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0254
text:
The drawing shows a central sulfur with two double-bonded oxygens (left and right), an OMe group on top, and a CF3 group on the bottom. This is methyl trifluoromethanesulfonate (methyl triflate).

SMILES: COS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F

name: sa_0256
text:
The drawing shows an NH with two substituents: Ph (phenyl) on the left and PMB on the right.

PMB is the p-methoxybenzyl group, CH2-C6H4-OMe with the methoxy para to the CH2.

That gives N-(4-methoxybenzyl)aniline: c1ccccc1NCc1ccc(OC)cc1.

SMILES: COc1ccc(CNc2ccccc2)cc1

name: sa_0248
text:
I read the drawing as cefcapene pivoxil, a cephalosporin prodrug.

- **Side chain:** a 2-aminothiazol-4-yl group sits on a carbon that is double-bonded to a CH–Et unit, and that same carbon carries the amide C=O. In the drawing the ethyl group and the amide carbonyl are on the same side of the double bond, so the alkene is cis (Z) and I wrote it with `/` and `\` marks.
- **Core:** the amide NH is attached to the β-lactam carbon (C7) by a wedge bond. The ring-fusion carbon (C6) carries a hashed H. The β-lactam fused to the six-membered ring has S, a CH2, and a ring C=C.
- **Substituents on the six-membered ring:** one carbon bears CH2–O–C(=O)NH2 (a carbamate). The other carries a C(=O)–O–CH2–O–pivaloyl ester, with the pivaloyl group expanded to C(=O)C(CH3)3.
- **Ring stereochemistry:** I did not derive the `@`/`@@` marks atom by atom from the wedge and hash. I took them from the standard natural cephalosporin configuration (6R,7R) and assumed the drawing follows it.

SMILES: CC/C=C(\C(=O)N[C@H]1[C@H]2SCC(COC(N)=O)=C(C(=O)OCOC(=O)C(C)(C)C)N2C1=O)c1csc(N)n1

name: sa_0257
text:
The drawing shows a 1,6-naphthyridin-2(1H)-one core carrying an N-ethyl group, a 7-NHMe group, and a substituted aryl group at C3.

**Core ring system.** The lactam ring contains N1 (bearing Et), C2 (=O), C3 (attached to the aryl group), C4 (CH), C4a, and C8a.
- The second ring runs from C4a to C5 (CH), then N6, then C7 (bearing NHMe), then C8 (CH), then C8a.
- N6 sits at the top, next to C5, which is bonded to C4a. This makes it a 1,6-naphthyridine.

**Aryl ring.** Its attachment carbon (call it a1) is bonded to the naphthyridinone C3.
- Going around the ring from a1: a2 is the CH at the top, a3 carries the NH urea, a4 carries F, a5 is CH, and a6 carries Br.
- The urea is NH–C(=O)–NH–Ph.

**SMILES assembly.** I wrote the core as O=C1N(CC)c2cc(NC)ncc2cc1, then attached the aryl group at C3 (the ring atom next to C=O):
- Core: CCn1c(=O)c(-c3cc(NC(=O)Nc4ccccc4)c(F)cc3Br)cc2cnc(NC)cc12
- Ring check: n1 (N1), c(=O) (C2), c(...) (C3), c (C4), c2 (C4a), c (C5), n (N6), c(NC) (C7), c (C8), c12 (C8a), which closes both rings.
- Aryl ring check: c3 (a1), c (a2), c(NC(=O)Nc4ccccc4) (a3), c(F) (a4), c (a5), c3Br (a6).

SMILES: CCn1c(=O)c(-c3cc(NC(=O)Nc4ccccc4)c(F)cc3Br)cc2cnc(NC)cc12

name: sa_0259
text:
The drawing shows three parts: a nitroimidazole ring, a CH2–O linker, and a para-substituted benzene ring.

**Imidazole ring.** It has five atoms: N1 (bearing a methyl group), C2 (bearing the CH2 substituent), N3, C4 (an unsubstituted CH), and C5 (bearing the nitro group). The bonds are C2=N3 and C4=C5, with N1 joined to C2 and C5.

**Linker.** C2 is attached to CH2, which is attached to O, which is attached to the benzene ring.

**Benzene ring.** It is para-substituted, with the oxygen on one carbon and SMe (a methylthio group) on the carbon opposite.

Writing the SMILES from N1: Cn1c([N+](=O)[O-])cnc1COc1ccc(SC)cc1

SMILES: Cn1c([N+](=O)[O-])cnc1COc1ccc(SC)cc1

name: sa_0255
text:
This structure is valrubicin (N‑trifluoroacetyladriamycin‑14‑valerate), a doxorubicin derivative. I wrote the SMILES by adapting the known doxorubicin SMILES to the groups shown in the drawing. I did not independently re‑derive each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes, so the stereo marks rest on the doxorubicin‑type configuration (7S,9S in the aglycone).

- **Aglycone:** a tetracyclic anthracyclinone with a methoxy group on the aromatic ring, two quinone carbonyls, and two phenolic OH groups. The saturated ring carries a tertiary OH and the sugar linked through an O‑glycoside.
- **C‑9 side chain:** C(=O)CH2–O–C(=O)–nBu, a 14‑valerate ester, replacing the CH2OH of doxorubicin.
- **Sugar:** a 2,6‑dideoxy sugar with a 4‑OH and a 3‑NH–C(=O)CF3 (trifluoroacetamide) in place of the free NH2 of doxorubicin.

SMILES: COc1cccc2c1C(=O)c1c(O)c3c(c(O)c1C2=O)C[C@@](O)(C(=O)COC(=O)CCCC)C[C@@H]3O[C@H]1C[C@H](NC(=O)C(F)(F)F)[C@H](O)[C@H](C)O1

name: sa_0261
text:
This is the gadoversetamide-type ligand (a DTPA bis(methoxyethylamide)) drawn with a separate Gd3+ ion.

Reading the structure from left to right:
- MeO–CH2CH2–NH–C(=O)–CH2–N(CH2COO−)–CH2CH2–N(CH2COO−)–CH2CH2–N(CH2COO−)–CH2–C(=O)–NH–CH2CH2–OMe.
- The three carboxylates are on the first, middle and last nitrogens, so there are three COO− groups in total.
- The gadolinium is drawn as a separate species, written [Gd+3]. The image labels it "Gd3+·" with a radical dot, but I treat it as a plain ion.

Charge check: three carboxylates give −3 and Gd gives +3, so the complex is neutral overall.

SMILES: COCCNC(=O)CN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CCN(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)NCCOC.[Gd+3]

name: sa_0262
text:
This looks like articaine, the thiophene local anesthetic, with a propylamino group on the side chain.

**Thiophene ring:** S is bonded to a CH carbon and to a carbon carrying CO2Me. That carbon (C2) is double-bonded to C3, which carries the NH amide. C3 is bonded to C4, which carries the methyl group. C4 is double-bonded to C5, the CH next to S.

**Side chain:** The amide nitrogen is attached to C(=O), which is bonded to CH(CH3). That CH carries an NH-nPr group. No wedges or hashes are drawn, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES check: CCCNC(C)C(=O)Nc1c(C(=O)OC)scc1C

Reading the ring in that SMILES: c1 (C3, bearing the amide N), then c(CO2Me) (C2), then s, then c (C5, the CH), then c1C (C4, bearing the methyl). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCCNC(C)C(=O)Nc1c(C(=O)OC)scc1C

name: sa_0263
text:
The drawing is an anthraquinone with two acetoxy groups and one carboxylic acid.

**Core and substituents**
- The central ring carries two C=O groups, one at the top and one at the bottom.
- The left benzene ring has an OAc on its lower carbon, the one adjacent to the bottom-carbonyl side.
- The right ring has a CO2H on its upper-right carbon and an OAc on its lower-left carbon.

**Right ring connectivity**
- The ring atoms are C4a (at 737,845), C9a (at 758,655), C1 (at 933,578), C2 (at 1088,690), C3 (at 1067,882) and C4 (at 890,960).
- Going around the ring: C9a (attached to the top C=O) – C1 (H) – C2 (CO2H) – C3 (H) – C4 (OAc) – C4a (attached to the bottom C=O).

**Left ring connectivity**
- C8a (at 427,617) is attached to the top C=O.
- C4a' (at 405,807) is attached to the bottom C=O and to the carbon bearing OAc at (230,883).
- The left ring runs C8a – CH (273,502) – CH (95,578) – CH (75,769) – C(OAc) (230,883) – C4a'.

**SMILES**
Start at the top carbonyl: O=C1c2cccc(OC(C)=O)c2C(=O)c2c(OC(C)=O)cc(C(=O)O)cc21

Check of the last ring: after the bottom C(=O), the next atom c2 is C4a. It is followed by c(OAc), which is C4; then c, which is C3 (H); then c(CO2H), which is C2; then c, which is C1 (H); and finally c21, which is C9a and closes onto the top carbonyl. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: O=C1c2cccc(OC(C)=O)c2C(=O)c2c(OC(C)=O)cc(C(=O)O)cc21

name: sa_0260
text:
I read this as a 7‑substituted camptothecin: the pentacyclic camptothecin core with a 2‑(trimethylsilyl)ethyl group on the carbon next to the benzo ring. That is karenitecin.

- **Core:** the lactone ring has a ring C=O and a CH2–O. The pyridone ring has its C=O on the nitrogen. The CH2 on that nitrogen leads into the five‑membered ring. The quinoline N sits in the aromatic benzo‑fused ring.
- **Substituent on the benzo side:** CH2CH2 followed by the TMS label, expanded to Si(CH3)3.
- **Stereocentre:** the quaternary carbon carries OH, ethyl, the lactone C=O and a ring carbon. The ethyl is drawn on a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer. With ethyl at the back, OH → lactone C(=O) → ring carbon runs counterclockwise on the page, which gives S. The SMILES below, with `[C@@]` and ethyl written first, also encodes S.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OCC2=C1C=C1N(C2=O)CC2=C1N=C1C=CC=CC1=C2CC[Si](C)(C)C

name: sa_0265
text:
The drawing shows a central CH carbon bonded to three groups: an OH, a CCl3 group, and a phosphorus atom. The phosphorus carries a P=O double bond and two OMe groups, so this is dimethyl (2,2,2-trichloro-1-hydroxyethyl)phosphonate (trichlorfon).

The stereocentre at the CH carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: COP(=O)(OC)C(O)C(Cl)(Cl)Cl

name: sa_0258
text:
This reads as torcetrapib: a 3,4-dihydro-2H-quinoline with the following substituents.

- **N1:** an ethyl carbamate (EtO2C–N).
- **C2:** an ethyl group on a hashed bond.
- **C4:** a nitrogen on a hashed bond, carrying a methyl carbamate (CO2Me) and a 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)benzyl group.
- **C6:** a CF3 on the fused benzene ring.

I assigned the stereocentres from the hashed bonds, treating each hash as pointing away from the viewer, so the implicit H sits toward the viewer.

- **C2:** the CIP priorities are N > C3 > Et > H. Reading N → C3 → Et on the page runs counterclockwise. With H toward the viewer this reverses, so the centre is R.
- **C4:** the priorities are N > C4a > C3 > H. Reading N → C4a → C3 runs clockwise. With H toward the viewer this reverses, so the centre is S.

That gives (2R,4S). I then chose the @/@@ marks in the SMILES so that the written order yields R at C2 and S at C4.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)N1[C@H](CC)C[C@H](N(Cc2cc(cc(c2)C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F)C(=O)OC)c2cc(ccc12)C(F)(F)F

name: sa_0266
text:
The drawing shows mescaline: a benzene ring with an aminoethyl chain and three methoxy groups.

- **Chain:** H2N is bonded to CH2, then CH2, then the ring carbon.
- **Ring:** a benzene ring with three adjacent OMe groups. Going around from the chain carbon, the next ring carbon is a CH, then C-OMe at the top right, then C-OMe at the right, then C-OMe at the lower right, then a CH back to the start. This is the 3,4,5-trimethoxy pattern.
- **Stereochemistry:** none is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: NCCc1cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c1

name: sa_0269
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with an HO group on the left-hand vertex. I name the ring positions from that carbon.

- C1 (left, at about 463,748) carries the OH.
- C2 (upper left, at about 600,510) carries a tBu group.
- C3 (upper right, at about 875,510) has no substituent, so it is CH.
- C4 (right, at about 1012,748) carries a tBu group.
- C5 (lower right, at about 875,987) has no substituent, so it is CH.
- C6 (lower left, at about 600,987) carries a tBu group.

So the tBu groups sit at C2, C4 and C6, which makes this 2,4,6-tri-tert-butylphenol.

The double bonds are C2=C3, C4=C5 and C6=C1, which is a valid Kekulé structure.

SMILES: Oc1c(C(C)(C)C)cc(C(C)(C)C)cc1C(C)(C)C

name: sa_0268
text:
This is a 1,4-dihydropyridine of the nifedipine type: a ring NH with a methyl on each flanking carbon, a 2-nitrophenyl group at C4, and an ester on each of C3 and C5.

The labels need careful reading. On the left, the chain runs C(=O)–O–CH2–"Ac", and "Ac" is the acetyl abbreviation. Expanded, that gives an O–CH2–C(=O)CH3 group, so the ester is an acetonyl ester: C(=O)OCC(C)=O.

The other ester is CO2Me, which is C(=O)OC.

Ring atoms:
- N1 (NH)
- C2, bearing a methyl, the top carbon attached to NH
- C3, bearing the acetonyl ester
- C4, the sp3 CH bearing the 2-nitrophenyl group
- C5, bearing CO2Me
- C6, bearing a methyl

SMILES: CC1=C(C(=O)OCC(C)=O)C(c2ccccc2[N+](=O)[O-])C(C(=O)OC)=C(C)N1

The benzene ring is attached at one carbon, and the adjacent carbon carries the nitro group, which makes it ortho.

SMILES: CC1=C(C(=O)OCC(C)=O)C(c2ccccc2[N+](=O)[O-])C(C(=O)OC)=C(C)N1

name: sa_0267
text:
The drawing is N²,N⁶-bis-Fmoc-lysine (Fmoc-Lys(Fmoc)-OH).

- **Backbone:** A CO2H group is attached to the stereocentre, which also carries an NH-Fmoc. A chain of four CH2 groups leads from the stereocentre to a second NH-Fmoc. This is the lysine skeleton.
- **Fmoc groups:** Each Fmoc is expanded as C(=O)OCH2 attached to fluorene, written `C(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12`.
- **Stereochemistry:** The wedge runs from the stereocentre to the CO2H, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2 > H. Going N (up) → CO2H (lower left) → CH2 (lower right) is counterclockwise, so the centre is S, the L-lysine configuration.
- **SMILES ordering:** L-lysine is `N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)O`. Writing the neighbours in the order CO2H, H, chain, N swaps N and CO2H, so the tag flips to `@`.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@H](CCCCNC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12)NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12

name: sa_0271
text:
This is a 1,4-dihydropyridine of the nicardipine type, with a cyclic phosphonate in place of the second ester.

**Dihydropyridine ring:** N1(H) is bonded to C2 (bearing a methyl) and C6 (bearing a methyl). C2=C3 and C5=C6 are the double bonds. C3 carries the ester, C4 carries the aryl group, and C5 carries the phosphorus group.

**Ester:** C(=O)OCCN(Bn)Ph, where Bn is CH2Ph and Ph is phenyl.

**Aryl group:** 3-nitrophenyl on C4.

**Phosphorus group:** P(=O) in a six-membered ring, P–O–CH2–C(CH3)2–CH2–O. This is the 5,5-dimethyl-1,3,2-dioxaphosphinane 2-oxide.

**Stereochemistry:** C4 is a stereocentre by connectivity but is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

**SMILES assembly:** CC1=C(C(=O)OCCN(Cc2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)C(c2cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c2)C(P2(=O)OCC(C)(C)CO2)=C(C)N1

Checking the ring: C1(CH3)=C(ester)–C4H(aryl)–C(P)=C(CH3)–N1, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC1=C(C(=O)OCCN(Cc2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)C(c2cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c2)C(P2(=O)OCC(C)(C)CO2)=C(C)N1

name: sa_0272
text:
The drawing shows a central carbon–carbon triple bond with a TMS group on each end, so the molecule is bis(trimethylsilyl)acetylene.

TMS is the trimethylsilyl group, Si(CH3)3. Expanding both ends gives C[Si](C)(C)C#C[Si](C)(C)C. The SMILES is valid and matches the drawing atom for atom. No stereochemistry applies.

SMILES: C[Si](C)(C)C#C[Si](C)(C)C

name: sa_0274
text:
The drawing shows a central vertex (a CH2) with two bonds going to labels written "NC" on the left and "CN" on the right.

The right label "CN" is attached through its C atom, so that arm is a nitrile (–C≡N).

The left label "NC" is written with N first and C second, and the bond reaches the C end of the label. The C is therefore the attachment atom, so that arm is also –C≡N, just written in reverse order. It is not an isocyanide, which would need the bond to land on N.

The molecule is malononitrile, N#CCC#N.

SMILES: N#CCC#N

name: sa_0273
text:
The image shows two separate molecules, so the SMILES has two components joined by a dot. I read both as 3α-hydroxy-5α-pregnane-11,20-dione derivatives. I took the stereocentre tags from the known SMILES for alfaxalone (recalled from memory) rather than deriving each one from the drawing, and I only spot-checked them against the drawn wedges and hashes.

- **Top molecule:** the 21-acetate of this steroid. The Ac–O–CH2–C(=O) side chain sits on C17, and it has an 11-ketone and a 3-OH.
- **Bottom molecule:** the parent compound, alfaxalone. It has an acetyl group on C17, an 11-ketone and a 3-OH.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawn wedges and hashes match the natural 3α,5α,8β,9α,10β,13β,14α,17β configuration, and the wedges and hashes were read from the drawing in the same way for both molecules.

SMILES: CC(=O)OCC(=O)[C@H]1CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC(=O)[C@H]3[C@H]2CC[C@@H]4[C@@]3(CC[C@H](C4)O)C)C.CC(=O)[C@H]1CC[C@@H]2[C@@]1(CC(=O)[C@H]3[C@H]2CC[C@@H]4[C@@]3(CC[C@H](C4)O)C)C

name: sa_0270
text:
I read this as the 6-chloro-17-acetoxy-pregna-4,6-diene-3,20-dione skeleton (the chlormadinone acetate constitution), but with every stereocentre drawn in the mirror-image sense.

**Connectivity**
- The steroid core has an enone in ring A: a C=O on the right, conjugated with the C4=C5 double bond.
- Ring B carries a second double bond (C6=C7), with Cl on C6.
- C17 on the five-membered ring D carries both an acetoxy group (the "OAc" label, O–C(=O)CH3) and an acetyl group (the "Ac" label, C(=O)CH3).
- There are two angular methyl groups, at C10 and C13.

**Stereochemistry**
- Both methyls (C10 and C13) are drawn with hashed bonds.
- The ring-fusion hydrogens are drawn as wedge at C9 (top, near the ring B/C junction), hashed at C8, and wedge at C14.
- The acetyl group at C17 is hashed.
- This is the opposite of the natural steroid arrangement (methyls wedged, C9–H hashed, C8–H wedged, C14–H hashed, C17 acetyl wedged). So the drawing shows the enantiomer of the natural series.
- I wrote the natural-series SMILES from memory of the progesterone pattern, not from re-deriving each centre from the picture. I then inverted every stereocentre to match the drawing.

SMILES: CC(=O)[C@@]1(CC[C@H]2[C@]1(CC[C@@H]3[C@@H]2C=C(C4=CC(=O)CC[C@@]34C)Cl)C)OC(=O)C

name: sa_0264
text:
I read the drawing as treprostinil with diethanolamine, written as a two-component salt/co-crystal (the acid is drawn neutral, not as a carboxylate).

**Diethanolamine:** HO‑CH2CH2‑NH‑CH2CH2‑OH, written `OCCNCCO`.

**Treprostinil part:**
- The side chain is n‑pentyl–CH(OH)–CH2–CH2–, attached to the cyclopentane ring. The hashed bond to the carbinol carbon gives (S) at that centre.
- The five‑membered ring carries the side chain on one carbon and a wedged OH on the adjacent carbon. It is fused to a six‑membered ring containing two CH2 groups, which is fused to a benzene ring.
- The benzene ring has an O‑CH2‑CO2H group on the carbon next to the ring‑fusion carbon that bears the CH2 attached to the cyclopentane ring‑fusion CH.
- The two ring‑fusion hydrogens are both hashed.

I assigned @/@@ at each stereocentre from the wedge and hash geometry and the atom order in the SMILES.

name: sa_0277
text:
The drawing shows Fmoc-protected methionine: a chain MeS–CH2–CH2–CH(NH–Fmoc)–CO2H, where Fmoc is the 9-fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl group on the nitrogen.

**Stereochemistry:** The only stereocentre is the α-carbon, and the CO2H bond is hashed (pointing away from the viewer). The substituent priorities are N > CO2H > CH2 > H, and the implicit H points toward the viewer. In the drawing, N (lower left) → CO2H (upper left) → CH2 (right) runs clockwise. Because the H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. This matches the L-methionine configuration, which in this SMILES ordering is `CSCC[C@H](N...)C(=O)O`.

**Assembled SMILES:** the Fmoc group is written as the carbamate `NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12`, attached to the α-carbon's N.

name: sa_0275
text:
I read the molecule as a 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroquinoline core, a type of structure seen in CETP inhibitors such as torcetrapib.

**Tetrahydroquinoline core**
- The ring nitrogen N1 carries an ethyl carbamate, CO2Et.
- C2 carries an ethyl group on a hashed bond.
- C3 is a plain CH2.
- C4 carries an exocyclic nitrogen on a hashed bond.
- The benzo ring has a CF3 on the carbon para to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to N1 (position 6).

**Substituent on the C4 nitrogen**
- A 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)benzyl group.
- A pyrimidin-2-yl ring bearing an O–CH2CH2CH2–CO2H chain at its 5-position. This is three CH2 groups between the ether oxygen and the carboxylic acid.

**Stereochemistry**
- Only the two hashed centres, C2 and C4, are stereocentres.
- Working from the drawn geometry, with the hashed group at the back and the implicit H toward the viewer, both centres come out as `@` in the SMILES order I wrote.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)N1[C@H](CC)C[C@H](N(Cc2cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c2)c2ncc(OCCCC(=O)O)cn2)c2cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc21

name: sa_0280
text:
The drawing shows ethyl cinnamate: EtO2C–CH=CH–Ph.

The chain runs from the EtO2C label at lower left up to a vertex at the top (about x=722, y=622), then down to a second vertex (about x=1000, y=833), and up to Ph at the right. The double bond is the one between those two vertices.

For geometry, the ester carbon sits lower-left of the first alkene carbon and the Ph sits upper-right of the second. The two substituents lie on opposite sides of the double bond, so it is trans (E).

Writing the SMILES in order: CCOC(=O)/C=C/c1ccccc1. The `/C=C/` pattern places the two substituents on opposite sides, which matches the E geometry.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)/C=C/c1ccccc1

name: sa_0279
text:
This is adefovir dipivoxil: the adenine N9 carries a CH2CH2–O–CH2–P(=O) chain, and the phosphorus bears two O–CH2–O–Piv groups.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- Adenine: the six-membered ring has N at the top and N at the right, plus the C–NH2 carbon. The five-membered ring has N9 bearing the chain and N7 at the bottom.
- Chain: N9 connects to CH2, then CH2, then O, then CH2, then P.
- Phosphorus: it has one =O and two O–CH2–O–Piv arms.

"Piv" is pivaloyl, C(=O)C(C)(C)C, so each arm is OCOC(=O)C(C)(C)C. The "OPiv" label is an O attached to Piv, which gives the CH2–O–C(=O)tBu ester.

The adenine SMILES with N9 substituted is n1cnc(N)c2ncn(R)c12.

Assembled SMILES: CC(C)(C)C(=O)OCOP(=O)(COCCn1cnc2c(N)ncnc12)OCOC(=O)C(C)(C)C

SMILES: CC(C)(C)C(=O)OCOP(=O)(COCCn1cnc2c(N)ncnc12)OCOC(=O)C(C)(C)C

Reading the chain from the left, the EtO2C carbon bonds to a vertex at the top, which bonds to a vertex at the bottom, which bonds to the CO2Et carbon. That gives two CH2 groups between the two ester carbons.

There are no wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry, so no stereochemistry is included.

name: sa_0285
text:
The drawing shows a central CH carbon bonded to three groups: a carboxylic acid (HO2C), an n-butyl chain (nBu), and a carbonyl carbon (C=O).

The carbonyl carbon is bonded to a nitrogen that carries a phenyl group. That nitrogen is also bonded to an NH, which carries a second phenyl group. This is a 1,2-diphenylhydrazide: C(=O)N(Ph)NHPh.

name: sa_0276
text:
I read the structure as a methyl heptanoate chain attached to a cyclopentanone ring that carries a hydroxyl group and a trans-alkenyl side chain.

**Ring (clockwise from the C=O):**
- The ring is a cyclopentanone: C(=O), then CH2, then CH(OH), then CH bearing the alkenyl chain, then CH bearing the ester chain.
- The OH is on a wedge bond.
- The ester chain is on a wedge bond.
- The alkenyl chain is on a hashed bond.

**Ester chain:** Six CH2 groups lead from the ring to a CO2Me group, which gives a methyl heptanoate substituent.

**Alkenyl chain:**
- The chain runs from the ring as CH=CH, then CH2, then a quaternary carbon.
- The two alkene substituents point to opposite sides, so the double bond is trans (E).
- The quaternary carbon carries OH, CH3 and n-butyl (CCCC). It is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label.

**Stereo assignment:** I worked out the three ring stereocentres from the wedge and hash geometry, with the implicit H opposite the wedged or hashed substituent in each case.

SMILES: COC(=O)CCCCCC[C@H]1C(=O)C[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1/C=C/CC(C)(O)CCCC

name: sa_0287

name: sa_0278
text:
I read the molecule as an aryl amide of a 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane. I did not run a SMILES validator; the atom-by-atom check below was done by hand.

- **Aryl ring:** a benzene ring carries the C(=O)N amide carbon. Ortho to it is an O–CH(CH3)CF3 ether. The methylsulfonyl group (MeO2S, i.e. S(C)(=O)=O) sits para to that ether oxygen and meta to the carbonyl.
- **Amide:** the carbonyl is bonded to the nitrogen of the bicyclic core, a 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane. This is a pyrrolidine with a fused cyclopropane CH2.
- **Core substituent:** the quaternary bridgehead carbon, drawn with a wedge bond, bears a 5-(trifluoromethyl)isoxazol-3-yl group. The isoxazole connects as C(=N)–CH=C(CF3)–O–N. The other bridgehead carbon is CH, with its H drawn as a wedge.
- **Side-chain stereocentre:** the O–CH(CH3)CF3 carbon has a hashed bond to CF3.

I assigned the three stereocentres from the drawn wedges and hashes. The quaternary bridgehead and the CH bridgehead came from the 2D coordinates by a signed-volume check. The side-chain CH came from the hashed CF3 with the implicit H toward the viewer, and I judged it more roughly.

SMILES: C[C@@H](Oc1ccc(S(C)(=O)=O)cc1C(=O)N1C[C@@]2(c3cc(C(F)(F)F)on3)C[C@H]2C1)C(F)(F)F

name: sa_0286
text:
The drawing is Nα,Nε-di-Boc-lysine (Boc-Lys(Boc)-OH), with S configuration at the α-carbon.

- **Backbone:** a carboxylic acid (HO₂C) is attached to the stereocentre. A four-carbon chain runs from the stereocentre to the terminal NH.
- **Substituents:** the stereocentre also carries an NH–Boc group, and the terminal NH on the chain carries a second Boc. Each Boc expands to C(=O)OC(C)(C)C.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CO₂H is on a wedge, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CO₂H > CH₂ > H. Going N (up) → CO₂H (lower left) → CH₂ (lower right) is counterclockwise with H at the back, which gives S, as in L-lysine.
- **SMILES chirality:** I wrote the chain carbon first, so the order around the stereocentre is chain, H, N, CO₂H. This corresponds to `[C@H]`, matching L-lysine's `N[C@@H](CCCCN)C(=O)O` after one swap.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)NCCCC[C@H](NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C(=O)O

name: sa_0289
text:
The drawing is a 1,4-dihydropyridine bearing a 3-nitrophenyl group at C4, methyl groups at C2 and C6, and two ester groups at C3 and C5.

Each ester is an OCH2CH2O-nPr group. The "nPr" label is n-propyl, so each side chain is C(=O)OCCOCCC.

- C5=C6, and C5 carries the right ester.

Going around the ring, the next atom is (530, 857), then (483, 965), which bears the NO2. The NO2 carbon is therefore separated from the attachment carbon by one carbon, so it is meta.

text:

name: sa_0303
text:
The drawing shows a bicyclic pyrrolizine core with a carboxylic acid and a "Bz" label.

- C1= closes the ring at C(a), which is double-bonded to CH, followed by CH=C2, which closes the ring to N. That carbon carries the Bz group.
- The ring-closure atoms are consistent.
- The pyrrole-like ring is N, C(a), CH, CH, C(Bz), so five atoms.

name: sa_0301
text:
I read this as cefozopran, a cephalosporin, and wrote the SMILES region by region.

- **Side chain on the left:** a 5-amino-1,2,4-thiadiazol-3-yl ring, `c1nsc(N)n1`, attached to a C(=N–OMe) carbon that carries the amide C=O.
- **Oxime geometry:** the OMe on the oxime nitrogen points to the same side as the amide carbonyl, so the thiadiazole is trans to the OMe (the syn, Z oxime). I encoded this as `CO/N=C(/c1nsc(N)n1)\C(=O)...`.
- **Core:** a β-lactam fused to a dihydrothiazine ring (S–CH2–C=C–N), with a COO⁻ on the ring carbon next to N and the lactam C=O at the bottom.
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows a wedge on the C7 N–H bond and a hash on the C6 H. I assigned these as `[C@H]1[C@H]2`, which I take to be the natural 6R,7R cephalosporin configuration.

name: sa_0307
text:
The drawing shows Fmoc-NH on a central carbon that also carries a CO2H group and an isopropyl group (iPr). The iPr group is on a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer.

**Connectivity:** The Fmoc group is the fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl carbamate, written Fmoc-N as `NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc21`. The central carbon is bonded to N, CO2H, iPr and one implicit H. This is the skeleton of valine, so the molecule is Fmoc-valine.

**Stereochemistry:** The CIP priorities at the stereocentre are N > CO2H > iPr > H.
- The implicit H points toward the viewer, because the iPr group is hashed (behind the plane).
- Viewed from the front, N (lower left) → CO2H (up) → iPr (lower right) runs clockwise.
- Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S.

This matches Fmoc-L-valine. The SMILES `CC(C)[C@H](N…)C(=O)O` encodes the S configuration, as in L-valine `CC(C)[C@H](N)C(=O)O`.

SMILES: CC(C)[C@H](NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc21)C(=O)O

name: sa_0299
text:
I read this as benidipine: a 1,4-dihydropyridine carrying two methyl groups, a methyl ester and a 3-nitrophenyl group. The second ester is an N-benzylpyrrolidin-3-yl ester. I assigned the two stereocentres from the wedge and hash bonds using CIP priorities.

**Dihydropyridine ring**
- The ring is N1H, C2(CH3)=C3, C4(H)(aryl), C5=C6(CH3).
- C3 carries the C(=O)O–pyrrolidinyl ester, and C5 carries CO2Me.
- C4 carries the 3-nitrophenyl group (the NO2 sits meta to the attachment point).

**Pyrrolidine ester**
- The ester oxygen is attached at C3 of an N-benzylpyrrolidine, and Bn is expanded to CH2Ph.

**Stereocentre at pyrrolidine C3** (bold wedge to O)
- Priorities are O > C2 (attached to N) > C4 > H.
- With H pointing away from the viewer, O → C2 → C4 runs counterclockwise, so the centre is S.
- In my SMILES this is `O[C@H]2CCN(Cc3ccccc3)C2`.

**Stereocentre at dihydropyridine C4** (hashed bond to the aryl group)
- C3 and C5 both have (C,C,C) substituents, and so does the aryl carbon. Going deeper, the aryl carbon drops below both ring carbons.
- C3 outranks C5 because, at the fifth sphere, the pyrrolidine carbon (C,C,H) beats the methyl carbon (H,H,H).
- Priorities are therefore C3 > C5 > aryl > H.
- H points toward the viewer. C3 → C5 → aryl runs clockwise on the page, which reverses to counterclockwise, so the centre is S.
- In my SMILES this is `[C@H]1` for the atom written after C3.

SMILES: COC(=O)C1=C(C)NC(C)=C(C(=O)O[C@H]2CCN(Cc3ccccc3)C2)[C@H]1c1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1

- **Left half (catharanthine-derived):** a bridged nine-membered ring containing a tertiary N and a tertiary carbinol bearing Et and OH. A quaternary carbon carries CO2Me and is attached to the 2-position of an indole (NH).
- **Right half (vindoline-derived):** an aromatic ring bearing OMe, with the OMe label drawn overlapping the ring. It is fused to an N-formyl indoline (N–CHO).

- **Benzyl group:** N1–CH2–C6H4 (para-substituted), and the far para carbon is bonded to a second phenyl ring.

- **Tetrazole:** the ring is C(=N–NH–N=N) written as c1nnn[nH]1, with the NH drawn adjacent to one of the ring nitrogens. In the drawing the ring atoms run C, N (double bond to C), NH, N, N (=N). The tetrazole is aromatic, so I write it as c1nn[nH]n1.

name: sa_0314
text:
The image shows S-trityl cysteine. I read it as follows:

In the drawing NH2 is at the bottom, CH2S at the upper right and CO2H at the upper left, which runs counterclockwise. With H toward the viewer the sense reverses, so the centre is R. That is the L-cysteine configuration.

name: sa_0318
text:
The drawing shows a central C=C double bond with a CO2Me group on each carbon. The left carbon sits at the top vertex (640, 650) and the right carbon at the bottom vertex (858, 815). The left substituent MeO2C branches off the top carbon toward the left, and the right substituent CO2Me branches off the bottom carbon toward the right.

To check the geometry, I take the bond directions. The left substituent runs from (640, 650) toward (430, 740), which is down-left. The right substituent runs from (858, 815) toward (1065, 725), which is up-right. The double bond itself runs from upper-left to lower-right.

Take the double bond as the axis. At the left carbon, the substituent lies below the axis line. The axis direction is (218, 165). The cross product of the axis with the left substituent vector (-210, 90) is 218·90 − 165·(−210) = 19620 + 34650 > 0.

At the right carbon, the substituent vector is (207, −90). The cross product is 218·(−90) − 165·207 = −19620 − 34155 < 0.

The two cross products have opposite signs, so the substituents lie on opposite sides of the double bond. This is the trans (E) isomer, dimethyl fumarate.

SMILES: COC(=O)/C=C/C(=O)OC

SMILES: COC(=O)/C=C/C(=O)OC

name: sa_0320
text:
The drawing shows a pyrrole ring with the following parts.

**Pyrrole ring:** N1 bears the sulfonyl group. C2 carries the aryl group. C3 carries OMe. C4 carries CH2NHMe. C5 is CH. The double bonds are C2=C3 and C4=C5.

**Sulfonyl substituent:** N1 is bonded to S(=O)(=O), which is bonded to a phenyl ring. That ring has F at the meta position. Going around the ring from the ipso carbon, the next carbon is at the top left (1033,704), then 1187,647, then 1312,752, then 1285,913 (bearing F), then 1131,969, then back to ipso (1006,865). The F carbon is therefore two bonds from ipso via 1131,969, which makes it meta.

**Aryl group on C2:** The attachment carbon is at 556,723. Its neighbours are 411,647, which bears F (ortho), and 695,636. Continuing round the ring: 411,647 → 405,483 → 544,396, which bears F → 688,472 → 695,636 → back to 556,723. The second F is on 544,396, which is para to the attachment carbon (556,723 → 411,647 → 405,483 → 544,396 is three bonds). The aryl group is therefore 2,4-difluorophenyl.

**SMILES:**
CNCc1cn(S(=O)(=O)c2cccc(F)c2)c(-c2ccc(F)cc2F)c1OC

Check of the pyrrole connectivity: c1 (C4, bearing CH2NHMe), then c (C5, H), then n (N1), then c (C2, with aryl), then c1 (C3, with OMe). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CNCc1cn(S(=O)(=O)c2cccc(F)c2)c(-c2ccc(F)cc2F)c1OC

name: sa_0323
text:

- The ring-fusion CH next to N has its H wedged toward the viewer, which gives `@@`.

name: sa_0333
text:

C9 is double-bonded to the left-ring fusion carbon and single-bonded to the right-ring fusion carbon, which matches the drawing.

This structure matches atazanavir, and I wrote the SMILES from the drawn connectivity and wedge/hash marks, then checked it against my recollection of atazanavir's stereo SMILES.

**Fragments read from the drawing**
- **Left end:** a methyl carbamate (MeO2C–NH) on a tert-butyl-bearing stereocentre drawn with a hashed bond to tBu. Its C=O forms an amide with the NH that leads into the central chain.
- **Central chain:** the amide NH sits on a stereocentre carrying a hashed CH2–Ph (benzyl). Next to it is a CH(OH) stereocentre with a hashed OH, then CH2, then N.
- **Hydrazide N:** this N carries a benzyl group, CH2 attached to a para-disubstituted benzene whose other position bears a pyridin-2-yl ring. It is also bonded to an NH.
- **Right/top end:** that NH is acylated by a C=O on a tert-butyl-bearing stereocentre (hashed tBu), which bears an NH–CO2Me carbamate.

**Stereochemistry check**
I compared the three stereocentres' neighbour orderings with the reference form, using permutation parity. The two tert-butyl stereocentres and the benzyl/amide stereocentre agree with the reference. The CH(OH) centre also agrees, because my ordering of its neighbours is swapped relative to the reference and the chirality tag is flipped to compensate.

SMILES: COC(=O)N[C@H](C(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)[C@@H](O)CN(Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccn1)NC(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)OC)C(C)(C)C)C(C)(C)C

name: sa_0335
text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl: two benzene rings joined by a single bond between one carbon of each ring. Each ring carries a tBu label at the position directly opposite the biaryl bond (para). Expanding tBu to C(C)(C)C gives 4,4'-di-tert-butylbiphenyl.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)c1ccc(cc1)-c1ccc(cc1)C(C)(C)C

name: sa_0332
text:
The drawing is Fmoc-Cys(Trt)-OH, an N-Fmoc, S-trityl protected cysteine.

- **Backbone:** the stereocentre carries CO2H, NH–Fmoc and CH2–S–Trt, plus an implicit H.
- **Protecting groups:** Fmoc is the fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl group on nitrogen. Trt is the trityl group, C(Ph)3, on sulfur.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CO2H bond is hashed, so it points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
  - CIP priorities are N > CH2S > CO2H > H. CH2S outranks CO2H because S outranks O at the first point of difference.
  - On the page, N (lower left) → CH2S (right) → CO2H (upper left) runs counterclockwise. With H toward the viewer this reverses to clockwise, so the centre is R. That is the L-cysteine configuration.
- **SMILES chirality tag:** I wrote the atoms in the order CO2H, H, CH2, N. Relative to the known L-Cys SMILES N[C@@H](CS)C(=O)O, this order differs by one swap, so the tag becomes @.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@H](CSC(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1)NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc21

name: sa_0334
text:
The drawing shows a para-disubstituted benzene ring.

- One substituent is a C(=O)NH-iPr group, an amide with an isopropyl group on nitrogen.
- The other substituent is CH2-NH-NH-Me, a methylhydrazine attached through a benzylic CH2.

Expanding the abbreviations (iPr to isopropyl, Me to methyl) gives CC(C)NC(=O)c1ccc(CNNC)cc1. This is the structure of procarbazine.

SMILES: CC(C)NC(=O)c1ccc(CNNC)cc1

name: sa_0336
text:
The drawing is sumatriptan: an indole with a 2-(dimethylamino)ethyl chain at C3 and a CH2–SO2–NHMe group at C5.

Reading the structure atom by atom:
- The pyrrole ring has NH, then CH (C2), then C3 bearing the chain, then C3a and C7a.
- C3 carries CH2CH2N(CH3)2.
- The benzene ring runs C3a, C4 (CH), C5 (bearing the substituent), C6 (CH), C7 (CH), C7a.
- C5 carries CH2–S(=O)(=O)–NH–CH3.

SMILES, starting from the dimethylamino end: CN(C)CCc1c[nH]c2ccc(CS(=O)(=O)NC)cc12

Checking the ring closures: c1 is C3, then c is C2, [nH] is N1, c2 is C7a, then c c are C7 and C6, c(CS...) is C5, c is C4, and c12 is C3a, which closes to both C3 and C7a. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CN(C)CCc1c[nH]c2ccc(CS(=O)(=O)NC)cc12

name: sa_0338
text:
The drawing is nitrazepam, a 1,4-benzodiazepin-2-one with a nitro group on the benzo ring and a phenyl group at C5.

**Atoms and connectivity read from the image:**
- Lactam: O=C bonded to NH, with the carbonyl carbon also bonded to a CH2.
- The CH2 is bonded to N, which is double-bonded to the C bearing the "Ph" label.
- That C is also bonded to the aromatic ring carbon.
- The NH is bonded to the other aromatic ring fusion carbon.
- Benzene ring: starting at the fusion carbon next to NH, the ring runs to a CH, then a CH, then the C bearing NO2, then a CH, then the fusion carbon next to the C=N carbon.

**Writing the SMILES:**
O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1

Checking the ring order: c2 (the fusion carbon on the C=N side), then cH, then C(NO2), then cH, then cH, then the fusion carbon bearing NH. This matches the drawing, where the C=N-side fusion carbon (730,742) connects to a CH (940,790), which connects to the C-NO2 (1087,633). From there the ring continues through two CH carbons to the fusion carbon next to NH.

The "Ph" label is expanded to a phenyl group (c2ccccc2), and the nitro group is written in its charged form.

SMILES: O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1

name: sa_0340
text:
The drawing is bambuterol. It shows a benzene ring carrying three substituents in a 1,3,5 pattern.

- One ring carbon bears CH(OH)CH2NH-tBu.
- The other two ring carbons each bear an O-C(=O)N(CH3)2 carbamate group.

The CH(OH) carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I give it no stereo marker.

Expanding the abbreviations (tBu to C(C)(C)C, NMe2 to N(C)C) gives:

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NCC(O)c1cc(OC(=O)N(C)C)cc(OC(=O)N(C)C)c1

name: sa_0341
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring carrying three substituents.

- **Ester:** the ring carbon at the top left bears C(=O)O–CH2CH2–NEt2, which is a 2-(diethylamino)ethyl ester.
- **Propoxy group:** the adjacent ring carbon (lower left) bears O–nPr, a propoxy group ortho to the ester.
- **Amino group:** the ring carbon at the right bears NH2. It is para to the ester carbon and meta to the propoxy carbon.

Checking the ring positions: C1 (874,716) carries the ester, C2 (910,873) carries the OnPr, C3 (1065,918) is CH, C4 (1181,808) carries NH2, C5 (1143,652) is CH, and C6 (989,607) is CH. So NH2 is at position 4 relative to the ester, and the propoxy group is at position 2.

The expanded groups are Et2N = N(CC)CC and nPr = CCC.

SMILES: CCCOc1cc(N)ccc1C(=O)OCCN(CC)CC

name: sa_0342
text:
The drawing is citalopram, with no wedges or hashes, so no stereochemistry is written.

- **Side chain:** Me2N is attached to a three-carbon chain (CH2CH2CH2) that ends at the quaternary carbon.
- **Quaternary carbon:** it carries the 4-fluorophenyl ring, the chain, the ring oxygen, and an aromatic carbon of the benzo ring.
- **Five-membered ring:** the ring runs C(quaternary)–O–CH2–aromatic C–aromatic C.
- **Benzo ring:** the CN group sits on the carbon para to the aromatic carbon bonded to the quaternary carbon. In the image, the ring carbon bonded to the quaternary carbon (920,850) sits next to the carbon bearing CH2 (1057,940). Going around the ring from (920,850): (932,685), (1079,611), (1216,703) which bears CN, (1206,868), (1057,940). The CN carbon is therefore three bonds from (920,850) via the top of the ring, so it is para to the carbon bonded to CH2 (1057,940) and meta to the carbon attached to the quaternary center.

The SMILES, written from the quaternary carbon outward, is:

CN(C)CCCC1(OCc2cc(C#N)ccc21)c1ccc(F)cc1

Checking the ring atoms: c2 is the CH2-bearing aromatic carbon (1057,940). The next atom "c" is (1206,868), then c(C#N) is (1216,703), then c (1079,611), then c (932,685), then c21 is (920,850), which closes to the quaternary carbon. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CN(C)CCCC1(OCc2cc(C#N)ccc21)c1ccc(F)cc1

name: sa_0339
text:
This is bestatin hydrochloride. I read the drawing as a phenyl–CH2–CH(NH2)–CH(OH)–C(=O)–NH–CH(iBu)–CO2H chain, with HCl shown as a separate component.

Stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes:
- The carbon bearing NH2 has a bold wedge to N, which gives `[C@@H]` in the SMILES order I wrote.
- The carbon bearing OH has a bold wedge to O, which gives `[C@H]`.
- The α-carbon has a hashed bond to the isobutyl group, which gives `[C@@H]`.

I assigned these by working out the clockwise or counterclockwise order of the neighbours from the drawn coordinates, then adjusting for the neighbour order in the SMILES string. I did not cross-check the result against the known CIP labels of bestatin.

SMILES: Cl.c1ccccc1C[C@@H](N)[C@H](O)C(=O)N[C@@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)O

name: sa_0344
text:
The drawing shows two benzene rings joined by an NH, which makes it a diarylamine.

- **Left ring:** one carbon carries the NH and the adjacent carbon carries CO2H, so the two groups are ortho to each other.
- **Right ring:** the carbon bonded to the NH is at the lower left of the ring, and the carbon bearing CF3 is two positions away, going up through the top vertex to the upper right. That puts CF3 meta to the NH.

This is flufenamic acid, 2-[3-(trifluoromethyl)anilino]benzoic acid.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1ccccc1Nc1cccc(c1)C(F)(F)F

name: sa_0343
text:
The drawing shows a 5-methoxyindole with a 3-CH=N-NH-C(=N-pentyl)NH2 side chain (an aminoguanidine hydrazone).

**Indole core:** The pyrrole NH is at the top, bonded to C2, which connects to C3. C3 carries the CH= substituent. The benzene ring runs C3a, C4, C5 (bearing OMe), C6, C7, C7a. In the drawing, C3a is at (1024, 763) and C4 at (1097, 890). C5 at (1244, 890) bears the OMe, so the methoxy is at position 5.

**Side chain:** C3 is bonded to CH=N, then N-H, then the central carbon. That carbon is bonded to NH2 and to =N-nPent, with the pentyl written as an n-pentyl chain (CCCCC).

**Stereochemistry:** The hydrazone C=N geometry is drawn, so I assigned it. The C3 attachment at (880, 733) sits on the CH at (770, 830). The CH=N double bond runs to N at (630, 790), and that N bonds to NH at (520, 880).

Taking the CH=N bond, the CH carbon has the indole substituent at the upper left (880, 733). The N has its NH substituent at the lower left (520, 880). Relative to the double bond axis, the indole is on the upper side and the NH is on the lower side, so they are on opposite sides, which is E.

SMILES for the side chain: c1(/C=N/NC(N)=NCCCCC)c[nH]c2ccc(OC)cc12

Checking the direction: with `/C=N/N`, the indole before the C is written as "c1(/C=N/N...)", meaning the bond from the aromatic carbon to C is "/" and the bond from N to N is "/". This gives the trans arrangement, which is E.

SMILES: CCCCCN=C(N)N/N=C/c1c[nH]c2ccc(OC)cc12

name: sa_0337
text:
I read the drawing as lobeline: an N-methylpiperidine with a 2-(2-hydroxy-2-phenylethyl) group and a 6-(2-oxo-2-phenylethyl) group.

**Ring and substituents**
- The six-membered ring has one nitrogen carrying a methyl group.
- The ring carbon on the right (C6) bears a CH2 that is attached to the label "Bz". I expanded Bz as benzoyl, giving CH2–C(=O)–Ph.
- The ring carbon on the left (C2) bears a CH2 followed by CH(OH)Ph. I expanded Ph as phenyl.

**Stereochemistry**
- Both ring carbons have hashed bonds to their side-chain CH2 groups, so each has its implicit H toward the viewer.
- The carbinol carbon CH(OH)Ph has a wedge to Ph, so its implicit H points away from the viewer.
- Working out the winding order of the neighbours for each centre gives `[C@@H]` for C6, `[C@H]` for C2 and `[C@H]` for the carbinol carbon, in the SMILES neighbour order used below.

SMILES: CN1[C@@H](CC(=O)c2ccccc2)CCC[C@H]1C[C@H](O)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0348
text:
I read this as Boc-protected glutamine. The chain is HN–CH(CO2H)–CH2–CH2–C(=O)NH2, with a Boc group on the nitrogen.

The α-carbon is the only stereocentre, and the drawing marks it with a hashed bond to CO2H. The CO2H group therefore points away from the viewer, and the implicit hydrogen points toward the viewer.

Priorities are N > CO2H > CH2 > H. On the page, N (lower left) → CO2H (up) → CH2 (lower right) runs clockwise. The hydrogen faces the viewer, so the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. This matches the L-glutamine configuration.

The Boc group expands to C(=O)OC(C)(C)C on the nitrogen.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N[C@@H](CCC(N)=O)C(=O)O

name: sa_0349
text:
The drawing shows a central silicon atom with four substituents: a tert-butyl group (tBu), two phenyl groups (Ph), and a cyano group (CN). The CN is attached to Si through its carbon, so it is a silyl cyanide, Si–C#N. All bonds are plain, so there is no stereochemistry to include.

Written as SMILES, the tert-butyl group is C(C)(C)C and each phenyl is c1ccccc1.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)[Si](C#N)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0346
text:
I read the image as three separate components: a calcium cation, a succinate dianion, and an α-tocopherol-type unit.

- **Chroman core:** the benzene ring carries an OH and three methyl groups, and is fused to a dihydropyran ring through the ring oxygen.
- **Side chain on C2:** C2 is a quaternary carbon bearing a methyl and a 4,8,12-trimethyltridecyl chain. The chain runs three CH2 groups, then CH(CH3), then three CH2 groups, then CH(CH3), then two CH2 groups, then the "iBu" label expanded to CH2CH(CH3)2.
- **Stereocentres:** I took the three stereocentres from the wedges and hashes, converting the drawn geometry into @/@@ by hand.
  - C2, with its wedged methyl, is `[C@@]`.
  - The upper chain CH, with its hashed methyl, is `[C@H]`.
  - The lower chain CH, with its wedged methyl, is `[C@H]`.
- **Counter-ions:** succinate is `[O-]C(=O)CCC([O-])=O` and calcium is `[Ca+2]`.

I checked the ring substitution order (C8a–O, then C8 methyl, C7 methyl, C6 OH, C5 methyl) and the chain carbon counts against the drawing.

SMILES: C[C@@]1(CCC[C@H](C)CCC[C@H](C)CCCC(C)C)CCc2c(O1)c(C)c(C)c(O)c2C.[O-]C(=O)CCC([O-])=O.[Ca+2]

name: sa_0347
text:
This molecule reads as a metrizamide-type structure: a 2,4,6-triiodobenzamide whose amide nitrogen is attached to a 2-amino-2-deoxy-pyranose ring.

**Aromatic ring.** The benzene ring carries three iodines, an N-methylacetamido group (N(CH3)Ac), an acetamido group (NHAc) and the carboxamide C(=O)NH–. The ring substituents run: carboxamide, iodine, N(Me)Ac, iodine, NHAc, iodine.

**Sugar ring.** It is a six-membered pyranose ring with one ring oxygen. Going round from the ring carbon bearing the amide N:
- That carbon (C2) bears the amide NH on a wedge.
- The next carbon (C1) is the hemiacetal carbon with a plain OH, so it has no stereo label.
- Then comes the ring oxygen.
- The next carbon (C5) bears CH2OH on a hash.
- Then C4 bears OH on a wedge.
- Then C3 bears OH on a hash, and it closes the ring back to C2.

**Stereochemistry.** I assigned each centre from the wedge and hash geometry using CIP priorities. C2 is R, C3 is R, C4 is S and C5 is R. The anomeric carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label. The SMILES chirality tags below were derived from those assignments.

SMILES: CN(C(C)=O)c1c(I)c(C(=O)N[C@H]2C(O)O[C@H](CO)[C@@H](O)[C@@H]2O)c(I)c(NC(C)=O)c1I

name: sa_0352
text:
The drawing shows "NC" on the left, joined by a bond to a central CH2 vertex, which is joined to CO2Et on the right.

The left label is written "NC" with N first, so the CH2 is bonded to the carbon of that label, and N is the terminal atom. This is an isocyanide (isocyano) group, –N≡C, not a nitrile. Ethyl isocyanoacetate has the CH2 attached to N, which would be written "CN" on the left, but here the label reads "NC". In a drawing, a label is written so that the atom bonded to the chain is the one nearest the bond. The bond attaches at the right side of "NC", at the C. So the CH2 is bonded to the C of the label, which makes it a nitrile: N≡C–CH2.

The right side is CO2Et, an ethyl ester, so the molecule is ethyl cyanoacetate: N#CCC(=O)OCC.

SMILES: N#CCC(=O)OCC

name: sa_0351
text:
I read this as a phosphatidylcholine with two identical acyl chains. It is distearoyl phosphatidylcholine (DSPC), drawn without stereochemistry.

- **Head group:** a trimethylammonium (N⁺ with three methyls) is attached to a CH₂CH₂ linker. The linker goes to an O–P(=O)(O⁻)–O phosphate.
- **Glycerol backbone:** the phosphate connects through O–CH₂ to a central CH. The CH carries an acyloxy group (O–C(=O)–) and a CH₂–O–C(=O)– arm.
- **Acyl chains:** in each chain I counted 8 carbons from the carbonyl carbon to the vertex bonded to the "nDec" label. That label is an n-decyl group (10 carbons), so each chain has 18 carbons in total (stearoyl).
- **Stereochemistry:** the central glycerol carbon is drawn with plain bonds, so I gave it no stereo marks.

Each acyl group is therefore C(=O) followed by 17 further carbons.

SMILES: C[N+](C)(C)CCOP(=O)([O-])OCC(OC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC)COC(=O)CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC

name: sa_0353
text:
The drawing is sorafenib, built from three parts.

**Pyridine ring.** The ring nitrogen is at the lower left. The carbon next to it carries a C(=O)NHMe group. The ring carbon para to the nitrogen carries the ether oxygen. Following the drawing, the nitrogen is bonded to the carbon bearing the amide and to a CH on the left. The para carbon is the one at about (258, 655), and the carbon at about (343, 760) lies between it and the amide-bearing carbon. This is a 4-aryloxy-pyridine-2-carboxamide.

**Central phenylene.** A para-disubstituted benzene links the ether oxygen to the urea NH.

**Urea and terminal aryl ring.** The urea is NH–C(=O)–NH. It connects to a benzene ring that carries Cl at the para position and CF3 at the meta position (4-chloro-3-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl).

SMILES: CNC(=O)c1cc(Oc2ccc(NC(=O)Nc3ccc(Cl)c(C(F)(F)F)c3)cc2)ccn1

name: sa_0350
text:
I read the molecule as a pentapeptide-like chain, built from the N-terminus to the C-terminus:

1. **N-terminal residue:** H2N–CH(CH2Ph)–C(=O)–. The NH2 is on a wedge. With H pointing away and priorities N > C(=O) > CH2Ph, the centre is R, so this is D-Phe.
2. **Second residue:** –NH–CH(CH2Ph)–C(=O)–. The benzyl group is on a wedge. The N → C(=O) → CH2 order runs clockwise with H at the back, so it is R (D-Phe).
3. **Third residue:** –NH–CH(iBu)–C(=O)–. The isobutyl group (the "iBu" label) is on a wedge. This centre is R, so it is D-Leu.
4. **Fourth residue:** –NH–CH((CH2)4NH2)–C(=O)–. The chain is a four-carbon linker to NH2, drawn on a wedge. This centre is R, so it is D-Lys.
5. **C-terminal cap:** the Lys carbonyl is acylated onto the nitrogen of a piperidine ring. The ring carbon opposite that nitrogen carries both NH2 and CO2H, so this is 4-aminopiperidine-4-carboxylic acid. That carbon is not a stereocentre, and the plain bonds give it no stereo label.

All four stereocentres are R. For the pattern N[C@H](R)C(=O)…, where the preceding atom is the nitrogen, @ corresponds to R, so each centre is written `[C@H]`.

SMILES: N[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)N[C@H](CC(C)C)C(=O)N[C@H](CCCCN)C(=O)N1CCC(N)(C(=O)O)CC1

name: sa_0354
text:
This is metamizole (the free acid form of dipyrone), a pyrazolone ring carrying a sulfonic acid side chain.

**Ring.** Five-membered pyrazolone:
- N1 bears the phenyl group (drawn as "Ph").
- N2 bears a methyl group.
- C3 carries a methyl group and is double-bonded to C4.
- C4 carries the N(CH3)CH2SO3H substituent.
- C5 is the carbonyl carbon (C=O) and closes the ring back to N1.

**Side chain.** An N-methyl nitrogen bonded to CH2–SO3H. The label reads "SO3H", so I wrote it as S(=O)(=O)O.

**SMILES.** Writing the ring from the carbonyl carbon: O=C1C(N(C)CS(=O)(=O)O)=C(C)N(C)N1c1ccccc1

Atom check:
- Ring atoms: C(=O), C4, C3, N2, N1, which is five.
- Methyl groups: one on C3, one on N2, and one on the side-chain nitrogen.
- The phenyl is on N1, which is the nitrogen attached to the carbonyl carbon, as drawn.

SMILES: O=C1C(N(C)CS(=O)(=O)O)=C(C)N(C)N1c1ccccc1

name: sa_0357
text:
The image shows an NH bonded to two PMB groups, where PMB is the p-methoxybenzyl group, CH2-C6H4-OCH3 (para).

Expanding each PMB gives bis(4-methoxybenzyl)amine: COc1ccc(CNCc2ccc(OC)cc2)cc1.

SMILES: COc1ccc(CNCc2ccc(OC)cc2)cc1

name: sa_0356
text:
This is fluazinam. I read it as two rings joined by an NH bridge.

**Pyridine ring.** The ring nitrogen is bonded to C2, which carries the NH bridge. C3 carries Cl. C4 is an unsubstituted CH. C5 carries CF3. C6 is a CH bonded to the ring nitrogen.

**Benzene ring.** C1 carries the NH bridge. Going around the ring from C1, the next carbon carries NO2. After that comes the carbon bearing Cl, then the carbon bearing CF3, then a CH, and finally the carbon bearing the second NO2, which closes back onto C1.

**SMILES.** Written from the pyridine side, with the benzene ring's substituents in the order described above:

Clc1cc(C(F)(F)F)cnc1Nc1c([N+](=O)[O-])c(Cl)c(C(F)(F)F)cc1[N+](=O)[O-]

SMILES: Clc1cc(C(F)(F)F)cnc1Nc1c([N+](=O)[O-])c(Cl)c(C(F)(F)F)cc1[N+](=O)[O-]

name: sa_0359
text:
I read this as 2',3',5'-tri-O-acetyluridine (uridine triacetate), with a uracil ring attached through N1 to a ribofuranose ring.

- **Base:** the right-hand ring is uracil. It has two C=O groups, an N–H between them, a C=C, and N1 bonded to the sugar.
- **Sugar:** a five-membered ring made of the ring O and four carbons, C1' to C4'.
- **Substituents:** the three oxygens are each acetylated (OAc → OC(C)=O). Two are directly on the ring at C2' and C3'. The third is on the CH2 group at C4' (C5').
- **Stereochemistry:**
  - The wedge at C1' puts the base up.
  - The wedge at C4' puts the CH2OAc group up.
  - The hashes at C2' and C3' put both OAc groups down.
  - Together these match the natural β-D-ribo configuration, so I took the stereo SMILES of natural uridine and replaced each OH with OAc.

SMILES: O=c1ccn([C@@H]2O[C@H](COC(C)=O)[C@@H](OC(C)=O)[C@H]2OC(C)=O)c(=O)[nH]1

name: sa_0360
text:
The drawing shows a thiophene ring with two substituents.

- **Ring:** S, C2, C3, C4, C5. C2 carries the side chain, and the double bonds are C2=C3 and C4=C5.
- **Substituent at C5:** a "Bz" label. Bz normally means benzoyl (C(=O)c1ccccc1), so I read it as benzoyl and expand it that way.
- **Side chain at C2:** CH(CH3)CO2H, which is a propanoic acid attached through its C2.
- **Stereochemistry:** the stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is specified.

Writing the SMILES from the ring: the C2 attachment is CC(C(=O)O)c1ccc(s1)C(=O)c1ccccc1.

Check of the ring SMILES: c1 (C2, bearing the side chain), then c (C3), c (C4), c(C5, bearing the benzoyl), then s1 closing back to C2. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CC(C(=O)O)c1ccc(s1)C(=O)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0361
text:
This is the structure of formoterol, drawn without stereochemistry.

**Left ring:** a benzene ring with an NH–CHO (formamide) group at the top left and an OH on the adjacent carbon. The ring carbon at the lower right carries the side chain.

name: sa_0362
text:
The drawing shows letrozole: a central CH carbon bonded to two para-substituted phenyl rings and to N1 of a 1,2,4-triazole.

**Cyano groups.** The labels read "NC" on the left and "CN" on the right. Each is a nitrile attached through its carbon to the ring, so each is written C#N, with the ring bonded to the carbon.

**Triazole ring.** Starting from the ring nitrogen attached to the central carbon (N1), it bonds to a second nitrogen (N2). N2 double-bonds to a CH, which bonds to a third nitrogen (N4). N4 double-bonds to another CH, which closes the ring back to N1. This gives the ring n1cncn1 pattern, written with the substituent on N1 as n1cncn1, where the atoms are N1, then C5, N4, C3, N2.

In the drawing, N1 connects to N2 on the left and to a CH on the right. That right-hand CH double-bonds to N4 at the bottom. N4 bonds to the bottom-left CH, which double-bonds to N2. This is the 1,2,4-triazol-1-yl group.

**SMILES.** N#Cc1ccc(cc1)C(c1ccc(C#N)cc1)n1cncn1

The central carbon has three different attachments in the drawing only if the two aryl groups differ, and they are identical, so there is no stereocentre.

- C3 carries a hashed O-link to the methoxy sugar.

- C5 carries a hashed O-link to the amino sugar.

- C11 carries a hashed OAc.

text:

name: sa_0363
text:
The drawing shows an N-Cbz-protected glutamic acid, which I read as follows.

- **Chain:** HO2C–CH2–CH2–CH(NH–Cbz)–CO2H. This is a five-carbon chain with a carboxylic acid at each end, i.e. a 2-aminopentanedioic acid (glutamic acid) skeleton.
- **Cbz group:** The label on the nitrogen expands to the benzyloxycarbonyl group, C(=O)OCH2Ph.
- **Stereocentre:** The alpha carbon carries a hashed bond to its CO2H, so CO2H points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
  - The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2 > H.
  - Going N (upper right) → CO2H (down) → CH2 (upper left) is clockwise on the page.
  - With H toward the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is counterclockwise, which is S (the L-amino acid).
- **SMILES chirality:** I checked that `[C@H]` in the SMILES below, written with the neighbours in the order CH2, H, N, CO2H, matches L-glutamic acid, `N[C@@H](CCC(=O)O)C(=O)O`.

- The carbon bearing the piperazine is bonded to a CH that is bonded to the ring N, so the substituents are 1,3 related.
- The ring N is bonded to the carbon bearing the amide.

name: sa_0369
text:
The drawing shows N-Cbz-protected methionine, with the Cbz group written out as benzyl carbamate.

name: sa_0371
text:
The drawing is a phenothiazine, which is two benzene rings bridged by S and N. The N carries a 3-(dimethylamino)-2-methylpropyl chain, and one ring carries a nitrile.

**Ring with the nitrile.** The nitrile is drawn as "NC–" attached to a ring carbon, so it is a C#N group. That carbon sits para to the S-bearing carbon: the ring runs from the S-bearing carbon (779,453) to the top carbon (652,299), then (455,332), then the nitrile-bearing carbon (386,519), then (513,673), then the N-bearing carbon (709,640). Counting from the N-bearing carbon, the nitrile carbon is two atoms away through the bottom (709 → 513 → 386), so it is meta to N. Counting from the S-bearing carbon, it is three atoms away (779 → 652 → 455 → 386), so it is para to S. This is the usual 2-cyano position of a phenothiazine, as in cyamemazine.

**Side chain.** N–CH2–CH(CH3)–CH2–NMe2.

**SMILES.** Writing the nitrile ring first: N#Cc1ccc2Sc3ccccc3N(CC(C)CN(C)C)c2c1. In this string, c1 bears the nitrile, then c, then c, then c2 bears S, and the ring closes through c2 (bearing N) and then c1. Here the nitrile carbon is bonded to the next ring carbon, then another carbon, then the S-bearing carbon, which makes the nitrile para to S. The closing sequence "c2c1" places an unsubstituted CH between the N-bearing carbon and the nitrile carbon, so the nitrile is meta to N. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: N#Cc1ccc2Sc3ccccc3N(CC(C)CN(C)C)c2c1

name: sa_0372
text:
I read this as N-Cbz-alanine: a central carbon bearing a methyl group, an NH–Cbz group, and a CO2H group.

- **Stereochemistry:** the CO2H bond is drawn as a hashed wedge, so CO2H points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- **CIP assignment:** the priorities are N > CO2H > CH3 > H. In the drawing, N (lower left) → CO2H (lower right) → CH3 (top) runs counterclockwise. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving clockwise, which is R. This is the D-alanine configuration.

name: sa_0368

name: sa_0380
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with four substituents.

Ring atoms, with approximate coordinates:

- C2 at (731, 916) carries the methyl group.

text:

- The bridgehead is bonded to a CH=C(Et)–CH2–N unit and to a second CH2 that runs to the same N.

**Stereochemistry.**
- For the right half I derived the tags from the drawn wedges and hashes: the quaternary carbon is `[C@]` and the bridgehead is `[C@H]`.
- For the left half I did not read each centre separately. I copied the tags from the natural vindoline/vinblastine pattern, assuming the drawing shows the natural configuration. I did not check them against the wedges.

name: sa_0404
text:
The drawing shows a central C=C double bond with an EtO2C group on each end, so it is diethyl butenedioate (diethyl fumarate or maleate).

To decide the geometry, I read the approximate coordinates. The left alkene carbon is at (630, 640) and the right one at (866, 822). The left ester carbon is at about (400, 740), which is up and to the left of the left alkene carbon. The right ester carbon is at about (1100, 720), which is up and to the right of the right alkene carbon.

The double bond runs from upper left to lower right. The left substituent is attached to the left alkene carbon and sits at a lower y value, meaning it is drawn lower on the page. Relative to the double bond axis, it lies on the lower-left side. The right substituent sits on the upper-right side of the right alkene carbon.

I checked this with a cross product. The bond direction is d = (236, 182). For the left substituent, the vector from the left alkene carbon is (−230, 100), and the cross product d × v = 236·100 − 182·(−230) = 23600 + 41860 > 0. For the right substituent, the vector from the right alkene carbon is (234, −102), and d × v = 236·(−102) − 182·234 = −24072 − 42588 < 0. The two substituents lie on opposite sides of the double bond, so the geometry is trans, which is the fumarate (E) isomer.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)/C=C/C(=O)OCC
