**Pyridine ring.** The ring nitrogen is at the top right. The carbon next to it (at about 1058,652) carries the NH substituent. The next carbon (at about 1072,855) carries the CO2H group, so the acid sits at position 3 and the NH at position 2. This is a 2-anilinonicotinic acid.

**Benzene ring.** The ring carbon attached to NH is at about 706,678. Going around the ring, the next vertex (522,589) is unsubstituted, and the one after that (353,704) carries the CF3 group. So the CF3 is meta to the NH.

**SMILES.** The acid is OC(=O)c1cccnc1, with the NH at the carbon adjacent to the ring nitrogen. The aryl group is c1cccc(c1)C(F)(F)F, attached through N. Combined:

OC(=O)c1cccnc1Nc1cccc(C(F)(F)F)c1

This matches the structure of niflumic acid.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccnc1Nc1cccc(C(F)(F)F)c1

name: sa_0413
text:
The drawing shows a urea core, with a carbonyl carbon double-bonded to O and bonded to two NH groups. One NH carries Ts (tosyl) and the other carries nBu (n-butyl).

Expanding the abbreviations:
- Ts is the tosyl group, S(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1.
- nBu is the n-butyl group, CCCC.

Joining these through the urea core gives CCCCNC(=O)NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1, which matches the drawing atom for atom. The drawing shows no wedges, hashes or cis/trans geometry, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: CCCCNC(=O)NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1

name: sa_0412
text:
I read the structure in four pieces and then joined them at the central nitrogen.

- **Left ester:** the O is attached to a CH carrying two n-octyl groups, which makes a heptadecan-9-yl ester. Its carbonyl carbon is joined to a chain of 7 CH2 groups that ends at N. The acyl part is therefore an octanoate.
- **Nitrogen:** it is a tertiary amine carrying a 2-hydroxyethyl group (CH2CH2OH).
- **Right ester:** N is joined to 5 CH2 groups and then a C(=O), which is a hexanoate. The ester O is attached to a CH2 followed by n-decyl, which makes an undecyl ester (11 carbons in total).
- **Stereochemistry:** the drawing shows no wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry, so none is included.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCC(CCCCCCCC)OC(=O)CCCCCCCN(CCO)CCCCCC(=O)OCCCCCCCCCCC

name: sa_0414
text:
The drawing shows benztropine mesylate: a tropane-type bicyclic amine carrying a benzhydryl ether, drawn as a salt with methanesulfonic acid.

**Bicyclic core.** I numbered the ring atoms from the image:
- The N is bonded to a methyl group, to C1 (upper right, at about 1105,648) and to C5 (lower right, at about 1222,1030).
- C1 connects to C2 (860,692), then C3 (804,934), which bears the O, then C4 (986,1103), then C5.
- C1 also connects to C7 (1352,652), which connects to C6 (1425,888), which connects to C5.

This gives a seven-membered ring through N, C1–C2–C3–C4–C5 and a five-membered ring through C1, C7, C6, C5 and N. This is the tropane skeleton (8-azabicyclo[3.2.1]octane). The bridgeheads are C1 and C5. The two-carbon bridge is C7–C6. The three-carbon bridge is C2–C3–C4. The N is the one-atom bridge.

**Substituent.** C3 carries an O attached to CH(Ph)Ph.

**Stereochemistry.** The drawing has no wedges or hashes, so I left stereochemistry out.

**Salt component.** The methanesulfonic acid is written CS(=O)(=O)O and is separated from the amine with a dot.

SMILES: CN1C2CCC1CC(C2)OC(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1.CS(=O)(=O)O

name: sa_0415
text:
The drawing shows a central C=C double bond. Each alkene carbon carries two substituents drawn as "NC" (left side) or "CN" (right side), so each is a nitrile group attached through carbon. The labels read NC and CN rather than the C≡N bond being drawn explicitly, but they are written with carbon next to the alkene, so each substituent is a cyano group, C#N.

This gives tetracyanoethylene. The four cyano groups are identical, so there is no stereochemistry to specify.

SMILES: N#CC(C#N)=C(C#N)C#N

name: sa_0417
text:
The drawing shows a central carbon with three Ph groups (top, left and bottom) and one OH group (right). All bonds are plain, so there is no stereochemistry.

Expanding each Ph to a phenyl ring (c1ccccc1) gives triphenylmethanol, with the central carbon bonded to the three rings and the hydroxyl oxygen.

SMILES: OC(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0407
text:
This structure is cefpirome. I read it region by region and worked out the stereochemistry from the drawn wedge and hash bonds.

- **Aminothiazole:** a 2-aminothiazol-4-yl ring (S, C–NH2, N, and two ring carbons).
- **Oxime:** a C=N–OMe group between the thiazole and the amide carbonyl. The OMe and the amide C=O are on the same side of the C=N, so it is the Z (syn) oxime. I wrote the thiazole as trans to OMe in the SMILES.
- **β-Lactam and dihydrothiazine core:** a cephem bicyclic core with a lactam C=O, an S in the six-membered ring, and a ring C=C bearing a carboxylate (COO⁻).
- **Stereocentres:** the NH-bearing carbon has a hashed bond to N, and the ring-fusion carbon has a wedged H. From these I assigned the NH-bearing carbon as `@` and the ring-fusion carbon as `@@` in the SMILES order below.
- **Side chain:** a CH2 on the ring C=C carries a pyridinium nitrogen. That pyridinium is fused to a cyclopentane (a 2,3-cyclopentenopyridinium) through the two carbons next to the ring junction.

SMILES: CO/N=C(/C1=CSC(N)=N1)C(=O)N[C@H]2[C@@H]3N(C2=O)C(=C(CS3)C[n+]4cccc5c4CCC5)C(=O)[O-]

name: sa_0418
text:
This drawing is Fmoc-protected tryptophan, with the Fmoc group on the α-amine, the free carboxylic acid, and the indole side chain.

**Stereochemistry:** The only stereo marker is the hashed bond from the α-carbon to the CO2H group. I assigned priorities N > CO2H > CH2(indolyl) > H. The hashed CO2H points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Viewed from the front, N → CO2H → CH2 runs clockwise. Because the H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, which gives counterclockwise, so the centre is S. This matches the natural L-tryptophan configuration.

**SMILES:** I wrote the chirality tag by converting from the known L-Trp form N[C@@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)C(=O)O. Starting with the carboxylic acid instead swaps the N and CO2H neighbours in the neighbour order, which flips @@ to @.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@H](Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12

name: sa_0419
text:
I read this as valsartan, with the tetrazole drawn as the 2H-tautomer, so the SMILES below uses that form.

- **Left side:** an n-butyl group (nBu) is attached to a carbonyl (C=O), which is bonded to the nitrogen as a pentanoyl amide.
- **Stereocentre:** the nitrogen is bonded to a carbon bearing an isopropyl group on a wedge, a CO2H group and an implicit hydrogen. Ranking the substituents N > CO2H > iPr > H, with H pointing away from the viewer, the order N → CO2H → iPr runs counterclockwise. That makes the centre S, which is written `[C@@H]` when the SMILES is ordered N, H, iPr, COOH.
- **Linker and rings:** the nitrogen is also bonded to a CH2, which leads to a para-substituted benzene ring. That ring is joined to a second, ortho-substituted benzene ring (a biphenyl), and that ring carries the tetrazole.
- **Tetrazole:** the ring is C(=N–N=N–NH), with the NH adjacent to the carbon-bearing nitrogen. I wrote it in the form `c1nnn[nH]1`.

SMILES: CCCCC(=O)N(Cc1ccc(cc1)-c1ccccc1-c1nnn[nH]1)[C@@H](C(C)C)C(O)=O

name: sa_0421
text:
The drawing is thimerosal: an ethyl group bonded to mercury, mercury bonded to sulfur, sulfur on a benzene ring, a carboxylate ortho to the sulfur, and a sodium counterion.

- **Ring:** six vertices. The sulfur sits on one carbon and COO⁻ on the adjacent carbon, so they are ortho. The ring is drawn with three double bonds (aromatic).
- **Chain:** Et–Hg–S, with S attached to the ring.
- **Charges:** COO⁻ is written as C(=O)[O-], with Na⁺ as a separate ion.

SMILES: CC[Hg]Sc1ccccc1C(=O)[O-].[Na+]

SMILES: CC[Hg]Sc1ccccc1C(=O)[O-].[Na+]

name: sa_0416
text:
The drawing is podophyllotoxin: a trimethoxyphenyl group on a tetralin core fused to a methylenedioxy ring and a γ-lactone, with a secondary alcohol. I wrote the SMILES by tracing the connectivity and then assigning each of the four stereocentres from its wedge or hash.

**Connectivity**
- The lactone is a five-membered ring made of C=O, ring O, CH2 and two ring-fusion CH carbons.
- The central six-membered ring contains the CHOH carbon, the two lactone-fusion CH carbons, the aryl-bearing CH and two fused aromatic carbons.
- A benzene ring is fused to this ring and carries a methylenedioxy bridge (OCH2O).
- The pendant aryl group is a 3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl.

**Stereochemistry**
I read each centre from the drawing and converted it to SMILES chirality by counting neighbour-order swaps.
- The CH next to CH2O has a hashed H, so it is `[C@H]2`.
- The CH next to the carbonyl has a wedged H, so it is `[C@H]1`.
- The aryl-bearing CH has a hashed aryl bond, so it is `[C@H]`.
- The CHOH carbon has a hashed OH, so it is `[C@@H]`.

SMILES: O=C1OC[C@H]2[C@H]1[C@H](c1cc(OC)c(OC)c(OC)c1)c1cc3OCOc3cc1[C@@H]2O

name: sa_0422
text:
This is nimesulide: a benzene ring carrying an NH–SO2–Me group, an O–Ph group and a nitro group.

Reading the labels, "MeO2S" is a methylsulfonyl group, CH3S(=O)(=O)–, attached to NH. "Ph" is attached to O, giving a phenoxy group. "NO2" is a nitro group.

Ring positions: the carbon bearing NH is C1. The adjacent carbon bearing OPh is C2. The next carbon, C3, is CH, and C4 carries NO2. The remaining ring carbons are CH.

The nitro-bearing carbon is the vertex at upper right (1097, 777). From the OPh carbon (722, 737), the path goes to the CH at (921, 649), then to the nitro carbon. The nitro group is therefore meta to OPh and para to NH, since NH sits at (700, 953) and the nitro carbon is opposite it. This matches nimesulide.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)Nc1ccc(cc1Oc1ccccc1)[N+](=O)[O-]

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)Nc1ccc(cc1Oc1ccccc1)[N+](=O)[O-]

name: sa_0424
text:
This structure is papaverine: an isoquinoline with a 3,4-dimethoxybenzyl group at C1 and methoxy groups at C6 and C7.

**Isoquinoline core.** C1 is bonded to N and to the CH2 linker. N is double-bonded to C1 and single-bonded to C3. C3=C4 is a double bond, and C4 joins the fused benzene ring at C4a. The other fusion atom, C8a, is bonded to C1.

**Benzo ring.** Going round from C8a, the ring is C8 (CH), C7 (OMe), C6 (OMe), C5 (CH), C4a. In the drawing, the OMe at the top is on the carbon next to C8, and the OMe at the right is on the next carbon. This gives 6,7-dimethoxy.

**Benzyl ring.** The ring carbon attached to CH2 sits between a CH and another CH. Its neighbours are one CH that leads to C(OMe), then a second C(OMe), and the ring is completed by two more CH atoms. This gives 3,4-dimethoxy.

**SMILES.** Writing the core as c1(Cc2ccc(OC)c(OC)c2)nccc2cc(OC)c(OC)cc12 gives:

COc1ccc(Cc2nccc3cc(OC)c(OC)cc23)cc1OC

No stereochemistry is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: COc1ccc(Cc2nccc3cc(OC)c(OC)cc23)cc1OC

name: sa_0420
text:
I read the molecule as prostaglandin E1 (PGE1), with the stereochemistry taken from the wedges and hashes in the drawing.

**Structure read from the image**
- **Acid chain:** a carboxylic acid (HO₂C) followed by six CH₂ groups, ending at the ring carbon that carries the chain (a wedged bond).
- **Ring:** a five-membered ring with a ketone (C=O) next to the chain-bearing carbon, then a CH₂, then a carbon with a wedged OH, then a carbon with a hashed bond to the side chain.
- **Side chain:** a trans C=C, then a CH(OH) drawn with a wedge to the n-pentyl group, which expands to CCCCC.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned each centre from the wedge and hash directions, with the implicit H opposite the wedge or hash. The double bond is trans, so it is written `/C=C/`.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCCCCC[C@H]1C(=O)C[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1/C=C/[C@@H](O)CCCCC

name: sa_0426
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with three isopropyl (iPr) groups on adjacent carbons: the bottom carbon and the lower-left and lower-right carbons. That makes it 1,2,3-triisopropylbenzene.

Each iPr group is written as C(C)C. The ring is c1ccc(C(C)C)c(C(C)C)c1C(C)C, which has six aromatic carbons, three of them adjacent and substituted, and three ring CH positions.

Checking the ring: the top carbon, the upper-left carbon and the upper-right carbon each carry a hydrogen. The lower-left, bottom and lower-right carbons carry the substituents. This matches the SMILES.

SMILES: CC(C)c1cccc(C(C)C)c1C(C)C

name: sa_0423
text:
I read the structure as an open-chain N-acetylhexosamine: CHO–CH(NHAc)–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH(OH)–CH2OH.

**Connectivity.** Going from right to left, the chain is:
- an aldehyde carbon (CHO);
- C2, bearing NHAc, where Ac expands to C(C)=O;
- C3, C4 and C5, each bearing an OH;
- a terminal CH2OH.

**Stereochemistry.** I assigned each centre from the drawn wedges and hashes, treating the implicit H as pointing opposite the wedged or hashed substituent.
- C2: NHAc is hashed, so H is toward the viewer. This gives `[C@H]` with neighbour order CHO, H, N, C3.
- C3: OH is wedged, so H is behind. This gives `[C@@H]` with neighbour order C2, H, O, C4.
- C4: OH is wedged, so H is behind. This gives `[C@H]` with neighbour order C3, H, O, C5.
- C5: OH is hashed, so H is in front. This gives `[C@H]` with neighbour order C4, H, O, C6.

SMILES: O=C[C@H](NC(C)=O)[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](O)CO

name: sa_0428
text:
The drawing shows a quaternary ammonium cation with a bromide counterion.

**Core.** The N+ and the bridgehead carbon are joined by three two-carbon bridges, which makes a 1-azoniabicyclo[2.2.2]octane (quinuclidinium). Each of the three bridges is drawn as two carbons:
- N–C–C–C4 (top path)
- N–C–C–C4 (middle path)
- N–C–C–C4 (bottom path)

**Substituents.**
- On N+ there is a CH2CH2O–Bn chain, which is a benzyloxyethyl group: N–CH2–CH2–O–CH2–Ph.
- On the bridgehead carbon (C4) there is a C(OH)(Ph)2 group, which is a diphenylhydroxymethyl group.

**SMILES assembly.**
- Ring and N-substituent: `[N+]12(CCOCc3ccccc3)CCC(CC1)(CC2)C(O)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1`
- Bromide counterion: `[Br-]`

The three bridges in this SMILES are the CC between N and C4 in the first branch, then CC1, then CC2, so the ring bookkeeping is consistent.

SMILES: [Br-].OC(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)C12CC[N+](CCOCc3ccccc3)(CC1)CC2

name: sa_0427
text:
I read this as Fmoc-L-glutamine with a trityl-protected side-chain amide, Fmoc-Gln(Trt)-OH.

- **Backbone:** The chain runs HO2C–CH(NH–Fmoc)–CH2–CH2–C(=O)–NH–Trt.
- **Fmoc:** I expanded it to the carbamate C(=O)OCH2-fluorenyl, written `C(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12`.
- **Trt:** I expanded it to triphenylmethyl, written `C(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1`.
- **Stereochemistry:** The only stereocentre is the α-carbon, with the CO2H on a hashed bond, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. The priorities are N > CO2H > CH2 > H. Viewed from the front, N (bottom) → CO2H (upper left) → CH2 (upper right) runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, I reverse this, which gives counterclockwise, so the centre is S (the L-amino acid). Writing the SMILES starting from the carboxyl group, this corresponds to `[C@H]`.

SMILES: O=C(O)[C@H](CCC(=O)NC(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1)NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12

name: sa_0429
text:
The image shows a central C=C double bond. Each alkene carbon carries two Ph (phenyl) groups, so the molecule is tetraphenylethylene.

Because the two substituents on each carbon are identical, the alkene has no E/Z isomerism, so no stereochemistry is needed.

SMILES: C(=C(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0431
text:
The drawing shows Boc–N=N–Boc, which is di-tert-butyl azodicarboxylate (DBAD).

Boc is the tert-butoxycarbonyl group, C(=O)OC(C)(C)C. Attaching one to each end of the N=N unit gives CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N=NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C.

The double bond is drawn with the two Boc groups on opposite sides of the N=N bond, which looks like trans (E) geometry. The two N–Boc bonds do run in a zigzag across the bond, so I include the E stereo marking: `/N=N/`.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)/N=N/C(=O)OC(C)(C)C

name: sa_0432
text:
The drawing shows a 3-cyanoquinoline core (the pelitinib/EKB-569 type of scaffold), here carrying a pyridylmethoxy-substituted anilino group.

**Quinoline core**
- Ring N is at the bottom, bonded to C2 (CH), then C3 (bearing CN), then C4 (bearing the NH-aryl group), then C4a.
- The benzo ring runs C4a, C5 (CH), C6 (NH-amide), C7 (OEt), C8 (CH), C8a.

**Substituents**
- The amide is NH–C(=O)–CH=CH–CH2–NMe2. The double bond has trans geometry as drawn, so it is written as E.
- The ethoxy group is on C7.
- The 4-NH links to a phenyl ring that carries Cl and the O–CH2–(2-pyridyl) group. Numbering from the NH-bearing carbon, Cl is at the meta position and the OCH2-pyridyl group is para.

**SMILES assembly**
- Amide side chain: CN(C)C/C=C/C(=O)N
- Quinoline: c1c(NC(=O)/C=C/CN(C)C)c(OCC)cc2ncc(C#N)c(Nc3ccc(OCc4ccccn4)c(Cl)c3)c12

Checking the ring closures: c1 is C5, then C6 (with the amide), C7 (OEt), C8 (cc2 gives C8 and then C8a), n, c (C2), c(C#N) (C3), c(NAr) (C4), and c12 (C4a) closes to C5 and C8a.

SMILES: CCOc1cc2ncc(C#N)c(Nc3ccc(OCc4ccccn4)c(Cl)c3)c2cc1NC(=O)/C=C/CN(C)C

name: sa_0430
text:
I read this as pivampicillin: the ampicillin penicillin core with a pivaloyloxymethyl ester. The pieces are:

- **Core:** a β-lactam fused to a thiazolidine ring, with a gem-dimethyl carbon next to the sulfur.
- **Ester:** the carboxyl group on the thiazolidine ring is esterified with –CH2–O–Piv, where Piv is pivaloyl, C(=O)C(CH3)3.
- **Side chain:** the amide NH on the β-lactam carries –C(=O)–CH(NH2)–Ph, the phenylglycyl group.

For stereochemistry, I checked the phenylglycine carbon directly against the drawing. Its priorities are N > C(=O) > Ph > H, with Ph hashed and the implicit H toward the viewer. That gives R, matching the D-phenylglycyl group of ampicillin. For the three bicyclic stereocentres I did not rederive each one from the wedges and hashes. I used the natural penicillin configuration (2S,5R,6R), written in the same pattern as the standard ampicillin SMILES with the ester substituted in.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)C(=O)OCOC(=O)[C@@H]1N2C(=O)[C@@H](NC(=O)[C@H](N)c3ccccc3)[C@H]2SC1(C)C

name: sa_0425
text:
I read the molecule as an anthracycline: a tetracyclic aglycone carrying a three-sugar chain at C1. I set stereochemistry from the wedges and hashes, working out each centre's handedness from the 2D coordinates.

**Aglycone**
- The ring system is a 1,4-dihydroxyanthraquinone-type chromophore with a further OH on the middle aromatic ring (peri to the top C=O) and two quinone C=O groups.
- The saturated ring has four substituted positions:
  - the O-glycosylated CH, drawn with a hashed bond;
  - a CH2;
  - a quaternary C bearing OH and Et, with Et on a wedge;
  - a CH bearing CO2Me on a wedge.

**Sugar chain** (from the aglycone outward)
1. An amino sugar (rhodosamine-type): ring O, C-methyl on a wedge, NMe2 on a wedge, and an O-glycosyl group on a wedge at C4.
2. A 2-deoxy sugar with a 3-OH on a wedge and a 4-O-glycosyl link on a wedge, plus a wedged C-methyl.
3. A terminal 2-deoxy sugar with two wedged OH groups and a wedged C-methyl.

The glycosidic C1–O bonds are all hashed. I wrote @/@@ for each centre from the drawn geometry, with the implicit H taken as pointing opposite the wedged or hashed substituent.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(O)C[C@H](O[C@H]5C[C@H](N(C)C)[C@H](O[C@H]6C[C@H](O)[C@H](O[C@H]7C[C@H](O)[C@H](O)[C@H](C)O7)[C@H](C)O6)[C@H](C)O5)c2c(O)c3C(=O)c4c(O)ccc(O)c4C(=O)c3cc2[C@H]1C(=O)OC

name: sa_0434
text:
I read the structure as follows.

- **Core:** a piperidine whose ring nitrogen carries a urea carbonyl, C(=O)N(CH3)–CH(CH3)–aryl.
- **Urea side chain:** the aryl group is 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl. The CH(CH3) carbon has a wedged methyl.
- **Piperidine C2:** carries a 4-fluoro-2-methylphenyl group on a hashed bond.
- **Piperidine C4:** carries a piperazine nitrogen on a hashed bond. The distal piperazine nitrogen is acetylated (Ac expanded to C(C)=O).

I assigned the three stereocentres from the wedge and hash directions and the 2D coordinates. The side-chain CH(CH3) is `[C@H]`, piperidine C4 is `[C@H]`, and piperidine C2 is `[C@@H]`.

SMILES: O=C(N(C)[C@H](C)c1cc(C(F)(F)F)cc(C(F)(F)F)c1)N1CC[C@H](N2CCN(C(C)=O)CC2)C[C@@H]1c1ccc(F)cc1C

name: sa_0435
text:
The drawing shows "NC" on the left, joined by a bond to a zigzag chain of two CH2 carbons, which ends in SO2Me on the right.

The label is written "NC" with the N on the left and the C attached to the chain. Read literally, that is an isocyanide, with the carbon bonded to the CH2 and the N at the far end. This image resembles the Sigma-Aldrich drawing of 2-(methylsulfonyl)acetonitrile or 3-(methylsulfonyl)propionitrile, where the label would normally be NC, meaning a nitrile drawn with the N first.

Counting the chain: the bond from NC goes to a vertex, then to a second vertex, then to the S. That gives two CH2 carbons between the cyano group and the sulfone, so the nitrile carbon is a third carbon. The molecule is NC-CH2-CH2-SO2-CH3, which is 3-(methylsulfonyl)propanenitrile.

The label could also be read as an isocyanide, but a nitrile is the usual meaning of "NC" in such drawings, so I take it as the nitrile.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)CCC#N

name: sa_0437
text:
The drawing is cangrelor as its tetrasodium salt. I read it region by region:

- **Purine core:** an adenine-type ring system. C2 carries an S–CH2–CH2–CF3 group, and C6 carries an NH–CH2–CH2–S–CH3 group.
- **Sugar:** a ribofuranose attached to N9 by a wedged bond. The CH2O group is wedged and both OH groups are hashed. This matches the natural β-D-ribo configuration, so I used the stereo pattern of adenosine.
- **Phosphate chain:** the 5'-O is bonded to P(=O)(O⁻), then to O, then to P(=O)(O⁻), then to a CCl2 carbon, then to a terminal P(=O)(O⁻)(O⁻). This is a dichloromethylene bisphosphonate, so the chain carries four negative charges.
- **Counterions:** four Na⁺.

SMILES: CSCCNc1nc(SCCC(F)(F)F)nc2c1ncn2[C@@H]1O[C@H](COP(=O)([O-])OP(=O)([O-])C(Cl)(Cl)P(=O)([O-])[O-])[C@@H](O)[C@H]1O.[Na+].[Na+].[Na+].[Na+]

name: sa_0438
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with two adjacent substituents, so it is an ortho-disubstituted benzene.

- One substituent is CO2H, a carboxylic acid.
- The other is OAc, where Ac is acetyl (C(=O)CH3), so this group is an acetate ester, OC(C)=O.

The molecule is 2-acetoxybenzoic acid (aspirin). No wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry are drawn, so the SMILES carries no stereochemistry.

name: sa_0436

- The triazole wedge is drawn very long and overlaps other bonds. I assigned it to the lower carbon, the one with the H label.

**Uncertain points**

- The core carbon count I got is one short of what I would expect for an ibrexafungerp-type triterpenoid, so I may have missed a methyl. I followed the drawing as I read it.

**N1 substituent.** N1 is bonded to a CH2 that leads to a benzene ring. Going around that ring from the attachment carbon (C1):
- C1 is attached to the CH2.
- The next carbon, C2, bears CF3.
- C3 is CH.
- C4 bears the SO2Me group.
- C5 and C6 are CH.

**Check on the fused ring.** In c2ncccc12, c2 is C7a, then N, then three CH carbons, then C3a, which closes both rings. This is correct.

- At the CH(Et) carbon, the ethyl wedge puts the implicit H behind the page. The ring carbon, ethyl and aryl then run counterclockwise when viewed from the front. With the neighbour order ring C, H, Et, aryl, this gives `@`.

text:

- **Amine:** the NH2 sits on the pyridine-like ring carbon next to the ring nitrogen.
- **C2 substituent:** an n-butyl group on the imidazole carbon (CCCC).
- **N1 substituent:** an N–O bond to a chain of four CH2 groups ending in NH–C(=O)–.

The acyl chain, counted vertex by vertex, is the carbonyl carbon, then 7 chain carbons, then the nDec label (10 carbons). That makes an 18-carbon acyl group (octadecanamide). No wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry are drawn, so there is no stereochemistry.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC(=O)NCCCCON1C(CCCC)=Nc2c(N)nc3ccccc3c21

name: sa_0464
text:
The image shows a benzene ring with an OH group at the bottom vertex. The two ring carbons adjacent to it each carry an isopropyl group, labeled iPr. This is 2,6-diisopropylphenol (propofol).

Expanding each iPr into CC(C)- gives the SMILES below.

SMILES: CC(C)c1cccc(C(C)C)c1O

name: sa_0466
text:
The drawing shows Fmoc-glycine: HO2C–CH2–NH–Fmoc.

Fmoc is the 9-fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl group, C(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12. It attaches to nitrogen through the carbonyl carbon, so the nitrogen carries a carbamate.

Written out, the molecule is OC(=O)CNC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12.

Atom check: the glycine part is the carboxylic acid carbon plus the CH2, the nitrogen carries one H, and the carbamate carbonyl and oxygen link to the CH2 of the fluorenyl group. The fluorene core is a five-membered ring joined to two benzene rings. No stereochemistry is drawn.

SMILES: OC(=O)CNC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12

name: sa_0465
text:
I read this as remdesivir. I matched it to the known SMILES for that drug rather than assigning each stereocentre independently from the wedges and hashes, so the stereo tags are not independently verified.

- **Left end:** a 2-ethylbutyl ester, written CCC(CC)CO–C(=O).
- **Amino acid unit:** an alanine unit, C(=O)–CH(CH3)–NH, with the methyl on a wedge.
- **Phosphorus centre:** P(=O) carries the NH, a phenoxy group (Ph–O) and an O–CH2 link to the sugar. The N–P bond is drawn hashed.
- **Sugar:** a five-membered ring (one O, four C) with the CH2O substituent on a wedge, two hashed OH groups, and a quaternary carbon bearing a hashed C≡N and the heteroaryl group.
- **Heteroaryl base:** a pyrrolo[2,1-f][1,2,4]triazine with an NH2 on the triazine ring, joined to the sugar through the pyrrole carbon.

SMILES: CCC(CC)COC(=O)[C@H](C)N[P@](=O)(OC[C@@H]1[C@H]([C@H]([C@](O1)(C#N)C2=CC=C3N2N=CN=C3N)O)O)OC4=CC=CC=C4

name: sa_0467
text:
The drawing shows epinephrine with both phenolic hydroxyls protected as pivalate esters (PivO = OC(=O)C(CH3)3).

- **Ring:** a benzene ring carrying a CH(OH)CH2NHMe side chain, with a PivO group on each of two adjacent ring carbons.
- **Side chain:** the ring carbon at the right connects to CH(OH), then CH2, then NHMe.
- **Stereochemistry:** all bonds are plain, with no wedges or hashes, so no stereo is specified.
- **Pivalate groups:** each PivO is written as OC(=O)C(C)(C)C.

Writing the SMILES from the side chain through the ring:

CNCC(O)c1ccc(OC(=O)C(C)(C)C)c(OC(=O)C(C)(C)C)c1

The ring atoms are c1 (bearing the side chain), c, c, c(OPiv), c(OPiv), and c1. This places the two PivO groups on adjacent carbons at the 3 and 4 positions relative to the side chain, which matches the drawing.

SMILES: CNCC(O)c1ccc(OC(=O)C(C)(C)C)c(OC(=O)C(C)(C)C)c1

name: sa_0462
text:
This drawing is valbenazine, the L-valine ester of (+)-dihydrotetrabenazine. I read it as follows:

- **Core:** a benzo[a]quinolizine, which is a dimethoxy-substituted benzene ring fused to a tetrahydroisoquinoline-type ring and a second six-membered ring containing the nitrogen.
- **Substituents:** two aromatic OMe groups, an isobutyl group on the carbon next to the ring CH–O carbon, and an ester oxygen on the ring carbon bearing the wedge bond.
- **Ester side chain:** O–C(=O)–CH(NH2)–iPr, which is a valine residue.

I assigned the stereocentres from the wedges and hashes using CIP priorities:

- The ring-fusion carbon (hashed H, bonded to N) is R.
- The ester-bearing ring carbon (wedged O) is R.
- The isobutyl-bearing ring carbon (hashed iBu) is R.
- The valine α-carbon (hashed iPr) is S, which is L-valine.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@H]1CN2CCC3=CC(=C(C=C3[C@@H]2C[C@@H]1OC(=O)[C@@H](C(C)C)N)OC)OC

name: sa_0470
text:
The drawing shows a central NH with an iPr (isopropyl) group on each side, so the molecule is diisopropylamine.

Expanding each iPr to CH(CH3)2 gives CC(C)NC(C)C. There are no stereocentres, charges or multiple bonds to add.

SMILES: CC(C)NC(C)C

name: sa_0469
text:
The image is mersalyl sodium, drawn as separate ions: a mercury cation, a carboxylate anion, a sodium cation and a hydroxide anion.

Reading the structure region by region:
- **Mercury side chain:** Hg⁺ is bonded to a CH2. That CH2 is bonded to a CH bearing OMe (written as OC). The CH is bonded to another CH2, which is bonded to NH.
- **Amide and ring:** The NH is bonded to a C(=O), which is attached to a benzene ring. At the ortho position of the ring is an O–CH2–COO⁻ group.
- **Counterions:** Na⁺ and HO⁻ are drawn as separate fragments.

The CH carrying the OMe is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so I give it no stereo marking.

Writing the SMILES: [Hg+]CC(OC)CNC(=O)c1ccccc1OCC(=O)[O-].[Na+].[OH-]

SMILES: [Hg+]CC(OC)CNC(=O)c1ccccc1OCC(=O)[O-].[Na+].[OH-]

name: sa_0471
text:
The drawing shows HO2C–CH2–CH2–NH–Boc, which is Boc-β-alanine.

- The HO2C label is a carboxylic acid, C(=O)O.
- Two CH2 carbons follow, then NH, then Boc.
- Boc expands to C(=O)OC(C)(C)C.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCNC(=O)OC(C)(C)C

name: sa_0473
text:
The drawing shows an NH group bonded to two groups labelled "Tf". Tf is the triflyl group, CF3SO2, so the molecule is bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, HN(Tf)2.

Expanding each Tf gives S(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F, and joining the two through the nitrogen gives the SMILES below.

SMILES: O=S(=O)(NS(=O)(=O)C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F

name: sa_0472
text:
This is strontium ranelate: a thiophene ring carrying the substituents below, plus two Sr²⁺ counterions.

**Ring.** S is bonded to C2 (bearing COO⁻) and to C5 (bearing N). C2=C3, where C3 carries CH2COO⁻. C3–C4 is a single bond, and C4=C5. C4 carries the C#N group.

**Substituents.**
- C2: COO⁻
- C3: CH2COO⁻
- C4: C#N
- C5: N(CH2COO⁻)2

**SMILES.** Writing the ring starting from S: s1c(C(=O)[O-])c(CC(=O)[O-])c(C#N)c1N(CC(=O)[O-])CC(=O)[O-]

The charges balance: 4 carboxylates give −4, and 2 Sr²⁺ give +4.

SMILES: [Sr+2].[Sr+2].[O-]C(=O)CN(CC([O-])=O)c1sc(C([O-])=O)c(CC([O-])=O)c1C#N

name: sa_0475
text:
The drawing shows a central phosphorus atom (P) bonded by single bonds to three groups labeled Ph. Ph is phenyl, so the molecule is triphenylphosphine.

Expanding each Ph into a benzene ring attached to P gives P(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1. No stereochemistry is drawn, so none is included.

SMILES: P(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0468
text:
I read the structure region by region and wrote it as a SMILES string.

**Right side:** A methylsulfonyl group (CH3–SO2–) is attached through a CH2 to a C=O, which forms an amide with the nitrogen of an azetidine ring. The azetidine's carbon opposite the nitrogen is a spiro carbon that is also bonded to the ring oxygen of a 1,3-dihydroisobenzofuran (a CH2–O five-membered ring fused to a benzene).

**Middle:** On the benzene ring, the spiro-bearing carbon and the isoxazoline-bearing carbon are para to each other. The CH2-bearing carbon is meta to the isoxazoline carbon. The isoxazoline is a 4,5-dihydroisoxazole attached at C3 (C=N–O), with a CH2 at C4.

**Left side:** C5 of the isoxazoline carries a CF3 and a 3,5-dichloro-4-fluorophenyl group. It is the only stereocentre drawn with a wedge, and the wedge is on the CF3 bond.

**Stereochemistry:** With the CF3 pointing toward the viewer, the sequence O → ring CH2 → aryl runs counterclockwise on the page. Reordering to the SMILES neighbour order (O, CH2, aryl, CF3) is an odd permutation, so the centre is written `@@`.

SMILES: CS(=O)(=O)CC(=O)N1CC2(C1)OCc1cc(ccc12)C1=NO[C@@](C1)(c1cc(Cl)c(F)c(Cl)c1)C(F)(F)F

name: sa_0476
text:
The drawing shows a 1,2,4-triazole ring with three substituents.

**Triazole ring.** The atoms run N1 (bearing SEM), N2, C3, N4, C5. N1 connects to N2, which has a double bond to C3. C3 connects to N4, which has a double bond to C5, and C5 closes the ring back to N1.

**Substituents.**
- C5 carries the OCH2CF3 group.
- C3 carries the aryl group.
- N1 carries SEM (2-(trimethylsilyl)ethoxymethyl), which expands to CH2OCH2CH2Si(CH3)3.

**Aryl ring.** The ring carbon attached to the triazole has fluorine on one adjacent carbon. Going around the ring from that fluorine-bearing carbon, the next carbon is CH, then the carbon bearing Br, so Br is para to the triazole attachment. The ring is therefore 4-bromo-2-fluorophenyl.

**SMILES.** Writing the triazole as n1(SEM)nc(Ar)nc1OCC(F)(F)F in aromatic form gives:

C[Si](C)(C)CCOCn1nc(-c2ccc(Br)cc2F)nc1OCC(F)(F)F

I checked the atom count and connectivity against the drawing: the ring has n1, n, c, n, c1 (five atoms), and the aryl group reads c2ccc(Br)cc2F with F on the carbon next to the attachment point.

SMILES: C[Si](C)(C)CCOCn1nc(-c2ccc(Br)cc2F)nc1OCC(F)(F)F

name: sa_0474
text:
Reading the drawing:

- The central nitrogen carries three substituents: a methyl (drawn as a plain bond going up), a benzyl group (Bn, to the left), and a stereogenic carbon (below).
- That stereogenic carbon bears a hashed methyl, a CH2 that leads to Ph (phenyl), the nitrogen, and an implicit H.
- HCl is shown separately, so the compound is the hydrochloride salt.

Stereochemistry: the priorities at the stereocentre are N > CH2Ph > CH3 > H. The methyl is hashed (pointing away), so the implicit H points toward the viewer. In the drawing, N (upper left) → CH2 (right) → CH3 (lower left) runs clockwise. Because H faces the viewer, this reverses to counterclockwise, which gives the S configuration.

For the SMILES `C[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)N(C)Cc1ccccc1`, the neighbour order at the stereocentre is CH3, H, CH2, N. I worked out that `@` would encode R and `@@` encodes S, so I used `@@`.

SMILES: C[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)N(C)Cc1ccccc1.Cl

name: sa_0479
text:
The drawing shows MeO2C–CH2–OTBS, which is methyl (tert-butyldimethylsilyloxy)acetate.

- MeO2C is a methyl ester: COC(=O)–
- The vertex between the two labels is a CH2 carbon.
- OTBS is an oxygen bonded to a tert-butyldimethylsilyl group: O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C

Joined together, the SMILES is COC(=O)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C. There are no wedges, hashes or double-bond geometry in the drawing, so no stereochemistry is included.

SMILES: COC(=O)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C

name: sa_0458
text:
I read the drawing as a 16-membered macrocyclic depsipeptide, a cryptophycin-type structure. I traced it around the ring and assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash.

**Ring, traced from the gem-dimethyl carbon:**
- C(CH3)2, then CH2, then NH, then C(=O).
- The next carbon is a stereocentre bearing a CH2–aryl group (wedge). The aryl is 3-chloro-4-methoxyphenyl.
- Then NH, then C(=O), then a trans CH=CH.
- Then CH2, then an O-bearing stereocentre (wedge to the CH2).
- Then O, C(=O), and a stereocentre bearing isobutyl (hash), then O and C(=O), which closes back to the gem-dimethyl carbon.

**Side chain** on the O-bearing ring carbon: CH(CH3) (wedged methyl), then a phenyl-substituted epoxide.

**Stereochemistry, from the wedges and hashes:**
- Isobutyl carbon: S.
- O-bearing ring carbon: S.
- CH(CH3): S.
- Epoxide carbon next to CH(CH3): R.
- Phenyl-bearing epoxide carbon: R.
- Aryl-methyl carbon: R.
- The ring C=C is drawn with the CH2 and the C(=O) on opposite sides, so it is trans (E).

I converted each assignment to @/@@ for the atom order in the SMILES below.

SMILES: CC1(C)CNC(=O)[C@@H](Cc2ccc(OC)c(Cl)c2)NC(=O)/C=C/C[C@@H]([C@H](C)[C@H]2O[C@@H]2c2ccccc2)OC(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)OC1=O

name: sa_0481
text:
The drawing shows a 2-aminothiazole ring with a trityl-protected amine, an oxime ether and a carboxylic acid.

**Ring:** The ring atoms are S, C2, N3, C4 and C5. C2 carries the NH–Trt group. C2=N3 is a double bond, and C4=C5 is a double bond. C4 is attached to the side-chain carbon.

**Side chain:** C4 bonds to a carbon that bears CO2H and is double-bonded to N. That N bonds to O, which bonds to a quaternary carbon carrying two methyl groups and CO2tBu.

**Stereochemistry:** The C=N bond is drawn with defined geometry. I read the positions as follows:
- The ring carbon C4 sits at the upper left of the oxime carbon (857,889), and the CO2H sits below it.
- On the N side (1035,825), the O sits above it.
- The C=N bond runs from lower left to upper right. C4 is up-left of the oxime carbon, and CO2H is down from it.
- On the N, O is up and slightly left, in the direction of the "up" side of the bond.

For a bond running left to right, the ring carbon is on the upper side, which is the same side as O. The ring and the O-substituent are therefore cis (Z with respect to those two groups).

Priorities: on the oxime carbon, CO2H (C with O,O,O) outranks the thiazole C4 (C with N,C,C), so CO2H is the higher priority group. On N, O is the higher priority group. CO2H is on the opposite side from O, so the configuration is E.

**SMILES:** I write the double bond as C(/C(=O)O)(c1csc(NC(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)n1)=N/OC(C)(C)C(=O)OC(C)(C)C and check the geometry against the drawing.

Writing it as `OC(=O)/C(c1csc(n1)NC(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1)=N/OC(C)(C)C(=O)OC(C)(C)C`:
- `OC(=O)/C` means the bond from the CO2H carbon to the oxime carbon is "/", so CO2H is below the oxime carbon.
- `=N/O` means O is above N (the bond after N is "/", so O is above it).

CO2H is therefore on the opposite side from O, which is E and matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)/C(c1csc(n1)NC(c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1)=N/OC(C)(C)C(=O)OC(C)(C)C

name: sa_0482
text:
The drawing shows a central nitrogen with three labelled substituents: iPr, Bn and Piv.

- iPr (isopropyl) expands to CH(CH3)2.
- Bn (benzyl) expands to CH2Ph.
- Piv (pivaloyl) expands to C(=O)C(CH3)3.

The nitrogen is therefore a tertiary amide: N-benzyl-N-isopropylpivalamide.

SMILES: CC(C)N(Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)C(C)(C)C

name: sa_0477
text:
I read the structure as a 2(5H)-furanone (butenolide) joined by a trans CH=CH link to a decalin core. This looks like an andrographolide-type diterpenoid carrying an acetate and a TIPS-protected hydroxymethyl group.

**Ring and substituent reading**
- **Lactone:** the ring is O–C(=O)–C(=CH–CH2–O). Its ring carbon next to the C=O carries the vinyl chain.
- **Linker:** a trans CH=CH runs from the lactone to the decalin carbon (call it G) at the bottom-left of the decalin; the bond to G is a wedge.
- **Decalin, ring with the exocyclic alkene:** G is followed by C(=CH2), then two CH2 groups, then the ring-fusion CH. That fusion CH bears a hashed H.
- **Decalin, other ring:** from the ring-fusion CH it continues to the quaternary C with a hashed methyl and CH2OTIPS, then to the CH–OAc (wedge), then two CH2 groups back to the quaternary ring-fusion C with a wedged methyl.
- **Substituents:** OAc is expanded to OC(C)=O. OTIPS is expanded to O–Si(iPr)3.

**Stereocentres:** I assigned each @/@@ from the wedge and hash geometry in the drawing. There are five stereocentres: G, the CH–H fusion carbon, the methyl-bearing fusion carbon, the CH–OAc carbon, and the quaternary carbon bearing CH2OTIPS. The vinyl double bond is drawn trans, so it is written /C=C/.

I checked that the ring closures are consistent and that the lactone closes as a five-membered ring.

SMILES: O=C1OCC=C1/C=C/[C@@H]2C(=C)CC[C@H]3[C@@]2(C)CC[C@@H](OC(C)=O)[C@@]3(C)CO[Si](C(C)C)(C(C)C)C(C)C

name: sa_0480
text:
I read the drawing as tri-O-TIPS-D-glucal: a dihydropyran ring (the glycal) carrying three triisopropylsilyl ethers. The SMILES comes from the ring atoms, then the stereocentres, then the TIPS expansion.

**Ring and substituents**
- The ring has an oxygen and five carbons: O–CH=CH–CH(OTIPS)–CH(OTIPS)–CH(CH2OTIPS)–back to O.
- The double bond is between the two carbons next to the ring oxygen side, C1=C2.
- The three silyl ethers are on C3 (hashed bond), C4 (wedged bond) and the exocyclic CH2 on C5 (hashed bond to the CH2).
- Each TIPS group is expanded to Si(CH(CH3)2)3.

**Stereocentres**

I assigned CIP descriptors from the wedges and hashes, ranking by substituent priority and viewing against the implicit hydrogen.
- C5 is R. O > C4 > CH2 appears counterclockwise from the front, and H points toward the viewer, so the true sense is clockwise.
- C4 is S. O > C5 > C3 appears counterclockwise with H at the back.
- C3 is R. O > C4 > C2 appears counterclockwise from the front, and H points toward the viewer, so the true sense is clockwise.

This matches the D-glucal pattern (3R,4S,5R), which has the known SMILES OC[C@H]1OC=C[C@@H](O)[C@@H]1O. Replacing each OH with OTIPS in that template keeps the neighbour order, so the @/@@ marks stay the same.

SMILES: CC(C)[Si](C(C)C)(C(C)C)OC[C@H]1OC=C[C@@H](O[Si](C(C)C)(C(C)C)C(C)C)[C@@H]1O[Si](C(C)C)(C(C)C)C(C)C

name: sa_0483
text:
The drawing shows a 4-quinolone core: a benzene ring fused to a pyridone ring. The ring nitrogen carries a PMB group, C3 carries a CO2H group, and C4 is a C=O.

PMB is the p-methoxybenzyl group, which expands to Cc1ccc(OC)cc1 attached through the CH2 (written Cc1ccc(OC)cc1 below).

SMILES for the molecule: OC(=O)C1=CN(Cc2ccc(OC)cc2)c2ccccc2C1=O

Atom check:
- The pyridone ring is N, CH=, C(CO2H), C(=O), and the two fusion carbons.
- In the drawing, N connects to the CH, which is double-bonded to C3 (the carbon bearing CO2H). C3 connects to C4 (C=O), and C4 connects to the fusion carbon C4a. The benzene ring closes back to C8a, which bonds to N.

This matches the SMILES above.

SMILES: OC(=O)C1=CN(Cc2ccc(OC)cc2)c2ccccc2C1=O

name: sa_0485
text:
The drawing shows an NH with two labelled substituents, tBu and Piv.

- tBu is tert-butyl, C(C)(C)C.
- Piv is pivaloyl, the acyl group C(=O)C(C)(C)C.

The nitrogen carries one hydrogen, a tert-butyl group and a pivaloyl group, so the molecule is N-tert-butylpivalamide.

The SMILES is CC(C)(C)NC(=O)C(C)(C)C. It has no stereochemistry, and the atoms match the drawing.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)NC(=O)C(C)(C)C

name: sa_0478
text:
I read the structure as a spiro compound: a piperidine ring and a cyclopentane ring sharing one carbon.

**Piperidine ring (six atoms):** the NH, a CH bearing a CH2CO2Et group (wedged bond), three CH2 groups, and the spiro carbon.

**Cyclopentane ring (five atoms):** the spiro carbon, three CH2 groups, and a CH bearing a CH2–O–TBDPS group (hashed bond).

**Substituents:**
- The ester is an ethyl ester, written CH2C(=O)OCH2CH3.
- TBDPS is tert-butyldiphenylsilyl, written Si(Ph)2(C(CH3)3).

**Stereocentres:** there are three, and I assigned each from the wedge or hash geometry.
- The CH carrying the CH2CO2Et group has its wedged bond toward the viewer, which gives `[C@H]`.
- The spiro carbon has its ring CH2 on a wedged bond toward the viewer, which gives `[C@@]`.
- The cyclopentane CH has its CH2O hashed bond away from the viewer, which gives `[C@@H]`.

I checked the atom order and ring closures against the drawing, and the SMILES below matches it atom for atom.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1CCC[C@@]2(N1)CCC[C@@H]2CO[Si](c1ccccc1)(c1ccccc1)C(C)(C)C

name: sa_0484
text:
The drawing shows an indoline (a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring containing N), with these substituents:

- **Indoline N:** carries n-octyl (nOct), which is CCCCCCCC.
- **Five-membered ring:** N, CH2, CH2, and the two fused aromatic carbons.
- **Benzene ring, going around from the fused carbon next to the CH2:**
  - The fused carbon C3a is bonded to the CH2.
  - The next carbon carries a methyl.
  - The next carbon carries CH2CO2H.
  - The next carbon carries a methyl.
  - The next carbon carries NH-Piv (pivaloyl amide).
  - The last carbon is the fused C7a, bonded to N.

Piv is pivaloyl, C(=O)C(C)(C)C, so the substituent is NHC(=O)C(C)(C)C.

SMILES, starting at the indoline N:
CCCCCCCCN1CCc2c(C)c(CC(=O)O)c(C)c(NC(=O)C(C)(C)C)c21

The HO2C-CH2 group is drawn as a CH2 attached to the ring, so the substituent is CH2COOH. Checking the ring closure: c2 (C3a) is bonded to c(C), then c(CC(=O)O), then c(C), then c(NHPiv), then c21 (C7a), which closes to N1 and to C3a. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCN1CCc2c(C)c(CC(=O)O)c(C)c(NC(=O)C(C)(C)C)c21

name: sa_0486
text:
The drawing shows an N‑trityl histidine methyl ester whose α‑amine carries a (4‑dimethylaminopyridin‑2‑yl)methyl group.

- **Imidazole:** the trityl‑bearing nitrogen is bonded to a CH, which is double‑bonded to the second ring nitrogen. That nitrogen connects to the carbon bearing the CH2 chain, which is double‑bonded to the other ring CH. This is the usual Nτ‑trityl histidine pattern.
- **Side chain:** the ring carbon is attached to CH2, then to the stereocentre, which carries CO2Me and an NH.
- **Pyridine:** NH–CH2 connects to the pyridine C2, next to the ring nitrogen, and NMe2 sits at C4.
- **Stereocentre:** the CO2Me group is on a wedge, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. The priorities are N > CO2Me > CH2 > H. Going N (right) → CO2Me (upper left) → CH2 (lower left) is counterclockwise, so the centre is S, as in L‑histidine. In the SMILES below, the neighbour order is ester C, H, CH2, N, and `[C@H]` gives S for that order.

SMILES: COC(=O)[C@H](Cc1cn(C(c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)cn1)NCc1cc(N(C)C)ccn1

name: sa_0488
text:
The drawing shows N-τ-trityl-L-histidine, read as follows.

- **Ring:** The five-membered ring is an imidazole. Its bottom-left nitrogen carries the Trt (trityl) group, which expands to C(Ph)₃. The top nitrogen is the unsubstituted ring N, drawn with a C=N double bond to the CH on its left. The ring carbon bonded to the CH₂ side chain is adjacent to that unsubstituted N, so the ring is 1-trityl-4-substituted.
